package agent

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/intercept"
	"github.com/Autumn-27/norma/agentcore"
	"github.com/Autumn-27/norma/harness"
	"github.com/Autumn-27/norma/llm"
	"github.com/Autumn-27/norma/permission"
	actool "github.com/Autumn-27/norma/tool"
	"github.com/Autumn-27/norma/transcript"
)

// Worker is an LLM work agent (docs §4.4): it claims ONE intent, completes it
// with real tools (Bash: kali tooling through the recording proxy), writes the
// FACTS it found back into the graph, and stops. It does NOT generate new
// directions (that is the planner's job) and does NOT keep exploring toward the
// goal on its own. Multiple workers run concurrently as goroutines.
// WebSearchOpts is the web-search backend selection the server pushes into each
// agent (planner/worker/main). Enabled=false leaves the web_search tool off.
// Backend is "ddgs" (no key), "brave-free" (BraveKey required), "tavily"
// (TavilyKey required), or "deepseek" (DeepSeek* required, filled from the
// active LLM profile). It maps directly onto agentcore.Options.
// Proxy is a dedicated egress proxy for the search request (http/https/socks5),
// independent of the traffic-recording MITM proxy — set it when the search endpoint
// is only reachable via a VPN/SOCKS proxy. Empty = direct.
//
// Note the deepseek backend differs in nature from the other three: DeepSeek has no
// directly callable search API — search exists only inside its Anthropic-compatible
// messages API (the web_search_20250305 server tool), so each search consumes one
// model call, and the search request is issued by DeepSeek's servers — it does NOT
// go through the local Proxy, nor into the traffic recording.
type WebSearchOpts struct {
	Enabled   bool
	Backend   string
	BraveKey  string
	TavilyKey string
	Proxy     string
	// DeepSeek* comes from the currently active LLM config (only the official
	// DeepSeek endpoint in anthropic format) — not configured separately; it follows
	// the LLM config switch.
	DeepSeekBaseURL string
	DeepSeekAPIKey  string
	DeepSeekModel   string
}

type Worker struct {
	findingRecorder FindingRecorder
	prov            llm.Provider
	model           string
	workDir         string
	proxyAddr       string
	proxyCACert     string            // recording proxy's CA cert path (for WebFetch HTTPS verify)
	webSearch       WebSearchOpts     // web_search tool backend selection (off by default)
	tx              *transcript.Store // raw LLM conversation persistence (nil = off)
	window          int               // context window in tokens (for compaction)
	windowFn        func() int        // optional dynamic task-chain minimum
	maxTurns        int               // max agent turns per run (0 = unlimited)
	// runTimeout is the wall-clock budget for the main exploration of one intent
	// (0 = unlimited). When it fires, the run is cut and a settlement round is
	// forced so already-identified facts get written back instead of being lost.
	runTimeout time.Duration
	// extraTools are host-provided tools (e.g. traffic query, oast) appended to
	// the worker's graph write-back tools.
	extraTools []actool.CoreTool
	// injectConstraints resolves whether this task's operation constraints get
	// injected into the worker system prompt. Read per run so the settings toggle
	// takes effect without rebuilding the agent. nil = inject (default).
	injectConstraints func() bool
	// nonStreamingFn resolves whether this run uses the non-streaming (Complete)
	// path. Read per run so a profile/task toggle takes effect without rebuilding
	// the agent. nil = streaming (default).
	nonStreamingFn func() bool
	// noaEnabledFn resolves whether this run uses the experimental noa context-
	// compression mechanism. Read per run, like nonStreaming. nil = off (built-in
	// compaction).
	noaEnabledFn func() bool
	// maxTokensFn resolves the per-reply output cap in tokens, on the same
	// per-run basis. nil or 0 = send no cap and let the endpoint decide.
	maxTokensFn func() int
	// lessonsBlock is the code-owned RSI evidence block appended verbatim after
	// the rendered system prompt. Empty = off. It is data, not instructions:
	// the server renders it from outcome records and sets it before the run.
	lessonsBlock string
}

// WorkerSessionID returns the stable transcript key used by a worker intent.
// Worker slots are reusable, so the intent id (rather than work#N) is the
// session identity. Keep this helper public so the Worker message API and UI
// can refer to exactly the conversation that will be resumed.
func WorkerSessionID(explorationID, intentID int64) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("exp%d-worker-i%d", explorationID, intentID)
}

const workerChatMarkerPrefix = "<!-- HIVE_WORKER_CHAT:"

func workerChatMarker(requestID string) string {
	return workerChatMarkerPrefix + requestID + " -->"
}

func hasWorkerChatMessage(messages []llm.Message, requestID string) bool {
	marker := workerChatMarker(requestID)
	for _, message := range messages {
		if message.Role == llm.RoleUser && strings.Contains(message.Text(), marker) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// SetNonStreaming wires a resolver deciding whether runs use the non-streaming
// model path (true = non-streaming). nil/unset = streaming (default). Read per
// run so a profile or task-chain toggle takes effect without rebuilding.
func (w *Worker) SetNonStreaming(fn func() bool) { w.nonStreamingFn = fn }

func (w *Worker) nonStreaming() bool { return w.nonStreamingFn != nil && w.nonStreamingFn() }

// SetNoaEnabled wires a resolver deciding whether runs use the experimental noa
// context-compression mechanism. nil/unset = off (built-in compaction). Read per
// run so the settings toggle takes effect without rebuilding the agent.
func (w *Worker) SetNoaEnabled(fn func() bool) { w.noaEnabledFn = fn }

// SetMaxTokens wires a resolver for the per-reply output cap. nil/unset or 0 =
// send no cap and let the endpoint decide. Read per run, like nonStreaming.
func (w *Worker) SetMaxTokens(fn func() int) { w.maxTokensFn = fn }

func (w *Worker) maxTokens() int {
	if w.maxTokensFn == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return w.maxTokensFn()
}

// SetConstraintInject wires a resolver deciding whether this task's operation
// constraints get injected into the worker system prompt. nil = inject (default).
func (w *Worker) SetConstraintInject(fn func() bool) { w.injectConstraints = fn }

// SetLessonsBlock sets the code-owned RSI evidence block appended after the
// rendered system prompt. Empty disables it. The block is rendered by the
// server from outcome records and is never editable through the prompt UI.
func (w *Worker) SetLessonsBlock(block string) { w.lessonsBlock = block }

// wantConstraints reports whether constraint injection is enabled (default yes).
func (w *Worker) wantConstraints() bool { return w.injectConstraints == nil || w.injectConstraints() }

// SetRunTimeout configures the per-intent wall-clock budget for the main
// exploration (0 = unlimited). When it fires, the SDK settlement phase still runs
// so facts are never lost to a timeout. Safe to call before Execute.
func (w *Worker) SetRunTimeout(run time.Duration) {
	w.runTimeout = run
}

// settleWrapUpPrompt is injected by the SDK settlement phase when a worker hits its
// turn/time budget: stop probing, write back what was found, then end with a
// plain-text one-liner (which becomes this run's displayed result).
const settleWrapUpPrompt = "You are about to be terminated because your budget is exhausted. Do not run any more commands/probes. Please, in order: (1) write back everything you have identified above but not yet written back, item by item — new assets with insert_assets, exploration conclusions/facts with record_fact, confirmed findings with report_finding; (2) **finally, in a single standalone sentence of plain text** summarize what you did and which key conclusions you reached (this sentence is shown as this run's result — be sure to output it)."

func NewWorker(prov llm.Provider, model, workDir string, tx *transcript.Store, window, maxTurns int, extra ...actool.CoreTool) *Worker {
	return &Worker{prov: prov, model: model, workDir: workDir, tx: tx, window: window, maxTurns: maxTurns, extraTools: extra}
}

// defaultToolsExcept returns actool.DefaultTools() minus the named tools (by
// CoreTool.Name()). Used to trim SDK default tools an agent shouldn't have.
func defaultToolsExcept(exclude ...string) []actool.CoreTool {
	drop := make(map[string]bool, len(exclude))
	for _, n := range exclude {
		drop[n] = true
	}
	all := actool.DefaultTools()
	out := make([]actool.CoreTool, 0, len(all))
	for _, t := range all {
		if !drop[t.Name()] {
			out = append(out, t)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func (w *Worker) SetCompactionWindowResolver(fn func() int) { w.windowFn = fn }

func (w *Worker) compactionWindow() int {
	if w.windowFn != nil {
		return w.windowFn()
	}
	return w.window
}

// SetProxy configures the recording proxy address that workers route target
// traffic through, plus the CA cert path WebFetch trusts to verify HTTPS through
// that MITM proxy. Empty addr disables the hint.
func (w *Worker) SetProxy(addr, caCert string) { w.proxyAddr, w.proxyCACert = addr, caCert }

// SetWebSearch selects the web_search backend for this worker (off by default).
func (w *Worker) SetWebSearch(o WebSearchOpts) { w.webSearch = o }

// proxyEnv builds the Bash-subprocess env that routes child-command HTTP through
// the egress proxy (the recording MITM when capture is on, or the global proxy
// directly when it is off) and, only when a MITM CA is present, makes the common
// toolchain trust it — so tools need no manual -x/--proxy/-k. Each ecosystem reads
// a different CA var (verified empirically): SSL_CERT_FILE→curl/urllib/Go/openssl,
// REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE→python requests (it ignores SSL_CERT_FILE), CURL_CA_BUNDLE→curl,
// GIT_SSL_CAINFO→git, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS→node; NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY makes Node 24+
// honor the proxy vars. ALL_PROXY is set too so a socks5 egress proxy (which curl
// only reads from ALL_PROXY, not HTTP(S)_PROXY) works in the capture-off path.
// Empty proxyAddr → nil (direct, unchanged env).
func proxyEnv(proxyAddr, caCert string) []string {
	if proxyAddr == "" {
		return nil
	}
	env := []string{
		"HTTP_PROXY=" + proxyAddr, "HTTPS_PROXY=" + proxyAddr,
		"http_proxy=" + proxyAddr, "https_proxy=" + proxyAddr,
		"ALL_PROXY=" + proxyAddr, "all_proxy=" + proxyAddr, // socks5 egress: curl reads only this
		"NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1", // Node 24+: honor HTTP(S)_PROXY in built-in fetch/http
	}
	if caCert != "" {
		env = append(env,
			"SSL_CERT_FILE="+caCert,
			"CURL_CA_BUNDLE="+caCert,
			"REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE="+caCert,
			"GIT_SSL_CAINFO="+caCert,
			"NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS="+caCert,
		)
	}
	return env
}

// workerDefaultTmpl is the built-in EDITABLE body (section [A]) of the worker
// system prompt, seeded into agent_prompts. The trafficTool block and the
// intermediate artifact output rules are NOT here — they are code-owned and
// appended by workerSystem after rendering (sections [B]/[C]), so editing the DB
// body can never drop them.
const workerDefaultTmpl = `You are an "executor" (work agent) of a network-security platform's authorized penetration testing system. You are assigned [ONE intent] (a one-sentence exploration direction), and your sole duty is: **complete this one intent, write the findings back into the knowledge graph, then stop and return.**

**Boundaries (red lines)**:
1. **Do only the one intent you were assigned**. **If, while exploring this intent, you glimpse a clue worth digging into beyond this intent** (a path leaked by an error, a point that could chain with other assets, the suspected entry of another exploit chain), **note it in a fact's summary and hand it to the planner**.
2. An initial setback (payload filtered / 404 / injection with no echo) does not mean the intent is exhausted — walk through all bypass means for this intent before outputting a conclusion;
3. Operate only within the authorized scope. If [operation constraints] are attached at the top of the system prompt, they are the highest-priority red lines: self-check before every command/probe; if it violates them, don't do it (even if it falls inside your assigned intent).

**Write back as you discover** (only what's written into the graph counts; what's in your head/text doesn't; write every result immediately — don't save it for the end and lose it when the step budget runs out). Three kinds of write-back, don't cross the graphs:
- **New asset/resource → insert_assets (asset graph)**: subdomains / services / endpoints / fingerprints / credentials and any asset [itself]. **Only assets are registered here; exploration conclusions/judgments don't go here — use record_fact.**
- **Exploration conclusion/fact → record_fact (exploration graph, pass intent_id)**: use it for all of those. **Consolidate multiple observations into [ONE] fact** (summary = one summarizing sentence + detail = the expansion of the summary, based on the real execution process) — not one fact per attribute; one intent usually produces only one fact, and splitting finely bloats the graph endlessly — **write one fact by default, merging everything mergeable into detail**; only use the facts array to split when there are genuinely [mutually independent, unmergeable] conclusions — that's a rare exception, not the norm. **Write only the delta**: record only what is [newly obtained] this time; don't re-record existing facts in different words (if it merely corroborates an existing one with nothing new, don't record it). **Write only what you actually saw**: give evidence (one line: the command + the most proving one or two output lines — brief; details in detail), and mark confidence (observed = seen directly / inferred = inferred from phenomena). **Declare the source** of every fact: target_response (content the target itself returned: page bodies, headers, error messages, banners, even when a tool fetched it), tool_output (a tool's own result about the target: port states, scanner verdicts, status codes and timings you measured), third_party_intel (OSINT, CVE databases, public reports), operator_input (given by the human operator), or inference (your own reasoning; the default).
- **Confirmed vulnerability → report_finding (exploration graph, with PoC, pass intent_id)**: **use it only when you actually triggered it this time and obtained reproducible evidence (request/response or command output)**. It is strictly forbidden to treat "version/fingerprint matching a CVE", "the parameter looks injectable", or "inference from external vulnerability databases/changelogs/code diffs" as confirmed, and don't substitute querying a CVE database or comparing patch versions for actually triggering it. Can't trigger it but suspicion remains → record an inferred fact with record_fact (the suspicion point + why it couldn't be triggered) for the planner; don't force it into a finding. Before registering, check list_findings / list_task_findings for an existing finding with the same root cause, endpoint, and parameter: the same defect again means extending that finding's evidence, not registering a duplicate (duplicates burn reviewer trust); a genuinely distinct entry point, parameter, or privilege level remains its own finding per the adversarial gate. When your confidence is not high, also fill report_finding's optional fields: counterevidence = what you tested that did not work; confidence_rationale = why the conclusion holds. Both are optional and never block reporting.


**Budget discipline (the deadline contract)**: your run has a step budget and a wall-clock budget. Before starting any command or probe, check it can finish well within what remains; never start work whose timeout can outlive the remaining budget — prefer the smaller variant that lands. When the budget is nearly spent or the wrap-up signal arrives, stop opening new work and land everything already collected (facts first, then findings): a result that exists only in your head is lost.

After completing this intent, summarize in one sentence what you did and which facts you wrote back.

Adversarial gate before report_finding:
- A candidate stays a hypothesis until you have actively tried to disprove it. Before reporting, argue the opposite case along five axes: **reachability** (can a real attacker actually get there?), **preconditions** (does exploitation need an unrealistic starting position?), **downstream controls** (does something between the trigger and the goal block the impact?), **scope** (is the affected asset inside the authorized scope?), and **simpler explanation** (is there a benign reason for the observation?).
- Eliminations need evidence at the same bar as confirmations: cite the specific request, response, or control that kills the candidate. "Probably validated downstream", "looks by design", or "internal only" eliminate nothing.
- Do not merge distinct candidates: different entry points, different parameters, or different attacker privilege levels are separate findings even when they share one narrative chain.
- Zero confirmed findings is a valid outcome. Never soften these gates to manufacture output; a precise negative ("class X tested across surfaces Y with method Z; clean"), recorded as a fact, is real work.

Finding quality gates (proof standard, measured impact, testing bounds):
- **The PoC must demonstrate the attacker's goal achieved end to end** (unauthorized data actually returned, the injected command actually executing with output, another user's resource actually read or modified), not merely that a vulnerable pattern exists or a vulnerable code path runs. When the mechanism fires but a downstream control blocks the goal, record a hardening note, not a finding.
- **Every reported finding carries a measured impact**: the attacker outcome as a number with its denominator ("3 of 20 payload variants returned other-tenant rows; 17 rejected", "commands executed: 2, output returned: yes") plus what the defense blocked. "The attacker can dump the table" is a claim; "3 of 20 payloads returned rows" is a measurement. If no number is obtainable, record what was attempted and why it is not measurable.
- **State the proof basis** on every finding: executed-live, executed-lab, or static-analysis-unexecuted. An executed proof outranks a static conclusion; anything never actually triggered is "potential/suspect", never confirmed.
- **Testing bounds** (bounded and non-destructive does NOT mean read-only): state-changing requests are in bounds when they are the finding's mechanism. Prove the mechanism on your own objects/accounts first, then confirm cross-entity reach on at most three non-owned objects with the smallest request that demonstrates the boundary; prefer reversible values, restore originals where possible, and record every touched object ID in the evidence.
- **Priority discipline**: low-impact oracles (user/account enumeration, account-existence checks, response-timing differences) and low-yield misconfigurations (permissive CORS) are not standalone findings; record them only when they directly chain into account takeover, authentication bypass, or mass data exposure.

Operator handoff on environmental blocks:
- When a command or tool fails for an environmental reason (a sandboxed or filtered network path, a missing binary or key, TLS or proxy interception, a permission this runtime lacks), stop after the first failure: do not retry with different flags, do not switch tools hunting for a bypass, and do not fall through to an equivalent command.
- Call ask_operator with the exact single command the operator should run in their own terminal: one line, copy-pastable, followed by what to paste back. One command per request; never batch. Wait for the reply instead of burning turns.`

// workerTrafficBlock is section [B]: the traffic-tool note, code-injected only when
// traffic capture (recording) is on — i.e. the traffic_* tools actually exist.
// Gated on recording, NOT on the egress proxy: a global proxy with capture off
// routes traffic but records nothing, so the tools would not be there. Not stored,
// not editable.
func workerTrafficBlock(recording bool) string {
	if !recording {
		return ""
	}
	return "\n\n**Traffic tools**:\n- traffic_search / traffic_get / traffic_blob: review responses, find already-visited resources — **check the traffic first, don't curl the same URL twice**. traffic_search **requires a host** and by default returns only 3 ultra-light index entries (id/method/url/status/resp_len, no response content) — explicitly raise limit when you need more; body_contains does full-text search in request/response bodies (at least 3 characters; supports substrings and CJK text, e.g. for passwords/keys/errors/internal addresses); to see one entry's raw content use traffic_get(id) — oversized bodies show as @blob sha256:<hash>, fetched in segments with traffic_blob(hash)."
}

// artifactSpec is section [C]: the code-owned, non-editable tail appended to every
// pentest agent's prompt — intermediate artifacts must land in the shared work
// dir, never /tmp. Guaranteed present regardless of how the DB body is edited.
func artifactSpec(dir string) string {
	return "\n\n**Intermediate artifact output rules**: all intermediate artifacts — scripts, payloads, captured response bodies, temporary data — **must be written to this task's work directory " + dir + "** (a relative path writes here; the absolute path works too) — **do NOT write to /tmp, do NOT use other absolute paths**."
}

// workerArtifactSpec is the worker's section [C]: its per-intent run dir is
// pre-created by the engine (ensureRunDir), so it just writes relative paths there
// — no manual mkdir, no cross-worker name collisions.
func workerArtifactSpec(runDir string) string {
	return "\n\n**Intermediate artifact output rules**: all intermediate artifacts — scripts, payloads, captured response bodies, temporary data — **must be written to this intent's dedicated work directory " + runDir + "** (already created automatically; just write with relative paths there — no manual mkdir needed) — **do NOT write to /tmp, do NOT use other absolute paths**."
}

// ensureRunDir builds and creates an agent's working directory under base:
// <base>/tasks/<taskID> for planner/main; <base>/tasks/<taskID>/i<intentID> for a
// worker (intentID<=0 → task dir only). The "tasks/" segment groups per-task dirs
// symmetrically with the chat agent's "sessions/<sessionID>". Best-effort mkdir — on
// failure, writes fail the same way an unwritable CWD would.
func ensureRunDir(base string, taskID, intentID int64) string {
	dir := filepath.Join(base, "tasks", strconv.FormatInt(taskID, 10))
	if intentID > 0 {
		dir = filepath.Join(dir, "i"+strconv.FormatInt(intentID, 10))
	}
	_ = os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755)
	return dir
}

// cmdOutDir is the SDK large-tool-output spill dir under an agent's run dir.
func cmdOutDir(dir string) string { return filepath.Join(dir, "cmd-output") }

func workerSystem(proxyAddr, caCert, dataDir, runDir string) string {
	body := renderSystem("worker", workerDefaultTmpl, WorkerVars{ProxyAddr: proxyAddr, DataDir: dataDir, Now: nowStr()})
	// caCert is present only when the recording MITM is on, which is exactly when
	// the traffic_* tools are registered — so it gates the traffic-tool note.
	// Optional finding guidance is added for every role after tool resolution.
	return body + untrustedContentTail(body) + workerTrafficBlock(caCert != "") + workerArtifactSpec(runDir) + noiseProfileBlock()
}

// renderIntentTask formats the claimed intent for the worker's launch USER message:
// the intent is the worker's whole job. It used to live in the system prompt; it now
// rides in the first user turn (together with the situational overview) so the system
// prompt stays static/role-only — same move as the planner's situational block.
// intentAssetIDs pulls the intent's target asset ids out of its payload
// (planner's add_intent stores them as a numeric asset_ids array). nil on absence
// or malformed payload.
func intentAssetIDs(intent *db.Node) []int64 {
	if intent == nil {
		return nil
	}
	var p struct {
		AssetIDs []int64 `json:"asset_ids"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(intent.Payload, &p); err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	return p.AssetIDs
}

func renderIntentTask(intent *db.Node) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("\n\n[The intent you claimed (your only job this time: do just this one, produce only facts, stop when done)]:\n%s\nIntent id: %d (pass it when writing back record_fact / report_finding)", string(intent.Payload), intent.ID)
}

// renderWorkerGraphOverview folds the global situational snapshot into the worker's
// launch USER message for AWARENESS ONLY. The framing is deliberately strong: the overview
// must NOT widen the worker's job — it still does only its assigned intent. Its sole
// purpose is letting the worker read context (existing facts/assets/hints)
// so it avoids redundant work and doesn't re-derive what others already found.
// The derived fields go inside env's frame (#124, F3); env is built once per
// launch message.
func renderWorkerGraphOverview(data map[string]any, env dataEnvelope) string {
	// coverage is a signal for the planner to judge "which class is under-tested /
	// whether to widen the scope" — it conflicts with the worker's boundary of "do
	// only the assigned intent, don't chase uncovered points" → drop it from the
	// worker view. data is a fresh map dedicated to this worker, so deleting the key
	// doesn't affect the planner.
	delete(data, "coverage")
	sections := renderOverviewSections(data, env)
	if sections == "" {
		return "" // fall back silently: the worker just won't have the global context
	}
	return env.intro() + "\n\n[Global exploration overview (read-only, helps you place your assigned intent in the bigger picture)]:\n" +
		"Below is the task's current exploration overview. Two purposes: first, know what others have already found — don't repeat; second, let you relate this intent to the global picture while exploring it.\n" +
		"**Digressing is good**: while exploring this intent, think deep and associate freely. The only boundary is — don't actually go execute other intents (that's other workers' business, scheduled by the planner). But whenever you associate a valuable clue (cross-asset linkage, the suspected entry of another exploit chain, a global-level suspicious point), **be sure to write it into a fact for the planner** — this is an important output of yours, not optional. Better to report one more for the planner to judge than to swallow it yourself." +
		sections
}

// Execute runs one intent. hooks (the per-task Guard) gates every tool call; may
// be nil. emit, if non-nil, receives one ActivityRecord per execution step.
// notifyFinding, if non-nil, is called (intentID, summary) when this worker writes
// a finding (report_finding) so the task's planner wakes mid-flight — with context
// on which intent found what — instead of waiting for the worker to finish.
// Returns the terminal reason (so the engine can distinguish completed vs
// max_turns) and a per-kind breakdown of what was written back (so an intent that
// explored but persisted nothing isn't mistaken for done, and the engine can log
// facts/assets/findings separately instead of lumping them under "facts").
func (w *Worker) Execute(ctx context.Context, name string, taskID int64, as *db.AssetStore, ts *db.ExplorationStore, intent *db.Node, hooks harness.HookRunner, emit func(db.Activity), enr EnrichTrigger, notifyFinding func(int64, string)) (harness.TerminalReason, WriteCounts, error) {
	return w.execute(ctx, name, taskID, as, ts, intent, hooks, emit, enr, notifyFinding, "", "")
}

// ExecuteWithMessage runs the next turn in the same intent conversation with a
// human-authored message. The HTTP handler does not edit the transcript;
// agentcore records the message as a normal user turn when this Worker starts.
// This keeps Worker continuation identical to the regular agent chat flow.
func (w *Worker) ExecuteWithMessage(ctx context.Context, name string, taskID int64, as *db.AssetStore, ts *db.ExplorationStore, intent *db.Node, hooks harness.HookRunner, emit func(db.Activity), enr EnrichTrigger, notifyFinding func(int64, string), requestID, message string) (harness.TerminalReason, WriteCounts, error) {
	return w.execute(ctx, name, taskID, as, ts, intent, hooks, emit, enr, notifyFinding, strings.TrimSpace(requestID), strings.TrimSpace(message))
}

func (w *Worker) execute(ctx context.Context, name string, taskID int64, as *db.AssetStore, ts *db.ExplorationStore, intent *db.Node, hooks harness.HookRunner, emit func(db.Activity), enr EnrichTrigger, notifyFinding func(int64, string), requestID, message string) (harness.TerminalReason, WriteCounts, error) {
	tsx := NewToolSet(ts, name)
	tsx.SetFindingRecorder(w.findingRecorder)
	tsx.SetTaskID(taskID)
	coverageEnabled := as == nil || as.CoverageEnabled(taskID)
	tsx.SetCoverageEnabled(coverageEnabled)
	if as != nil {
		tsx.SetAssetStore(as, as.Companies())
	}
	tsx.SetOwnerNode(intent.ID)         // assets this worker discovers anchor to its intent → visible to the task
	tsx.SetEnrich(enr)                  // async DNS/HTTP auto-completion for assets this worker writes
	tsx.SetNotifyFinding(notifyFinding) // when report_finding lands, wake the planner on the spot with "which intent + finding"
	// base = built-in worker tools ∪ host tools (traffic) ∪ default tools (incl. Bash);
	// then augment with the agent's visible skills/MCP. During the SDK settlement
	// phase, Bash is hidden via Settlement.DisabledTools (no local gating needed).
	base := append(tsx.DropCoverageTools(tsx.WorkerTools()), w.extraTools...)
	// The worker deliberately gets no MultiEdit/Glob/Grep: precise file edits use Edit,
	// searching goes through Bash(grep/find) — narrowing the tool surface and reducing
	// low-value calls. The rest of the SDK default tools (Read/Write/Edit/LS/Bash/Sleep)
	// are kept as usual.
	base = append(base, defaultToolsExcept("MultiEdit", "Glob", "Grep")...)
	ctx = WithRunInfo(ctx, RunInfo{TaskID: taskID, ExplorationID: explorationID(ts), IntentID: intent.ID})
	tools, def, cleanup := AugmentTools(WithToolQuery(ctx, nodeSummary(intent)), "worker", base)
	defer cleanup()

	// The intent is the worker's [sole duty, an invariant across the whole run] → it
	// goes into the system prompt together with the launch instruction and the raw
	// data of the intent's anchored target assets: the system prompt is rebuilt for
	// every run and can never be compacted away, so the intent stays present in long
	// runs, and a resumed run doesn't depend on whether the transcript kept that first
	// message. The cost is the system prompt mixing in per-intent volatile data and
	// losing cross-intent cache reuse; that is a deliberate trade (losing the intent is
	// far worse than spending tokens). The divergence from the planner ("situation
	// block in the user turn") is intentional: the planner itself is the intent
	// producer with no single mandate; the worker has one. Only the [global situation
	// overview] stays in the launch user message — it is degradable and tolerates
	// staleness, so compacting it away is harmless.
	// This intent's dedicated work dir <workDir>/tasks/<taskID>/i<intentID> is created
	// by the engine first.
	runDir := ensureRunDir(w.workDir, taskID, intent.ID)
	// The run-wide intent is not the current tool action. Do not forward it or
	// inherit a parent run's background into the action reviewer.
	ctx = intercept.WithReviewContext(ctx, runDir, intercept.ReviewBackground{})
	overview := renderWorkerGraphOverview(tsx.graphOverviewData(), newDataEnvelope())
	sysBody := workerSystem(w.proxyAddr, w.proxyCACert, w.workDir, runDir) + w.lessonsBlock
	if w.wantConstraints() {
		sysBody += constraintBlock(ts) // inject the operation constraints (if any) into the system prompt; the worker strictly obeys them during execution
	}
	// intent block → intent-anchored assets block → launch instruction, appended to
	// the system tail in that order (same append pattern as constraintBlock).
	sysBody += renderIntentTask(intent)
	if as != nil {
		if ids := intentAssetIDs(intent); len(ids) > 0 {
			if assets, err := as.GetByIDs(ids); err == nil && len(assets) > 0 {
				if b, err := json.Marshal(assets); err == nil {
					sysBody += "\n\nThe target assets corresponding to this intent's asset_ids:\n" + string(b)
				}
				// The assets this intent explicitly targets → automatically join the task's
				// test scope (same conservative granularity as insertAssets). upsertTaskScope's
				// ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + the uq_task_scope unique index guarantee no
				// duplicate additions; reruns/retries are idempotent no-ops as well.
				// asset_ids can trace back to target content, so these auto rows count
				// toward coverage only under a declared domain or IP root (db.declaredScopeFilter);
				// coverage scope, not enforced.
				// When the asset-coverage feature is off, the test scope (denominator) is no
				// longer accumulated.
				if coverageEnabled {
					for _, a := range assets {
						_ = as.AddAutoScope(taskID, a.Type, a.Domain, a.URL, a.IP)
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}
	sysBody += "\n\nStart executing the intent above: do only it, produce only facts, assets, findings, stop when done."
	system, boundary := deferredSystem(sysBody, def)
	// The task-level deadline (injected via ctx) clamps this run's wall-clock budget +
	// decides the wrap-up prompt (see taskclock.go).
	tc := taskClockFrom(ctx)
	maxDur, clamped := clampMaxDuration(tc.DeadlineUnix, w.runTimeout)
	settle := wrapupSettlement("worker", []string{"Bash"})
	if tc.DeadlineUnix > 0 {
		settle = wrapupSettlementForTask("worker", []string{"Bash"}, clamped)
	}
	opts := agentcore.Options{
		Provider:        w.prov,
		SystemPrompt:    system,
		DynamicBoundary: boundary,
		Tools:           withWebFetch(ctx, tools, w.proxyAddr, w.proxyCACert),
		DeferredTools:   def.Deferred,
		UnlockSet:       def.Unlock,
		PermissionMode:  permission.ModeBypass,
		// WebFetch (added to Tools above) goes through the recording proxy, so its
		// HTTP is recorded just like curl; loading the proxy CA lets MITM-re-signed
		// HTTPS certs [verify normally] (rather than disabling verification). Direct
		// when proxy is empty. Every redirect hop goes through the target gate.
		// Web search (optional). ddgs needs no key; brave-free needs BraveKey; tavily needs TavilyKey.
		// WebSearchProxy is a dedicated egress proxy (http/https/socks5), unrelated to the traffic-recording MITM proxy; empty = direct.
		EnableWebSearch:       w.webSearch.Enabled,
		WebSearchBackend:      w.webSearch.Backend,
		BraveSearchAPIKey:     w.webSearch.BraveKey,
		TavilySearchAPIKey:    w.webSearch.TavilyKey,
		DeepSeekSearchBaseURL: w.webSearch.DeepSeekBaseURL,
		DeepSeekSearchAPIKey:  w.webSearch.DeepSeekAPIKey,
		DeepSeekSearchModel:   w.webSearch.DeepSeekModel,
		WebSearchProxy:        w.webSearch.Proxy,
		// Bash subcommands' HTTP goes through the recording proxy + trusts its CA by
		// default (tools need no -x/-k).
		BashEnv:    proxyEnv(w.proxyAddr, w.proxyCACert),
		WorkingDir: runDir,
		MaxTurns:   w.turnCap(ctx), // 0 = unlimited (configurable in agent management); clamped by the intent budget
		// Wall-clock budget, judged at turn boundaries without interrupting mid-flight;
		// 0 = unlimited. When a task-level deadline exists, clamp to min(own budget, time
		// until the deadline) so this run naturally enters wrap-up when the task hits its
		// deadline (see taskclock.go).
		MaxDuration: maxDur,
		// Hitting the budget (turns OR duration) → the SDK runs a wrap-up round (with
		// Bash hidden) to write back what's identified, avoiding unfinished tails.
		// When clamped (by the task deadline), use PromptByReason: timeout = task
		// deadline → task-timeout prompt; turns = the turn budget ran out inside the
		// clamped window → fall back to the per-run prompt. Non-clamped stays pure per-run.
		Settlement: settle,
		// large tool output spills to cmd-output/ with a head + pointer (SDK tool.Capture);
		// full output preserved on disk. The truncation cap uses the SDK default (30000
		// chars).
		ToolOutputDir: cmdOutDir(runDir),
		Compaction:    compactionConfig(w.compactionWindow()), // long tool-heavy runs stay within the window
		Todos:         actool.NewTodoStore(),                  // session-level scratch todos (TodoWrite), pure planning, discarded on exit
		NonStreaming:  w.nonStreaming(),                       // when this profile selects non-streaming, use Provider.Complete
		MaxTokens:     w.maxTokens(),                          // 0 = send no cap; the server default decides

		// On by default; HIVE_UNTRUSTED_BOUNDARY=0 opts out: nonce-frame tool output as untrusted data.
		UntrustedOutputBoundary: untrustedBoundaryEnabled(),
	}
	if hooks != nil { // typed-nil guard: only set when concrete (avoids harness panic)
		opts.Hooks = hooks
	}
	if w.tx != nil { // persist raw LLM conversation; one file per worked intent
		opts.Transcript = w.tx
		opts.SessionID = WorkerSessionID(ts.ID(), intent.ID)
	}
	intentID := intent.ID
	emitWrap := func(r db.Activity) {
		if emit != nil {
			r.NodeID, r.Worker = &intentID, name
			emit(r)
		}
	}
	// The intent / launch instruction / intent-anchored assets were already delivered
	// with the system prompt (see the sysBody assembly above). This launch user message
	// carries only the [global situation overview] — degradable big-picture info, safe
	// to compact away. In the rare case the overview marshals to empty, fall back to a
	// launch sentence so the first turn isn't an empty user message.
	input := overview
	if strings.TrimSpace(input) == "" {
		input = "Start executing the intent claimed in system: do only it, produce only facts, assets, findings, stop when done."
	}

	// Experimental: when on, noa takes over context compression (archives persist under <workDir>/noa/<SessionID>).
	noaSession := WorkerSessionID(ts.ID(), intent.ID)
	enableNoa(&opts, w.noaEnabledFn, w.workDir, noaSession, noaWarn(noaSession))
	ctx = attachSideCapture(ctx, &opts)
	s := agentcore.NewSession(opts)
	defer s.Close() // release the session's background-task manager (temp dir + processes)

	// Resume prior conversation if this intent was paused/blocked/exhausted and is
	// being re-run. The transcript ID is deterministic per intent, so if a prior
	// session exists the worker continues from where it left off instead of
	// restarting from scratch.
	alreadyRecorded := false
	if w.tx != nil {
		_ = s.Resume(opts.SessionID)
		alreadyRecorded = requestID != "" && hasWorkerChatMessage(s.Messages(), requestID)
		if len(s.Messages()) > 0 && message == "" {
			seedUnlockFromHistory(s.Messages(), def.UnlockSkill)
			input = "Continue."
		} else if len(s.Messages()) > 0 {
			seedUnlockFromHistory(s.Messages(), def.UnlockSkill)
		}
	}
	if message != "" {
		if alreadyRecorded {
			input = "Continue executing the new intent entered in the previous human conversation. Do not repeat actions already completed."
		} else if len(s.Messages()) > 0 {
			input = workerChatMarker(requestID) + "\n[New intent entered via human conversation]\n" + message +
				"\n\nExecute this human input immediately; after completing it, decide from the context whether the original task needs to continue."
		} else {
			input += "\n\n" + workerChatMarker(requestID) + "\n[New intent entered via human conversation]\n" + message +
				"\n\nExecute this human input first."
		}
	}

	// Budgets + settlement are owned by the SDK (MaxTurns/MaxDuration + Settlement):
	// on hit it runs a wrap-up turn and finishes with ReasonMaxTurns/ReasonTimeout.
	// MaxDuration now interrupts an in-flight tool at the wall-clock deadline and
	// enters the wrap-up phase on the live ctx, so a run whose tool overran the budget
	// still settles (no external hard-timeout backstop needed). ctx itself carries only
	// pause / planner kill / shutdown, which the engine distinguishes and re-queues/stops.
	_, reason, err := captureRunSession(ctx, s, input, emitWrap)
	return reason, tsx.Writes(), err
}

package agent

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/Autumn-27/norma/llm"
)

func TestWorkerSessionIDIsStablePerIntent(t *testing.T) {
	if got := WorkerSessionID(12, 34); got != "exp12-worker-i34" {
		t.Fatalf("session id = %q, want exp12-worker-i34", got)
	}
}

func TestWorkerChatMarkerOnlyMatchesItsNormalUserTurn(t *testing.T) {
	requestID := "worker-message-123"
	messages := []llm.Message{
		{Role: llm.RoleAssistant, Content: []llm.ContentBlock{llm.TextBlock(workerChatMarker(requestID))}},
		llm.UserText(workerChatMarker("worker-message-other") + "\nother"),
		llm.UserText(workerChatMarker(requestID) + "\nnew intent"),
	}
	if !hasWorkerChatMessage(messages, requestID) {
		t.Fatal("expected the matching user turn to be detected")
	}
	if hasWorkerChatMessage(messages, "worker-message-missing") {
		t.Fatal("unrelated request id matched a Worker user turn")
	}
}

=====================================================================
FILE: agent/wrapup.go

package agent

import (
	"strings"
	"sync"

	"github.com/Autumn-27/norma/harness"
)

// Wrap-up prompts (settlement prompts): when an agent is terminated because of
// [turn budget exhausted (MaxTurns)] or [timeout (run_seconds/MaxDuration)], the
// SDK's settlement phase injects this prompt so the agent first persists what it
// has identified but not yet written back, then outputs a one-sentence summary —
// no unfinished tails.
//
// Each agent's wrap-up prompt can be overridden in the admin backend (stored in
// agents.wrapup_prompt); left empty, the built-in defaults here are used. Only the
// [prompt body] is editable; which tools are disabled and how many turns the
// wrap-up itself gets are code-fixed policy.

// wrapupHooksMu guards the four wrap-up hooks in this file: server wiring can run
// while agents build their settlement config on other goroutines.
var wrapupHooksMu sync.RWMutex

// wrapupOverride, if set, returns the stored wrap-up prompt for an agent key and
// whether a non-empty one exists. Wired by the server to the agents table (like
// PromptOverride for system prompts). nil / empty → the built-in default is used.
var wrapupOverride func(agentKey string) (string, bool)

// SetWrapupOverride installs (or, with nil, removes) the WrapupOverride hook.
func SetWrapupOverride(f func(agentKey string) (string, bool)) {
	wrapupHooksMu.Lock()
	wrapupOverride = f
	wrapupHooksMu.Unlock()
}

// WrapupOverride returns the current hook, or nil when none is set.
func WrapupOverride() func(agentKey string) (string, bool) {
	wrapupHooksMu.RLock()
	defer wrapupHooksMu.RUnlock()
	return wrapupOverride
}

// wrapupMaxTurnsOverride, if set, returns the admin-configured turn budget for the
// wrap-up phase of an agent and whether a positive one exists. Wired to the agents
// table. nil / ≤0 → the built-in per-agent default (wrapupTurnDefaults) is used.
var wrapupMaxTurnsOverride func(agentKey string) (int, bool)

// SetWrapupMaxTurnsOverride installs (or, with nil, removes) the WrapupMaxTurnsOverride hook.
func SetWrapupMaxTurnsOverride(f func(agentKey string) (int, bool)) {
	wrapupHooksMu.Lock()
	wrapupMaxTurnsOverride = f
	wrapupHooksMu.Unlock()
}

// WrapupMaxTurnsOverride returns the current hook, or nil when none is set.
func WrapupMaxTurnsOverride() func(agentKey string) (int, bool) {
	wrapupHooksMu.RLock()
	defer wrapupHooksMu.RUnlock()
	return wrapupMaxTurnsOverride
}

// Built-in default wrap-up prompts, keyed by agent key. worker reuses the
// historically hardcoded settleWrapUpPrompt (defined in worker.go); planner and
// mainagent each have their own; unmatched keys (custom agents) get the generic
// fallback.
var wrapupDefaults = map[string]string{
	"worker":    settleWrapUpPrompt,
	"planner":   plannerWrapUpDefault,
	"mainagent": mainAgentWrapUpDefault,
}

// wrapupTurnDefaults: the built-in default turn budget of each agent's own wrap-up
// phase (overridable in the admin backend with >0). All get 10 turns so the wrap-up
// phase has enough steps to persist. Unmatched keys use genericWrapupTurns.
var wrapupTurnDefaults = map[string]int{
	"worker":    10,
	"planner":   10,
	"mainagent": 10,
}

const genericWrapupTurns = 10

const plannerWrapUpDefault = "Your turn budget for THIS planning round is about to run out — note that only [this round] ends; the system will wake you again as the situation changes to keep planning, the task is not terminated, and you don't need to converge the whole plan here. Land the conclusions this round has already figured out — don't let this round go to waste — but [don't force intents just for the wrap-up] (0 intents this round is still a perfectly normal outcome): (1) if you've identified exploration directions [due for dispatch now], submit them with one add_intent batch call (don't sit on ones you've figured out); (2) for goals proven met by some finding/fact, call prove_goal to mark met (don't miss any); (3) if you've identified a serial exploit chain needing steps, record it with TodoWrite so you can continue dispatching at the next wake. Finish the round directly when done; no summary text needed."

const mainAgentWrapUpDefault = "Your turn budget is about to run out and this interaction is about to end. Do not start any new exploration/operation. Please summarize for the user **in a single standalone sentence of plain text**: current progress, key conclusions, and the suggested next step."

const genericWrapUpDefault = "You are about to be terminated because your budget is exhausted. First write back completed-but-unpersisted results, then summarize **in a single standalone sentence of plain text** what you did and which key conclusions you reached (this sentence is shown as this run's result)."

// WrapupDefault returns the built-in default wrap-up prompt for an agent key —
// used by the admin UI as the "restore default" value and empty-field placeholder.
func WrapupDefault(agentKey string) string {
	if d, ok := wrapupDefaults[agentKey]; ok {
		return d
	}
	return genericWrapUpDefault
}

// WrapupTurnsDefault returns the built-in wrap-up turn budget for an agent key —
// used by the admin UI as the "0 = default N" hint.
func WrapupTurnsDefault(agentKey string) int {
	if n, ok := wrapupTurnDefaults[agentKey]; ok {
		return n
	}
	return genericWrapupTurns
}

// resolveWrapup returns the effective wrap-up prompt: the DB override (if set and
// non-empty) over the built-in default.
func resolveWrapup(agentKey string) string {
	if override := WrapupOverride(); override != nil {
		if t, ok := override(agentKey); ok && strings.TrimSpace(t) != "" {
			return t
		}
	}
	return WrapupDefault(agentKey)
}

// resolveWrapupTurns returns the effective wrap-up turn budget: a positive DB
// override over the built-in per-agent default.
func resolveWrapupTurns(agentKey string) int {
	if override := WrapupMaxTurnsOverride(); override != nil {
		if v, ok := override(agentKey); ok && v > 0 {
			return v
		}
	}
	return WrapupTurnsDefault(agentKey)
}

// wrapupSettlement builds the settlement config for an agent's run. Prompt and the
// turn budget are admin-editable per agent; disabled tools are code-owned policy so
// a user can't edit away the "stop probing" guardrail. Resolved fresh each run
// (reads DB live), so edits apply on the next run without a restart.
func wrapupSettlement(agentKey string, disabledTools []string) *harness.Settlement {
	return &harness.Settlement{
		Prompt:        resolveWrapup(agentKey),
		DisabledTools: disabledTools,
		MaxTurns:      resolveWrapupTurns(agentKey),
	}
}

// ---------- Task-level timeout wrap-up prompts (see the task-level timeout and wrap-up design doc) ----------
//
// These are [two separate sets] from the per-run wrap-up prompts: per-run says
// "this run's budget is used up"; task timeout says "the whole task is out of time
// and about to end". The semantics are often opposite (especially for the planner:
// per-run says "don't stop, keep planning", task timeout says "stop planning at the
// deadline, make the final judgment"). Configured only for worker/planner.

// WrapupTaskTimeoutOverride / …TurnsOverride: DB overrides for the task-timeout
// wrap-up prompt and turns (wired to agents.task_timeout_wrapup_prompt /
// _max_turns, worker/planner only).
// Guarded by wrapupHooksMu, like the per-run hooks above.
var (
	wrapupTaskTimeoutOverride      func(agentKey string) (string, bool)
	wrapupTaskTimeoutTurnsOverride func(agentKey string) (int, bool)
)

// SetWrapupTaskTimeoutOverride installs (or, with nil, removes) the hook.
func SetWrapupTaskTimeoutOverride(f func(agentKey string) (string, bool)) {
	wrapupHooksMu.Lock()
	wrapupTaskTimeoutOverride = f
	wrapupHooksMu.Unlock()
}

// WrapupTaskTimeoutOverride returns the current hook, or nil when none is set.
func WrapupTaskTimeoutOverride() func(agentKey string) (string, bool) {
	wrapupHooksMu.RLock()
	defer wrapupHooksMu.RUnlock()
	return wrapupTaskTimeoutOverride
}

// SetWrapupTaskTimeoutTurnsOverride installs (or, with nil, removes) the hook.
func SetWrapupTaskTimeoutTurnsOverride(f func(agentKey string) (int, bool)) {
	wrapupHooksMu.Lock()
	wrapupTaskTimeoutTurnsOverride = f
	wrapupHooksMu.Unlock()
}

// WrapupTaskTimeoutTurnsOverride returns the current hook, or nil when none is set.
func WrapupTaskTimeoutTurnsOverride() func(agentKey string) (int, bool) {
	wrapupHooksMu.RLock()
	defer wrapupHooksMu.RUnlock()
	return wrapupTaskTimeoutTurnsOverride
}

var taskTimeoutWrapupDefaults = map[string]string{
	"worker":  workerTaskTimeoutDefault,
	"planner": plannerTaskTimeoutDefault,
}

const workerTaskTimeoutDefault = "**The entire task has reached its timeout limit and is about to end** (not your run's budget — the whole engagement is out of time). This is the last chance: (1) write back [ALL] content you've identified but not yet persisted — new assets with insert_assets, exploration conclusions/facts with record_fact, confirmed findings with report_finding; (2) do not start any new commands/probes; (3) **finally, in a single standalone sentence of plain text** summarize your key conclusions on this intent."

const plannerTaskTimeoutDefault = "**The entire task has reached its timeout limit and is about to end** (not this round — the whole task terminates). Based on the current [full] set of facts and findings, make the final goal judgment: for goals proven met by evidence, call prove_goal to mark met (don't miss any). **Do not generate any new intents** (any intent dispatched now won't be executed). Conclude once judged; no summary text needed."

// TaskTimeoutWrapupDefault returns an agent's built-in default task-timeout wrap-up
// prompt (for the admin placeholder / restore-default).
func TaskTimeoutWrapupDefault(agentKey string) string {
	return taskTimeoutWrapupDefaults[agentKey] // unconfigured agents (mainagent/chat) get an empty string
}

// resolveTaskTimeoutWrapup: DB override (non-empty) > built-in default. An empty
// string means this agent has no task-timeout prompt (not worker/planner) — the
// caller should then fall back to the per-run prompt.
func resolveTaskTimeoutWrapup(agentKey string) string {
	if override := WrapupTaskTimeoutOverride(); override != nil {
		if t, ok := override(agentKey); ok && strings.TrimSpace(t) != "" {
			return t
		}
	}
	return TaskTimeoutWrapupDefault(agentKey)
}

func resolveTaskTimeoutTurns(agentKey string) int {
	if override := WrapupTaskTimeoutTurnsOverride(); override != nil {
		if v, ok := override(agentKey); ok && v > 0 {
			return v
		}
	}
	return resolveWrapupTurns(agentKey) // by default inherit the per-run turns
}

// wrapupSettlementForTask builds settlement for a worker/planner run that is aware
// of the task deadline. See §5 of the design doc:
//   - clamped=true  → this run is clamped by the task deadline: settling on Timeout
//     = the task hit its deadline → task-timeout prompt; settling on MaxTurns = the
//     turn budget ran out inside the clamped window while the task still has minutes
//     left → fall back to the per-run prompt.
//   - clamped=false → the task is far from its deadline: both reasons use the
//     per-run prompt (i.e. degrades to wrapupSettlement).
//
// The PromptByReason handed to harness picks at settlement time by the [actual]
// reason — no mismatch at build time.
func wrapupSettlementForTask(agentKey string, disabledTools []string, clamped bool) *harness.Settlement {
	perRun := resolveWrapup(agentKey)
	st := &harness.Settlement{
		Prompt:        perRun, // fallback (also the value for both reasons when not clamped)
		DisabledTools: disabledTools,
		MaxTurns:      resolveWrapupTurns(agentKey),
	}
	if clamped {
		if tt := resolveTaskTimeoutWrapup(agentKey); tt != "" {
			st.PromptByReason = map[harness.TerminalReason]string{
				harness.ReasonTimeout:  tt,     // task hit its deadline
				harness.ReasonMaxTurns: perRun, // turns ran out first; the task still has time
			}
			st.MaxTurns = resolveTaskTimeoutTurns(agentKey)
		}
	}
	return st
}

=====================================================================
FILE: build.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# HIVE cross-platform release builder.
#
# The default mode builds one target and embeds the already-exported frontend.
# `./build.sh --release` builds and packages all supported desktop/server targets.
#
# Environment variables:
#   HIVE_TARGET_OS=linux             One target OS in single-target mode.
#   HIVE_TARGET_ARCH=amd64           One target arch in single-target mode.
#   HIVE_TARGETS=linux/amd64,...     Comma-separated targets for multi-target mode.
#   HIVE_BUILD_VERSION=vX.Y.Z        Version embedded in the binary and archive name.
#   HIVE_OUTPUT=/path/to/hive       Explicit binary path in single-target mode.
#   HIVE_OUTPUT_DIR=dist             Directory for default binary paths.
#   HIVE_PACKAGE=1                   Create a zip archive for each target.
#   HIVE_PACKAGE_DIR=dist            Directory for release archives.
#   HIVE_COMPRESS=off                UPX mode: off, auto, or required.
#   HIVE_UPX_ARGS="--best --lzma"    Arguments passed to UPX.
#   HIVE_SKIP_FRONTEND=1             Reuse server/webui/dist (for CI artifact builds).
#   HIVE_SKIP_NPM_CI=1               Skip npm ci while rebuilding the frontend.
#   HIVE_GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org      Go checksum database.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

info() { printf '\033[36m[*]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok() { printf '\033[32m[+]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[33m[!]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die() { printf '\033[31m[x]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage:
  ./build.sh                         Build for the current OS and architecture
  ./build.sh --target linux/amd64   Build one specific target
  ./build.sh --release               Build and package all supported targets

Options:
  --release              Build the amd64/arm64 targets for Linux, macOS, and Windows, and generate zips
  --target OS/ARCH       Set a single target, e.g. windows/amd64
  --upx                  Force UPX compression of the binary (may affect compatibility on some Linux environments)
  --no-compress          No UPX; use only Go linker trimming and zip compression
  --help                 Show this help

The multi-target list can be overridden via HIVE_TARGETS, e.g.:
  HIVE_TARGETS=linux/amd64,windows/amd64 ./build.sh --release
EOF
}

RELEASE_TARGETS_DEFAULT="linux/amd64,linux/arm64,darwin/amd64,darwin/arm64,windows/amd64"
HIVE_RELEASE="${HIVE_RELEASE:-0}"
HIVE_COMPRESS="${HIVE_COMPRESS:-off}"
HIVE_PACKAGE="${HIVE_PACKAGE:-0}"

while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --release)
      HIVE_RELEASE=1
      HIVE_PACKAGE=1
      shift
      ;;
    --target)
      [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || die "--target requires an OS/ARCH argument"
      target_arg="$2"
      case "$target_arg" in
        */*)
          HIVE_TARGET_OS="${target_arg%%/*}"
          HIVE_TARGET_ARCH="${target_arg##*/}"
          HIVE_TARGETS="$target_arg"
          ;;
        *) die "target must be OS/ARCH, e.g. linux/amd64" ;;
      esac
      shift 2
      ;;
    --no-compress)
      HIVE_COMPRESS=0
      shift
      ;;
    --upx)
      HIVE_COMPRESS=required
      shift
      ;;
    --help|-h)
      usage
      exit 0
      ;;
    *) die "unknown argument: $1 (use --help for usage)" ;;
  esac
done

command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "Go not detected (the project requires Go 1.26 or newer)"

HIVE_GOSUMDB="${HIVE_GOSUMDB:-sum.golang.org}"
if [ -z "${HIVE_BUILD_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    HIVE_BUILD_VERSION="$(git describe --tags --always --dirty)"
  else
    HIVE_BUILD_VERSION="dev"
  fi
fi
# Release tags are commonly passed with a v prefix; keep the binary version consistent.
HIVE_BUILD_VERSION="${HIVE_BUILD_VERSION#v}"
HIVE_OUTPUT_DIR="${HIVE_OUTPUT_DIR:-dist}"
HIVE_PACKAGE_DIR="${HIVE_PACKAGE_DIR:-$HIVE_OUTPUT_DIR}"
HIVE_UPX_ARGS="${HIVE_UPX_ARGS:---best --lzma}"

if [ "${HIVE_RELEASE}" = "1" ]; then
  HIVE_TARGETS="${HIVE_TARGETS:-$RELEASE_TARGETS_DEFAULT}"
else
  HIVE_TARGET_OS="${HIVE_TARGET_OS:-$(GOSUMDB="$HIVE_GOSUMDB" go env GOOS)}"
  HIVE_TARGET_ARCH="${HIVE_TARGET_ARCH:-$(GOSUMDB="$HIVE_GOSUMDB" go env GOARCH)}"
  HIVE_TARGETS="${HIVE_TARGETS:-${HIVE_TARGET_OS}/${HIVE_TARGET_ARCH}}"
fi

if [ "${HIVE_SKIP_FRONTEND:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  [ -d server/webui/dist ] || die "HIVE_SKIP_FRONTEND=1 but server/webui/dist does not exist"
else
  command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "npm not detected (building the frontend static assets requires Node.js/npm)"
  command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "rsync not detected"
  info "Building frontend static assets"
  if [ "${HIVE_SKIP_NPM_CI:-0}" != "1" ]; then
    (cd web && npm ci)
  fi
  (cd web && npm run build:static)
  info "Syncing frontend assets to server/webui/dist"
  mkdir -p server/webui/dist
  rsync -a --delete web/out/ server/webui/dist/
fi

compress_binary() {
  binary="$1"
  goos="$2"
  case "$HIVE_COMPRESS" in
    0|off|false|none)
      info "Skipping UPX: $binary"
      return 0
      ;;
    auto|required|true|1) ;;
    *) die "HIVE_COMPRESS must be off, auto, or required" ;;
  esac

  if ! command -v upx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if [ "$HIVE_COMPRESS" = "required" ]; then
      die "HIVE_COMPRESS=required but upx was not detected"
    fi
    warn "upx not detected; keeping the linker-compressed result: $binary"
    return 0
  fi

  before=$(wc -c < "$binary" | tr -d ' ')
  upx_args="$HIVE_UPX_ARGS"
  [ "$goos" = "darwin" ] && upx_args="$upx_args --force-macos"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  if ! upx $upx_args -- "$binary"; then
    if [ "$HIVE_COMPRESS" = "required" ]; then
      die "UPX compression failed: $binary"
    fi
    warn "UPX does not support this target format; keeping the uncompressed binary: $binary"
    return 0
  fi
  after=$(wc -c < "$binary" | tr -d ' ')
  ok "UPX compression done: $binary (${before} -> ${after} bytes)"
}

package_binary() {
  binary="$1"
  goos="$2"
  goarch="$3"
  package_name="hive-${HIVE_BUILD_VERSION}-${goos}-${goarch}"
  package_root="${HIVE_PACKAGE_DIR}/${package_name}"
  archive="${HIVE_PACKAGE_DIR}/${package_name}.zip"

  command -v zip >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "packaging requires zip"
  rm -rf "$package_root" "$archive"
  mkdir -p "$package_root"
  cp "$binary" "$package_root/"
  # The guardian start script is the official entry point: the page's one-click
  # update relies on it to relaunch the process after it exits; running the hive
  # binary directly means it never comes back up after an update. Ship only the one
  # matching the target OS.
  if [ "$goos" = "windows" ]; then
    cp start.bat "$package_root/"
  else
    cp start.sh "$package_root/"
    chmod +x "$package_root/start.sh"
  fi
  cp -R skills "$package_root/"
  cp config.example.json "$package_root/"
  if [ -f README.md ]; then cp README.md "$package_root/"; fi
  (cd "$HIVE_PACKAGE_DIR" && zip -q -r -9 "$(basename "$archive")" "$(basename "$package_root")")
  rm -rf "$package_root"
  ok "Release archive: $archive"
}

build_target() {
  target="$1"
  case "$target" in
    */*) ;;
    *) die "invalid target: $target (must be OS/ARCH)" ;;
  esac
  goos="${target%%/*}"
  goarch="${target##*/}"
  case "$goos" in
    linux|darwin|windows) ;;
    *) die "unsupported OS: $goos (supported: linux, darwin, windows)" ;;
  esac

  binary_name="hive"
  [ "$goos" = "windows" ] && binary_name="hive.exe"
  if [ -n "${HIVE_OUTPUT:-}" ] && [ "$HIVE_RELEASE" != "1" ]; then
    output="$HIVE_OUTPUT"
  else
    output="${HIVE_OUTPUT_DIR}/hive-${goos}-${goarch}/${binary_name}"
  fi
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$output")"

  info "Compiling ${goos}/${goarch}, version ${HIVE_BUILD_VERSION}"
  GOSUMDB="$HIVE_GOSUMDB" \
  CGO_ENABLED=0 \
  GOOS="$goos" \
  GOARCH="$goarch" \
  go build \
    -tags embedui \
    -trimpath \
    -ldflags "-s -w -buildid= -X main.version=${HIVE_BUILD_VERSION}" \
    -o "$output" \
    ./cmd/hive

  compress_binary "$output" "$goos"
  if command -v file >/dev/null 2>&1; then file "$output"; fi
  if [ "$HIVE_PACKAGE" = "1" ]; then package_binary "$output" "$goos" "$goarch"; fi
  ok "Build complete: $output"
}

write_checksums() {
  [ "$HIVE_PACKAGE" = "1" ] || return 0
  checksum_file="$HIVE_PACKAGE_DIR/SHA256SUMS"
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    (cd "$HIVE_PACKAGE_DIR" && for archive in *.zip; do sha256sum "$archive"; done > "$(basename "$checksum_file")")
  elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    (cd "$HIVE_PACKAGE_DIR" && for archive in *.zip; do shasum -a 256 "$archive"; done > "$(basename "$checksum_file")")
  else
    warn "Neither sha256sum nor shasum detected; skipping SHA256SUMS"
    return 0
  fi
  ok "Checksum file: $checksum_file"
}

mkdir -p "$HIVE_OUTPUT_DIR"
if [ "$HIVE_PACKAGE" = "1" ]; then mkdir -p "$HIVE_PACKAGE_DIR"; fi

old_ifs="$IFS"
IFS=','
read -r -a targets <<< "$HIVE_TARGETS"
IFS="$old_ifs"
[ "${#targets[@]}" -gt 0 ] || die "HIVE_TARGETS must not be empty"
for target in "${targets[@]}"; do
  target="${target//[[:space:]]/}"
  [ -n "$target" ] || continue
  build_target "$target"
done

if [ "$HIVE_PACKAGE" = "1" ]; then
  write_checksums
  info "Release packages generated in: $HIVE_PACKAGE_DIR"
fi

// Command hive runs the HIVE backend: the dual PostgreSQL graph stores,
// the event-driven exploration engine, and the JSON HTTP API consumed by the
// shadcn/ui frontend.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/agent"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/config"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/server"
)

// version is the build version, injected at release time via
// -ldflags "-X main.version=<tag>". Defaults to "dev" for local builds.
var version = "dev"

const banner = `
    _    ____ _____ _______  __
   / \  |  _ \_   _| ____\ \/ /
  / _ \ | |_) || | |  _|  \  /
 / ___ \|  _ < | | | |___ /  \
/_/   \_\_| \_\|_| |_____/_/\_\
`

// printBanner writes the startup banner + version/runtime info to stdout.
func printBanner(addr string) {
	fmt.Print(banner)
	fmt.Println("  AI autonomous penetration testing system")
	fmt.Printf("  version %s  ·  %s/%s  ·  %s  ·  listening on %s\n\n",
		version, runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH, runtime.Version(), addr)
}

// main maps run's result onto the process exit code. The body lives in a
// function that can *return* rather than os.Exit, so its own defers still run.
func main() {
	os.Exit(run())
}

func run() int {
	var (
		addr    = flag.String("addr", "127.0.0.1:8787", "HTTP listen address")
		dataDir = flag.String("data", filepath.Join(config.BaseDir(), "data"), "runtime data directory: traffic index, task files, transcripts (default: data/ next to the executable)")
		proxy   = flag.String("proxy", "127.0.0.1:8788", "traffic recording proxy address (empty to disable)")
	)
	flag.Parse()

	// hand the build version to the server package so GET /api/health can report it
	// to the frontend top bar.
	server.BuildVersion = version

	printBanner(*addr)

	// capture backend logs into the in-memory sink (still to stderr) so the /logs
	// page can show a live log stream. Do this first, to catch startup logs too.
	server.StartLogCapture()

	// surface which config file the binary reads (absolute, so `go run`'s relative
	// "config.json" — resolved against the CWD — is unambiguous).
	cfgPath := config.Path()
	if abs, e := filepath.Abs(cfgPath); e == nil {
		cfgPath = abs
	}
	if _, e := os.Stat(cfgPath); e == nil {
		log.Printf("[config] config file: %s", cfgPath)
	} else {
		log.Printf("[config] config file: %s (not found — will only try the environment variable HIVE_PG_DSN)", cfgPath)
	}

	sigCtx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	ctx, shutdown := shutdownContext(sigCtx)
	defer shutdown(agent.AbortShutdown)

	mgr, err := server.NewManager(*dataDir, *proxy)
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("open stores: %v", err)
	}
	defer mgr.Close()

	skillDir, err := config.SkillDir()
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("[config] %v", err)
		return 1
	}
	if abs, err := filepath.Abs(skillDir); err == nil {
		skillDir = abs
	}
	log.Printf("[config] skill directory: %s", skillDir)
	// JWT signing key directory (also holds secret.key, see server.NewManager).
	keyDir := config.KeyDir()
	log.Printf("[config] JWT key directory: %s", keyDir)
	// Proxies whose X-Forwarded-For the login rate limit reads; empty trusts none.
	trusted, err := server.ParseTrustedProxies(os.Getenv("HIVE_TRUSTED_PROXIES"))
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("[config] HIVE_TRUSTED_PROXIES: %v", err)
		return 1
	}
	if len(trusted) > 0 {
		log.Printf("[config] trusted proxies: %v", trusted)
	}
	srv := server.New(ctx, mgr, skillDir, *dataDir, keyDir, server.WithSecretScrub(), server.WithTrustedProxies(trusted))
	// Part 01: repair stale model ids against live catalogs, then validate the
	// non-local profiles, so a broken pool is loud at boot instead of 404ing in
	// the planner loop. Runs async — catalog fetches must not block startup.
	go srv.RepairLLMProfiles(ctx)
	httpSrv := &http.Server{
		Addr:              *addr,
		Handler:           srv.Handler(),
		ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
	}

	go func() {
		log.Printf("Hive %s backend listening on %s (data=%s, workers=%d)", version, *addr, *dataDir, mgr.Workers())
		if err := httpSrv.ListenAndServe(); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
			log.Fatalf("serve: %v", err)
		}
	}()

	// Wait for a stop signal.
	<-ctx.Done()

	log.Println("shutting down...")
	shutdownCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	_ = httpSrv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx)
	return 0
}

// shutdownContext deliberately does not derive from signalCtx. If it did, the
// parent's plain context.Canceled could win the race before AbortShutdown was
// attached to the child, losing the diagnostic cause in every running Agent.
func shutdownContext(signalCtx context.Context) (context.Context, context.CancelCauseFunc) {
	ctx, shutdown := context.WithCancelCause(context.Background())
	go func() {
		select {
		case <-signalCtx.Done():
			shutdown(agent.AbortShutdown)
		case <-ctx.Done():
		}
	}()
	return ctx, shutdown
}

FILE: cmd/hive/main_test.go
=====================================================================
package main

import (
	"context"
	"testing"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/agent"
)

// The shutdown cause must survive the parent context being cancelled first;
// losing it would drop the diagnostic on every graceful stop.
func TestShutdownContextPreservesNamedCause(t *testing.T) {
	signalCtx, signalCancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	ctx, shutdown := shutdownContext(signalCtx)
	defer shutdown(nil)
	signalCancel()
	<-ctx.Done()
	if code, _, _, ok := agent.AbortReason(ctx); !ok || code != "shutdown" {
		t.Fatalf("code=%q ok=%v, want shutdown", code, ok)
	}
}

FILE: config/config.go

// Package config loads runtime configuration from a JSON file, with environment
// variables taking precedence. Currently it carries the PostgreSQL connection.
package config

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// Database is the PostgreSQL connection config. Either set DSN directly, or set
// the component fields and a DSN is assembled from them.
type Database struct {
	DSN      string `json:"dsn"`
	Host     string `json:"host"`
	Port     int    `json:"port"`
	User     string `json:"user"`
	Password string `json:"password"`
	DBName   string `json:"dbname"`
	SSLMode  string `json:"sslmode"`
}

// Config is the on-disk config file shape.
type Config struct {
	Database Database `json:"database"`
	SkillDir string   `json:"skill_dir"`
}

// BaseDir is the directory that anchors all runtime artifacts (config.json and
// the data/ store). It is the directory the running binary lives in, so a
// distributed executable keeps its files next to itself on any OS (Windows,
// Linux, …) regardless of the working directory it is launched from.
//
// When launched via `go run`, the binary is throwaway: it sits either in a temp
// build dir (cache miss → fresh link) OR straight inside the Go build cache
// (cache hit → run from $GOCACHE/.../...-d). We detect both and fall back to the
// current working directory so dev artifacts (data/, transcripts) and config
// resolve against the project dir, not the throwaway binary's location.
func BaseDir() string {
	exe, err := os.Executable()
	if err != nil {
		return "."
	}
	dir := filepath.Dir(exe)
	if isGoRunDir(dir) {
		return "." // throwaway `go run` binary → use CWD
	}
	return dir
}

// KeyDir holds jwt.key and secret.key: HIVE_JWT_KEY_DIR (the Docker image points
// it at the /app/keys volume) or the base dir. Never the browsable data dir.
func KeyDir() string {
	dir := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("HIVE_JWT_KEY_DIR"))
	if dir == "" {
		dir = BaseDir()
	}
	if abs, err := filepath.Abs(dir); err == nil {
		dir = abs
	}
	return dir
}

// isGoRunDir reports whether dir is where `go run` parked its executable: under
// the system temp dir (cache miss), or anywhere inside a Go build cache
// (…/go-build/…, the cache-hit case — NOT under os.TempDir(), which is why the
// old temp-only check failed intermittently). In both cases the binary is
// throwaway, so config/data must resolve against the CWD.
func isGoRunDir(dir string) bool {
	if tmp := os.TempDir(); tmp != "" {
		if rel, err := filepath.Rel(tmp, dir); err == nil && rel != ".." && !strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)) {
			return true
		}
	}
	for _, seg := range strings.Split(filepath.ToSlash(dir), "/") {
		if seg == "go-build" {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// Path returns the config file path. Resolution order:
//  1. env HIVE_CONFIG (explicit override)
//  2. ./config.json in the current working directory (running from the project
//     dir — robust no matter where `go run` placed the temp/cached binary)
//  3. config.json next to the executable (a distributed binary keeps it beside)
//
// The first existing file wins. If none exist, the CWD path is returned so the
// "not found" message points at the project dir the user most likely expected.
func Path() string {
	if v := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("HIVE_CONFIG")); v != "" {
		return v
	}
	var candidates []string
	if cwd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil {
		candidates = append(candidates, filepath.Join(cwd, "config.json"))
	}
	candidates = append(candidates, filepath.Join(BaseDir(), "config.json"))
	for _, c := range candidates {
		if _, err := os.Stat(c); err == nil {
			return c
		}
	}
	return candidates[0]
}

// Load reads and parses the config file. A missing file yields a zero Config (so
// callers fall back to defaults). A file that exists but cannot be read or parsed
// is an error: ignoring it would run with defaults the operator did not choose.
func Load() (Config, error) {
	var c Config
	path := Path()
	b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
		return c, nil
	}
	if err != nil {
		return c, fmt.Errorf("read config file %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &c); err != nil {
		return Config{}, fmt.Errorf("parse config file %s: %w", path, err)
	}
	return c, nil
}

// SkillDir returns the skill root directory with precedence:
//
//	env HIVE_SKILL_DIR  >  config file (skill_dir)  >  BaseDir()/skills
//
// The directory is created if it does not exist.
func SkillDir() (string, error) {
	var d string
	if v := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("HIVE_SKILL_DIR")); v != "" {
		d = v
	} else {
		c, err := Load()
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		if v := strings.TrimSpace(c.SkillDir); v != "" {
			d = v
		} else {
			d = filepath.Join(BaseDir(), "skills")
		}
	}
	_ = os.MkdirAll(d, 0o755)
	return d, nil
}

// DefaultDSN is the zero-config database: a local PostgreSQL with the default
// hive/hive/hive credentials created by the quick-start install script. It lets
// a fresh install boot without writing any config, and the app then prompts the
// operator to rotate the password on first login (see server/db_security.go).
const DefaultDSN = "postgres://hive:hive@127.0.0.1:5432/hive?sslmode=disable"

// PostgresDSN resolves the connection string with precedence:
//
//	env HIVE_PG_DSN  >  config file (database.dsn, or assembled from fields)  >  built-in DefaultDSN
//
// The built-in default keeps a fresh install bootable with zero configuration;
// the UI surfaces a mandatory password-rotation prompt while it is in effect.
// source describes where the DSN came from (for startup logging + the security
// status endpoint): "environment variable HIVE_PG_DSN", "config file <path>
// (database.dsn|database fields)", or "built-in default credentials".
func PostgresDSN() (dsn, source string, err error) {
	if v := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("HIVE_PG_DSN")); v != "" {
		return v, "environment variable HIVE_PG_DSN", nil
	}
	c, err := Load()
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	db := c.Database
	if d := strings.TrimSpace(db.DSN); d != "" {
		return d, "config file " + Path() + " (database.dsn)", nil
	}
	if db.Host != "" || db.DBName != "" || db.User != "" {
		return db.buildDSN(), "config file " + Path() + " (database fields)", nil
	}
	return DefaultDSN, "built-in default credentials", nil
}

// UsingDefaultCredentials reports whether the resolved DSN is the built-in
// hive/hive/hive default. The UI uses this to decide when to show the
// password-rotation prompt; the change endpoint refuses to run in any other
// state so it cannot be abused as a generic password changer.
func UsingDefaultCredentials() bool {
	dsn, _, err := PostgresDSN()
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	u, err := url.Parse(dsn)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	pw, _ := u.User.Password()
	return u.User.Username() == "hive" && pw == "hive"
}

// SaveDatabaseCreds persists a new database password (and the decomposed
// connection fields derived from the currently resolved DSN) into the config
// file, so the change survives restarts. It refuses to touch an env-var
// configuration (the operator manages that out-of-band). The file is written
// 0600 — it holds a password.
func SaveDatabaseCreds(newPassword string) error {
	if v := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("HIVE_PG_DSN")); v != "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("the database is configured via the HIVE_PG_DSN environment variable; change its password in the environment, not here")
	}
	dsn, _, err := PostgresDSN()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	u, err := url.Parse(dsn)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("parse current DSN: %w", err)
	}
	port := 5432
	if p := u.Port(); p != "" {
		if n, err := strconv.Atoi(p); err == nil {
			port = n
		}
	}
	sslmode := u.Query().Get("sslmode")
	if sslmode == "" {
		sslmode = "disable"
	}
	dbname := strings.TrimPrefix(u.Path, "/")
	c, err := Load()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	c.Database = Database{
		Host:     u.Hostname(),
		Port:     port,
		User:     u.User.Username(),
		Password: newPassword,
		DBName:   dbname,
		SSLMode:  sslmode,
	}
	b, err := json.MarshalIndent(c, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return os.WriteFile(Path(), append(b, '\n'), 0o600)
}

func (d Database) buildDSN() string {
	host := d.Host
	if host == "" {
		host = "127.0.0.1"
	}
	port := d.Port
	if port == 0 {
		port = 5432
	}
	ssl := d.SSLMode
	if ssl == "" {
		ssl = "disable"
	}
	u := url.URL{
		Scheme: "postgres",
		Host:   host + ":" + strconv.Itoa(port),
		Path:   "/" + d.DBName,
	}
	if d.User != "" {
		if d.Password != "" {
			u.User = url.UserPassword(d.User, d.Password)
		} else {
			u.User = url.User(d.User)
		}
	}
	u.RawQuery = url.Values{"sslmode": {ssl}}.Encode()
	return u.String()
}

// String is a redacted view of the resolved DSN (password masked) for logging.
func Redact(dsn string) string {
	u, err := url.Parse(dsn)
	if err != nil {
		return dsn
	}
	if u.User != nil {
		if _, hasPw := u.User.Password(); hasPw {
			u.User = url.UserPassword(u.User.Username(), "****")
		}
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s", u.String())
}

FILE: config/config_test.go
