// The dial reads its address as the check reads the URL: same key for case,
// trailing dot, Unicode, IPv6 brackets and IPv4-mapped IPv6. net/http dials the
// ASCII form of a Unicode name with the scheme's port written (S3).
func TestPinnedDialNormalisesLikeTheCheck(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct{ rawURL, addr string }{
		{"https://App.Example.COM./x", "App.Example.COM.:443"},
		{"http://bücher.example/", "xn--bcher-kva.example:80"},
		{"https://[2001:DB8::1]:8443/", "[2001:db8::1]:8443"},
		{"http://[::ffff:192.0.2.1]/", "[::ffff:192.0.2.1]:80"},
	} {
		want, err := urlTarget(tc.rawURL)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		got, err := addrTarget("tcp", tc.addr)
		if err != nil || got != want {
			t.Errorf("%s: dial key %+v (%v), check key %+v", tc.addr, got, err, want)
		}
	}
	var dialled string
	tr := &http.Transport{DialContext: func(_ context.Context, _, addr string) (net.Conn, error) {
		dialled = addr
		return nil, errors.New("recorded")
	}}
	_, _ = (&http.Client{Transport: tr}).Get("http://bücher.example/")
	if dialled != "xn--bcher-kva.example:80" {
		t.Fatalf("net/http dialled %q, want the ASCII name and the scheme's port", dialled)
	}
}

// Concurrent dials of one host share one lookup; the cached answer is not
// used, and the cache holds the new answer afterwards.
func TestPinnedDialFreshLookupCollapsed(t *testing.T) {
	g, rec := dialGate(t)
	srv, _, port := pinnedServer(t, "fresh")
	rec.route("203.0.113.7:"+port, srv.Listener.Addr().String())
	g.pin("app.example.com", atoiPort(t, port), "203.0.113.7")
	g.res.set("app.example.com", "203.0.113.9")
	if _, err := g.ic.resolve.lookup(context.Background(), "app.example.com", false); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// The cache now holds 203.0.113.9, which no pin covers: a dial that used it
	// would open a request, which this fixture cannot.
	g.res.set("app.example.com", "203.0.113.7")
	hold := make(chan struct{})
	g.res.mu.Lock()
	g.res.hold = hold
	g.res.mu.Unlock()
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	errs := make(chan error, 2)
	for range 2 {
		wg.Go(func() {
			conn, err := PinnedDialer("WebFetch", true)(g.ctx(), "tcp", "app.example.com:"+port)
			if err == nil {
				conn.Close()
			}
			errs <- err
		})
	}
	eventually(t, "the shared lookup", func() bool { return g.res.lookups("app.example.com") == 2 })
	time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
	close(hold)
	wg.Wait()
	close(errs)
	for err := range errs {
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("dial: %v", err)
		}
	}
	if n := g.res.lookups("app.example.com"); n != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("%d lookups, want the cached one and one shared by both dials", n)
	}
	g.ic.resolve.mu.Lock()
	cached := g.ic.resolve.entries["app.example.com"].ips
	g.ic.resolve.mu.Unlock()
	if !slices.Equal(cached, []string{"203.0.113.7"}) || !slices.Equal(rec.calls(), []string{"203.0.113.7:" + port, "203.0.113.7:" + port}) {
		t.Fatalf("cache %v, dialled %v", cached, rec.calls())
	}
}

// The compared addresses are tried in canonical order, the first that accepts
// wins; tcp4 skips the IPv6 ones.
func TestPinnedDialTriesAddressesInOrder(t *testing.T) {
	g, rec := dialGate(t)
	srv, _, port := pinnedServer(t, "second")
	rec.refuse["203.0.113.7:"+port] = true
	rec.route("203.0.113.8:"+port, srv.Listener.Addr().String())
	g.pin("app.example.com", atoiPort(t, port), "203.0.113.7", "203.0.113.8")
	g.res.set("app.example.com", "203.0.113.8", "203.0.113.7")
	if body, err := get(g.ctx(), pinnedClient(true), "http://app.example.com:"+port+"/"); err != nil || body != "second" {
		t.Fatalf("fetch: %q, %v", body, err)
	}
	if got := rec.calls(); !slices.Equal(got, []string{"203.0.113.7:" + port, "203.0.113.8:" + port}) {
		t.Fatalf("dialled %v", got)
	}

	g, rec = dialGate(t)
	rec.route("203.0.113.8:"+port, srv.Listener.Addr().String())
	g.pin("app.example.com", atoiPort(t, port), "2001:db8::1", "203.0.113.8")
	g.res.set("app.example.com", "2001:db8::1", "203.0.113.8")
	conn, err := PinnedDialer("WebFetch", true)(g.ctx(), "tcp4", "app.example.com:"+port)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("tcp4: %v", err)
	}
	conn.Close()
	if got := rec.calls(); !slices.Equal(got, []string{"203.0.113.8:" + port}) {
		t.Fatalf("tcp4 dialled %v, want the IPv4 address only", got)
	}
}

// S1: the context net/http passes to DialContext carries the values of the

	}
}

// S4: dialling the pinned address keeps HTTPS verified against the name of
// the request. A name the certificate does not hold fails verification.
func TestPinnedDialHTTPSVerifiesName(t *testing.T) {
	g, rec := dialGate(t)
	srv := httptest.NewTLSServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { _, _ = w.Write([]byte("verified")) }))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	_, port, _ := net.SplitHostPort(srv.Listener.Addr().String())
	rec.route("203.0.113.7:"+port, srv.Listener.Addr().String())
	// httptest's certificate holds example.com.
	for _, host := range []string{"example.com", "other.example"} {
		g.pin(host, atoiPort(t, port), "203.0.113.7")
		g.res.set(host, "203.0.113.7")
	}
	client := pinnedClient(true)
	client.Transport.(*http.Transport).TLSClientConfig = &tls.Config{RootCAs: srv.Client().Transport.(*http.Transport).TLSClientConfig.RootCAs}
	if body, err := get(g.ctx(), client, "https://example.com:"+port+"/"); err != nil || body != "verified" {
		t.Fatalf("https by the pinned address: %q, %v", body, err)
	}
	_, err := get(g.ctx(), client, "https://other.example:"+port+"/")
	var verr *tls.CertificateVerificationError
	if !errors.As(err, &verr) {
		t.Fatalf("a name the certificate does not hold: %v, want a verification error", err)
	}
	if got := rec.calls(); !slices.Equal(got, []string{"203.0.113.7:" + port, "203.0.113.7:" + port}) {
		t.Fatalf("dialled %v", got)
	}
}

// S6: with keep-alive off (as Norma sets it on a transport with a dialer, and
// the custom tool on its own), a second fetch of one client dials again: a pin
// changed in between applies to it.
func TestPinnedDialNoReuseAcrossCalls(t *testing.T) {
	g, rec := dialGate(t)
	srv, _, port := pinnedServer(t, "again")
	rec.route("203.0.113.7:"+port, srv.Listener.Addr().String())
	rec.route("203.0.113.8:"+port, srv.Listener.Addr().String())
	p := atoiPort(t, port)
	g.pin("app.example.com", p, "203.0.113.7")
	g.res.set("app.example.com", "203.0.113.7")
	client := pinnedClient(true)
	u := "http://app.example.com:" + port + "/"
	if _, err := get(g.ctx(), client, u); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	g.store.revoke("app.example.com", p)
	g.pin("app.example.com", p, "203.0.113.8")
	g.res.set("app.example.com", "203.0.113.8")
	if _, err := get(g.ctx(), client, u); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := rec.calls(); !slices.Equal(got, []string{"203.0.113.7:" + port, "203.0.113.8:" + port}) {
		t.Fatalf("dialled %v, want a new dial under the new pin", got)
	}
}

// S5: the redirected request keeps the original request's context, so the
// hop's redirect check and the hop's dial read the same target scope.
func TestRedirectContextCarriesScope(t *testing.T) {
	g, rec := dialGate(t)
	final, finalHits, finalKey := hopServer(t, "")
	start, _, startKey := hopServer(t, final.URL+"/final")
	for _, key := range []string{startKey, finalKey} {
		host, port, _ := net.SplitHostPort(key)
		g.pin(host, atoiPort(t, port), host)
	}
	var hopScope TargetScope
	var hopOK bool
	client := pinnedClient(true)
	policy := client.CheckRedirect
	client.CheckRedirect = func(req *http.Request, via []*http.Request) error {
		hopScope, hopOK = TargetScopeFromContext(req.Context())
		return policy(req, via)
	}
	if body, err := get(g.ctx(), client, start.URL+"/start"); err != nil || body != "hop-reached" || finalHits.Load() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("redirect: %q, %v", body, err)
	}
	if !hopOK || hopScope.TaskID != g.scope.TaskID || hopScope.Interceptor != g.ic {
		t.Fatalf("hop context scope = %+v (%v), want the scope of the call", hopScope, hopOK)
	}
	if got := rec.calls(); !slices.Equal(got, []string{startKey, finalKey}) {
		t.Fatalf("dialled %v, want the origin then the hop through the pinned path", got)
	}
}

// D-2: a request raised while the upstream proxy is set says the platform does
// not bind the connection.
func TestNameOnlyReasonSaysConnectionNotBound(t *testing.T) {
	scope := TargetScope{TaskID: "7"}
	r := target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7")
	const sentence = "This approval is name-only. The platform does not bind the connection to these addresses."
	if got := targetReason(scope, r, nil, true); !strings.Contains(got, sentence) {
		t.Fatalf("name-only reason = %q", got)
	}
	if got := targetReason(scope, r, nil, false); strings.Contains(got, "does not bind") {
		t.Fatalf("reason without the upstream proxy = %q", got)
	}
}

// D-2: the first-use row of an unmarked pin used while the upstream proxy is

func TestPinUsedRecordsEffectiveNameOnly(t *testing.T) {

		t.Fatalf("rows %v, target %+v; want a name-only first use", got, g.store.logged[0].Audit.Targets[0])
	}
}

package intercept

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"strings"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// metadataAddrs are instance-metadata addresses that lie outside the link-local
// ranges and would otherwise pass as private or public unicast.
var metadataAddrs = []netip.Addr{
	netip.MustParseAddr("fd00:ec2::254"),   // AWS IMDS over IPv6
	netip.MustParseAddr("100.100.100.200"), // Alibaba Cloud
}

// ValidateExemptionHost checks the host of an entry an operator adds to the
// target-gate exemption list. host is expected in normalised form.
//
// An exemption on a name is resolved at check time and is void when the name
// resolves to a private, loopback, link-local or unspecified address. An IP
// literal is never resolved, so that rule cannot protect it and the literal is
// checked here instead. A private unicast address is allowed: an internal
// service the operator names on purpose (10.0.0.5:8080). Loopback, link-local
// (169.254.0.0/16 holds the cloud metadata address 169.254.169.254; fe80::/10),
// unspecified and multicast addresses are never accepted, nor are the metadata
// addresses outside the link-local ranges. A host that is not an IP literal
// passes: names are the void rule's business.
func ValidateExemptionHost(host string) error {
	addr, err := netip.ParseAddr(host)
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	addr = addr.Unmap().WithZone("")
	kind := ""
	switch {
	case addr.IsLoopback():
		kind = "a loopback"
	case addr.IsUnspecified():
		kind = "the unspecified"
	case addr.IsLinkLocalUnicast():
		kind = "a link-local (metadata range)"
	case addr.IsMulticast():
		kind = "a multicast"
	}
	for _, m := range metadataAddrs {
		if addr == m {
			kind = "an instance-metadata"
		}
	}
	if kind != "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("%s is %s address and can never be exempt from target approval", host, kind)
	}
	return nil
}

// ErrInvalidExemption is wrapped by the reason an exemption entry is refused.
var ErrInvalidExemption = errors.New("invalid exemption")

// SetDerivedExemptions installs the function that lists the endpoints of the
// platform's own services, as URLs or host:port: the LLM gateways, the search
// backend in use and the platform proxies. They are exempt because the
// configuration names them. They are computed at check time and never stored,
// so they follow the configuration and cannot be set through the exemption
// list. A derived exemption is never resolved and never voided: an internal
// relay for a platform service is a normal deployment.
func (i *Interceptor) SetDerivedExemptions(f func() []string) {
	i.mu.Lock()
	i.derivedExempt = f
	i.mu.Unlock()
}

// proxyPorts are the ports net/http dials for a proxy URL without one, for the
// schemes schemePorts has no default for.
var proxyPorts = map[string]int{"socks5": 1080, "socks5h": 1080}

// DerivedExemptions returns the exemptions derived from the configuration, as
// exact host and port. An endpoint without a port gets the one net/http dials
// (the scheme's default, 1080 for socks5); one with neither is not listed.
func (i *Interceptor) DerivedExemptions() []db.TargetExemption {
	i.mu.RLock()
	f := i.derivedExempt
	i.mu.RUnlock()
	out := []db.TargetExemption{}
	if f == nil {
		return out
	}
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, raw := range f() {
		t, ok := NormalizeTarget(raw)
		if scheme, _, found := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(raw), "://"); ok && found && t.Port == 0 {
			t.Port = proxyPorts[strings.ToLower(scheme)]
		}
		if !ok || t.Port == 0 || t.Kind == TargetCIDR || seen[db.TargetKey(t.Host, t.Port)] {
			continue
		}
		seen[db.TargetKey(t.Host, t.Port)] = true
		out = append(out, db.TargetExemption{Host: t.Host, Port: t.Port})
	}
	return out
}

// Exemptions returns the stored exemption list and its digest.
func (i *Interceptor) Exemptions() ([]db.TargetExemption, string, error) {
	return i.targets.Exemptions()
}

// SetExemptions validates list and stores it as the exemption list; the change
// is appended to the exemption log with changedBy. An entry is an exact host
// and port: a name or an IP literal, no wildcard, no suffix, no CIDR, and a
// port between 1 and 65535. It returns the list as stored (hosts normalised,
// duplicates dropped) and its digest.
func (i *Interceptor) SetExemptions(list []db.TargetExemption, changedBy string) ([]db.TargetExemption, string, error) {
	out := []db.TargetExemption{}
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, e := range list {
		kind, host, ok := normalizeHost(e.Host, true)
		switch {
		case !ok || kind == TargetCIDR || kind == TargetDomain && !validHostname(host):
			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %q is not an exact host name or IP address", ErrInvalidExemption, e.Host)
		case e.Port < 1 || e.Port > 65535:
			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %s needs a port between 1 and 65535, got %d", ErrInvalidExemption, host, e.Port)
		}
		if err := ValidateExemptionHost(host); err != nil {
			return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("%w: %v", ErrInvalidExemption, err)
		}
		if key := db.TargetKey(host, e.Port); !seen[key] {
			seen[key] = true
			out = append(out, db.TargetExemption{Host: host, Port: e.Port, Note: strings.TrimSpace(e.Note)})
		}
	}
	raw, err := json.Marshal(out)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", err
	}
	digest := digestInput(raw)
	if err := i.db.ReplaceTargetExemptions(out, changedBy, digest); err != nil {
		return nil, "", err
	}
	return out, digest, nil
}

// exemptions is the exemption list as one gated call sees it.
type exemptions struct {
	derived map[string]bool // db.TargetKey(host, port)
	stored  map[string]bool
	digest  string // of the stored list
}

func (i *Interceptor) loadExemptions() (exemptions, error) {
	stored, digest, err := i.targets.Exemptions()
	if err != nil {
		return exemptions{}, err
	}
	ex := exemptions{derived: map[string]bool{}, stored: map[string]bool{}, digest: digest}
	for _, e := range i.DerivedExemptions() {
		ex.derived[db.TargetKey(e.Host, e.Port)] = true
	}
	for _, e := range stored {
		ex.stored[db.TargetKey(e.Host, e.Port)] = true
	}
	return ex, nil
}

// voidsExemption reports whether one resolved address voids a stored
// exemption on a name: a private address (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, the
// unique local range fc00::/7), or one that is never exempt as a literal
// either (loopback, link-local 169.254.0.0/16 and fe80::/10, unspecified,
// multicast, instance metadata). One such address is enough.
func voidsExemption(ip string) bool {
	a, err := netip.ParseAddr(ip)
	if err != nil {
		return true
	}
	a = a.Unmap().WithZone("")
	return a.IsPrivate() || ValidateExemptionHost(a.String()) != nil
}

package intercept

import (
	"slices"
	"testing"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// An operator may exempt a private unicast IP literal, never a loopback,
// link-local (cloud metadata), unspecified or multicast one.
func TestValidateExemptionHost(t *testing.T) {
	for _, host := range []string{
		"10.0.0.5", "172.16.0.1", "192.168.1.1", "fd00::1", // private unicast
		"203.0.113.7", "2001:db8::1", // public
		"pypi.org", "internal.corp", "localhost", // names: the void rule's business
	} {
		if err := ValidateExemptionHost(host); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s refused: %v", host, err)
		}
	}
	for _, host := range []string{
		"169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2", "169.254.0.1", "fe80::1", "fe80::1%eth0", // link-local, metadata
		"::ffff:169.254.169.254",           // the same address, IPv4-mapped
		"fd00:ec2::254", "100.100.100.200", // metadata outside link-local
		"127.0.0.1", "127.8.8.8", "::1", "::ffff:127.0.0.1", // loopback
		"0.0.0.0", "::", // unspecified
		"224.0.0.1", "239.255.255.250", "ff02::1", "ff05::2", // multicast
	} {
		if err := ValidateExemptionHost(host); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s accepted, want it refused", host)
		}
	}
}

// A proxy endpoint configured without a port is exempt on the port net/http
// dials for it (OPEN-9): the scheme's default, 1080 for socks5. An endpoint
// with no port and no known scheme is not listed.
func TestDerivedExemptionsDefaultProxyPort(t *testing.T) {
	ic := New(nil)
	ic.SetDerivedExemptions(func() []string {
		return []string{"socks5://egress.example.net", "SOCKS5H://dns.example.net", "http://proxy.example.net", "https://gw.example.net", "bare.example.net", "socks5://set.example.net:9050"}
	})
	want := []db.TargetExemption{
		{Host: "egress.example.net", Port: 1080}, {Host: "dns.example.net", Port: 1080}, {Host: "proxy.example.net", Port: 80},
		{Host: "gw.example.net", Port: 443}, {Host: "set.example.net", Port: 9050},
	}
	if got := ic.DerivedExemptions(); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("derived exemptions = %+v, want %+v", got, want)
	}
}

package intercept

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/netip"
	"regexp"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// executeExtraTool is the tool that runs a deferred tool (every MCP tool, and
// the custom tools flagged deferred). The hook sees it, never the inner name.
const executeExtraTool = "ExecuteExtraTool"

// noTargetTools are the tools whose input names no network target: the search
// tool (its input is a query), the file and session tools, and the platform's
// domain tools, which read and write the platform's own records. Every name
// that is not listed here is scanned, so a tool added later is gated by default.
var noTargetTools = toolSet(
	"web_search",
	"Read", "Write", "Edit", "MultiEdit", "LS", "Glob", "Grep",
	"TodoWrite", "sleep", "TaskOutput", "TaskStop", "TaskList",
	// exploration graph, assets, findings, goals (agent.ToolSet)
	"graph_overview", "list_findings", "list_facts", "node_detail", "expand_digest",
	"get_worker_output", "get_worker_trace", "search_all_worker_traces",
	"add_hint", "add_intent", "steer_work", "kill_work",
	"set_goals", "set_constraints", "list_goals", "prove_goal", "goal_met",
	"insert_assets", "add_company_scope", "add_task_scope", "list_assets",
	"list_untested_assets", "list_companies", "report_finding", "record_fact",
	"save_task_credential", "list_task_credentials", "ingest_bbot", "ingest_scan_output", "record_coverage",
	// cross-task orchestration, findings and retests (server)
	"list_tasks", "list_llm_profiles", "spawn_task", "pause_task", "get_task_graph",
	"list_task_findings", "add_task_hint", "get_task_worker_trace",
	"list_task_worker_traces", "search_task_worker_traces", "get_task_node_detail",
	"update_finding_report", "get_finding_traffic", "bind_finding_traffic",
	"get_finding_retest_context", "record_finding_retest_result",
	"delete_assets_by_host", "create_skill", "update_skill_file",
	// the operator runs the command, not the platform
	"ask_operator",
	// recorded traffic
	"traffic_search", "traffic_get", "traffic_blob",
)

func toolSet(names ...string) map[string]bool {
	m := make(map[string]bool, len(names))
	for _, n := range names {
		m[n] = true
	}
	return m
}

// ExtractTargets returns the network targets a tool call declares in its
// input, normalised and without duplicates, in order of appearance.
//
// WebFetch names its target exactly. The command tools are read with the
// command-string rules: URLs with a scheme, IP literals, IP:port, host:port and
// CIDR. A bare host name is not a target there, because a file name such as
// x.py is a valid host name. Every other tool that is not known to have no
// target has each string of its input read with the same rules. This is what
// the model declared: a command can hide its target, and the process resolves
// names on its own. The gate detects a declared target; it does not prevent an
// undeclared connection.
func ExtractTargets(toolName string, input []byte) []Target {
	return extractDeclared(toolName, input).targets
}

// extractDeclared reads what a tool call declares: its targets, as
// ExtractTargets returns them, and the URLs it writes, as written, for the URL
// block rules. A URL is kept only when it names a target.
func extractDeclared(toolName string, input []byte) targetList {
	if toolName == executeExtraTool {
		var in struct {
			ToolName string          `json:"tool_name"`
			Params   json.RawMessage `json:"params"`
		}
		if json.Unmarshal(input, &in) == nil && in.ToolName != "" && in.ToolName != executeExtraTool {
			toolName, input = in.ToolName, in.Params
		}
	}
	if noTargetTools[toolName] {
		return targetList{}
	}
	var out targetList
	switch toolName {
	case "WebFetch":
		u := declaredFields(input).URL
		if t, ok := NormalizeTarget(u); ok {
			out.add(t)
			out.urls = append(out.urls, strings.TrimSpace(u))
		}
	case "Bash", "shell_open", "Monitor":
		out.scan(declaredFields(input).Command)
	case "shell_send":
		out.scan(declaredFields(input).Text)
	default:
		out.scanStrings(input)
	}
	return out
}

// declaredInput holds the fields of the built-in tools that carry a target.
type declaredInput struct {
	URL     string `json:"url"`
	Command string `json:"command"`
	Text    string `json:"text"`
}

// declaredFields decodes the input into a struct, as the tools themselves do:
// a key matches whatever its case and the last duplicate wins. The gate
// therefore reads the value the tool will run, not another spelling of the key.
func declaredFields(input []byte) declaredInput {
	var in declaredInput
	_ = json.Unmarshal(input, &in) // a field of another type is skipped, the others are kept
	return in
}

type targetList struct {
	targets []Target
	seen    map[Target]bool
	urls    []string // the URLs that name a target, as written
}

func (l *targetList) add(t Target) {
	if l.seen[t] {
		return
	}
	if l.seen == nil {
		l.seen = map[Target]bool{}
	}
	l.seen[t] = true
	l.targets = append(l.targets, t)
}

// scanStrings reads every string of a JSON input, in document order. It walks
// the tokens instead of decoding into a map, so both values of a duplicated key
// are read: the gate cannot know which one the tool behind the call keeps.
func (l *targetList) scanStrings(input []byte) {
	dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(input))
	for {
		tok, err := dec.Token()
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		if s, ok := tok.(string); ok {
			l.scan(s)
		}
	}
}

// shellMeta are the characters that end a word for an unquoted shell.
const shellMeta = `|;&(){},\`

// urlHosts returns the readings of the authority of a URL found in a command.
// Whether the URL is quoted decides how its authority is read when a shell
// character sits in it: 'http://a.example;@b.example/' names b.example to the
// client, and without the quotes the shell ends the URL at a.example. A
// backslash is dropped by the shell and kept inside quotes. The gate cannot
// tell which applies, so it returns every reading and each one is a target.
func urlHosts(authority string) []string {
	host := func(s string) string {
		s = s[strings.LastIndexByte(s, '@')+1:]
		if i := strings.IndexAny(s, shellMeta); i >= 0 {
			s = s[:i]
		}
		return s
	}
	out := []string{host(authority)}
	if i := strings.IndexAny(authority, shellMeta); i >= 0 {
		out = append(out, host(authority[:i]), host(strings.ReplaceAll(authority, `\`, "")))
	}
	return out
}

var (
	// A URL with a scheme: the scheme, the authority, then the rest of the token.
	// The rest is consumed so that what a path or a query contains is not read
	// as a target.
	reURL = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)\b([a-z][a-z0-9+.\-]*://)([^\s/?#"'<>` + "`" + `]*)[^\s"'<>` + "`" + `]*`)
	// [IPv6] and [IPv6]:port.
	reBracketed = regexp.MustCompile(`\[([0-9A-Fa-f:.]+(?:%[\w.\-]+)?)\](?::(\d{1,5}))?`)
	// IPv4, IPv4:port and IPv4/len.
	reIPv4 = regexp.MustCompile(`\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{1,3}){3}(?:/\d{1,2}|:\d{1,5})?`)
	// IPv6 and IPv6/len: at least two colons, checked by the parser afterwards.
	reIPv6 = regexp.MustCompile(`[0-9A-Fa-f:.]*:[0-9A-Fa-f:.]*:[0-9A-Fa-f:.]*(?:%[\w.\-]+)?(?:/\d{1,3})?`)
	// name:port, for a name with a dot and an alphabetic last label, or localhost.
	// A single label is not read as a host: user:1234 and image:22 are not targets.
	reHostPort = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)(?:localhost|[a-z0-9_](?:[a-z0-9_\-]*[a-z0-9_])?(?:\.[a-z0-9_](?:[a-z0-9_\-]*[a-z0-9_])?)*\.[a-z][a-z0-9\-]*[a-z0-9]):\d{1,5}`)
)

// scan reads the targets of one string with the command-string rules. Each
// form is blanked once it is read, so a later rule never reads part of it again.
func (l *targetList) scan(s string) {
	if s == "" {
		return
	}
	b := []byte(s)
	blank := func(from, to int) {
		for i := from; i < to; i++ {
			b[i] = ' '
		}
	}
	each := func(re *regexp.Regexp, read func(m []int) bool) {
		for _, m := range re.FindAllSubmatchIndex(b, -1) {
			if read(m) {
				blank(m[0], m[1])
			}
		}
	}
	each(reURL, func(m []int) bool {
		scheme, found := string(b[m[2]:m[3]]), false
		for _, host := range urlHosts(string(b[m[4]:m[5]])) {
			// A host that is not a name ($HOST, a glob) is what the shell or the
			// client will make of it, which the gate cannot read.
			if t, ok := NormalizeTarget(scheme + host); ok && (t.Kind != TargetDomain || validHostname(t.Host)) {
				l.add(t)
				found = true
			}
		}
		if found {
			// The whole token, path and query included, from the original string.
			l.urls = append(l.urls, s[m[0]:m[1]])
		}
		// The scheme and what follows the authority are never read again. An
		// authority that named no host is: an address written in it still counts.
		blank(m[0], m[4])
		blank(m[5], m[1])
		return found
	})
	each(reBracketed, func(m []int) bool {
		a, err := netip.ParseAddr(string(b[m[2]:m[3]]))
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		t := Target{Kind: TargetIP, Host: a.Unmap().WithZone("").String()}
		if m[4] >= 0 {
			t.Port = validPort(string(b[m[4]:m[5]]))
		}
		l.add(t)
		return true
	})
	each(reIPv6, func(m []int) bool {
		start, end := m[0], m[1]
		if start > 0 && isWord(b[start-1]) || end < len(b) && (isWord(b[end]) || b[end] == ':') {
			return false
		}
		kind, host, ok := normalizeHost(string(b[start:end]), false)
		// "::" alone is punctuation (a slice, a scope operator), not an address.
		if !ok || kind == TargetDomain || host == "::" {
			return false
		}
		l.add(Target{Kind: kind, Host: host})
		return true
	})
	each(reIPv4, func(m []int) bool {
		start, end := m[0], m[1]
		if start > 0 && (isWord(b[start-1]) || b[start-1] == '.') {
			return false
		}
		// The address alone, when what follows it is not a port or a prefix length.
		addrEnd := start + bytes.IndexAny(b[start:end], "/:")
		if addrEnd < start {
			addrEnd = end
		}
		if !endsToken(b, end) {
			end = addrEnd
			if !endsToken(b, end) {
				return false
			}
		}
		a, err := netip.ParseAddr(string(b[start:addrEnd]))
		if err != nil {
			return false
		}
		t := Target{Kind: TargetIP, Host: a.String()}
		if end > addrEnd {
			switch suffix := string(b[addrEnd+1 : end]); b[addrEnd] {
			case '/':
				if p, err := netip.ParsePrefix(string(b[start:end])); err == nil {
					t = Target{Kind: TargetCIDR, Host: p.Masked().String()}
				}
			case ':':
				t.Port = validPort(suffix)
			}
		}
		l.add(t)
		return true
	})
	each(reHostPort, func(m []int) bool {
		start, end := m[0], m[1]
		// Not the tail of a longer word, a path or an address, and not the head of
		// a version number (name:1.25).
		if start > 0 && (isWord(b[start-1]) || strings.IndexByte(`.-/\`, b[start-1]) >= 0) {
			return false
		}
		if !endsToken(b, end) {
			return false
		}
		host, port, _ := strings.Cut(string(b[start:end]), ":")
		n := validPort(port)
		_, host, ok := normalizeHost(host, false)
		if n == 0 || !ok {
			return false
		}
		l.add(Target{Kind: TargetDomain, Host: host, Port: n})
		return true
	})
}

// endsToken reports whether the token that ends before b[i] really ends there:
// what follows is not a word character and not a dot that continues a name or
// a number.
func endsToken(b []byte, i int) bool {
	if i >= len(b) {
		return true
	}
	if isWord(b[i]) {
		return false
	}
	return b[i] != '.' || i+1 >= len(b) || !isWord(b[i+1])
}

func isWord(c byte) bool {
	return c >= 'a' && c <= 'z' || c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z' || c >= '0' && c <= '9' || c == '_'
}

// validPort returns the port s names, 0 when it is not one.
func validPort(s string) int {
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(s)
	if err != nil || n < 1 || n > 65535 {
		return 0
	}
	return n
}

=====================================================================
FILE: intercept/target_gate.go

package intercept

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// Block codes of the gate decision. Like the codes of a target request they
// are carried in the model-facing text of the blocked call. None of them opens
// an approval request.
const (
	// TargetResolveFailed: a name did not resolve, so there is no address to
	// compare with a pin or to show to a human.
	TargetResolveFailed = "TARGET_RESOLVE_FAILED"
	// TargetRuleBlocked: an asset block rule matches a target.
	TargetRuleBlocked = "TARGET_RULE_BLOCKED"
	// TargetTooMany: the call names more unpinned targets than one call may request.
	TargetTooMany = "TARGET_TOO_MANY"
)

// maxUnpinnedTargets is how many distinct targets without a covering pin one
// call may request approval for. Each approval is one click on one host.
const maxUnpinnedTargets = 5

// literalResolver is the resolver recorded for an IP literal or a CIDR: the
// address is what was written, nothing was resolved.
const literalResolver = "literal"

// targetStore is what the gate reads and writes. The database implements it.
type targetStore interface {
	// BlockRules returns the asset block rules that apply to the scope: the
	// global ones and, for a task, its own. Allow rules play no role in the gate.
	BlockRules(scope db.TargetScopeRef) ([]db.AssetInterceptRule, error)
	// ActivePins returns the active pins that may cover (host, port) in scope,
	// the pin on the exact port first.
	ActivePins(scope db.TargetScopeRef, host string, port int) ([]*db.TargetPin, error)
	// Exemptions returns the stored exemption list and its digest.
	Exemptions() ([]db.TargetExemption, string, error)
	// LogDecision records an outcome no human took.
	LogDecision(db.TargetDecision) error
}

type dbTargetStore struct{ d *db.DB }

func (s dbTargetStore) BlockRules(scope db.TargetScopeRef) ([]db.AssetInterceptRule, error) {
	rules, err := s.d.ListAssetInterceptRules()
	if err != nil || scope.TaskID == 0 {
		return rules, err
	}
	block, _, err := s.d.Assets().TaskInterceptRulesSplit(scope.TaskID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return append(rules, block...), nil
}

func (s dbTargetStore) ActivePins(scope db.TargetScopeRef, host string, port int) ([]*db.TargetPin, error) {
	return s.d.ActiveTargetPins(scope, host, port)
}

func (s dbTargetStore) Exemptions() ([]db.TargetExemption, string, error) {
	list, raw, err := s.d.TargetExemptions()
	if raw == "" {
		raw = "[]"
	}
	return list, digestInput([]byte(raw)), err
}

func (s dbTargetStore) LogDecision(r db.TargetDecision) error {
	_, err := s.d.LogTargetDecision(r)
	return err
}

// CheckTargets decides, for one tool call of a gated scope, whether every
// network target the call declares may be reached: extraction, asset block
// rules, exemptions, resolution and the pin lookup. It creates no approval
// request and never waits.
//
// A block is reported in the result (Code, Reason and the target that caused
// it) and logged as a decided row. Otherwise the returned requests are the
// targets no pin covers, each with the addresses a human has to read; the
// caller passes them to RequestTargets and checks again after the decisions.
// No request and no code means the call may run.
//
// With the gate off the call returns at once: nothing is extracted, resolved,
// read or written.
func (i *Interceptor) CheckTargets(ctx context.Context, scope TargetScope, toolName string, input []byte) ([]TargetRequest, TargetResult) {
	if scope.Enabled == nil || !scope.Enabled() {
		return nil, TargetResult{}
	}
	declared := extractDeclared(toolName, input)
	if len(declared.targets) == 0 {
		return nil, TargetResult{}
	}
	c := &targetCheck{i: i, ctx: ctx, scope: scope, tool: toolName, input: input, urls: declared.urls}
	return c.run(declared.targets)
}

// targetCheck is one run of the gate decision.
type targetCheck struct {
	i     *Interceptor
	ctx   context.Context
	scope TargetScope
	ref   db.TargetScopeRef
	tool  string
	input []byte
	urls  []string // the URLs the call declares, as written, for the URL block rules
	// redirectFrom is the origin (host:port) of a redirect hop; empty for a call.
	redirectFrom string
	// fresh makes every lookup skip the cache: the decision of a connection
	// (dialTarget) compares the answer it is about to dial.
	fresh bool
	// checked is what the run decided about each target, read by dialTarget.
	checked []*checkedTarget
}

// What let a target pass, recorded in checkedTarget.cover.
const (
	coverDerived  = "derived"   // an exemption derived from the configuration
	coverStored   = "stored"    // a stored exemption that holds
	coverPin      = "pin"       // a pin that holds every resolved address
	coverNameOnly = "name_only" // a pin that is name-only for this call
)

// checkedTarget is one target of the call and what the gate learned about it.
type checkedTarget struct {
	Target
	ips        []string // resolved addresses; the literal itself for an IP or a CIDR
	resolver   string
	resolvedAt time.Time
	err        error // the name did not resolve
	exemptVoid bool
	cover      string // what let the target pass; empty when nothing did
}

func (t Target) String() string {
	return targetName(TargetRequest{Host: t.Host, Port: t.Port})
}

func (t *checkedTarget) audit(outcome string) db.InterceptTarget {
	return db.InterceptTarget{Host: t.Host, Port: t.Port, Kind: t.Kind, ResolvedIPs: t.ips,
		Resolver: t.resolver, ResolvedAt: t.resolvedAt, Outcome: outcome, ExemptVoid: t.exemptVoid}
}

func (c *targetCheck) run(targets []Target) ([]TargetRequest, TargetResult) {
	i := c.i
	var err error
	if c.ref, err = c.scope.ref(); err != nil {
		return nil, TargetResult{Code: TargetGateUnavailable, Host: targets[0].Host, Port: targets[0].Port, Reason: err.Error()}
	}
	first := &checkedTarget{Target: targets[0]}
	rules, err := i.targets.BlockRules(c.ref)
	if err != nil {
		return c.block(TargetGateUnavailable, "gate_unavailable", first, "the asset rules could not be read: "+err.Error())
	}
	ex, err := i.loadExemptions()
	if err != nil {
		return c.block(TargetGateUnavailable, "gate_unavailable", first, "the exemption list could not be read: "+err.Error())
	}

	// Block rules come first, and an exempt or pinned host that matches one is
	// blocked. They are matched on what the call declares before anything is
	// resolved: a hit there costs no lookup, for any target of the call.
	//
	// URL rules (exact_url, fuzzy_url) are matched once per decision, on the
	// URLs as the call writes them. That is a known limit: exact_url compares
	// the string as written, so another case, encoding (%2F), a trailing slash,
	// an added query or /./ does not match, and fuzzy_url is evaded by encoding
	// the substring; a command can also build its URL at run time. To keep an
	// agent away from a host, a domain, IP or CIDR rule is the one to write.
	if rule, u, hit := db.MatchAssetInterceptRules(rules, nil, nil, c.urls); hit {
		ct := &checkedTarget{Target: targets[0]}
		if t, ok := NormalizeTarget(u); ok {
			ct.Target = t
		}
		return c.block(TargetRuleBlocked, "rule_blocked", ct, fmt.Sprintf("%s is blocked by an asset rule. %s", u, rule.Reason()))
	}
	// Then the declared form of every target: the name as written, the IP
	// literal, the range.
	checked := make([]*checkedTarget, len(targets))
	c.checked = checked
	for n, t := range targets {
		ct := &checkedTarget{Target: t}
		checked[n] = ct
		if t.Kind != TargetDomain {
			ct.ips, ct.resolver, ct.resolvedAt = []string{t.Host}, literalResolver, time.Now().UTC()
		}
		if rule, hit := blockRule(rules, ct); hit {
			return c.block(TargetRuleBlocked, "rule_blocked", ct, fmt.Sprintf("%s is blocked by an asset rule. %s", t, rule.Reason()))
		}
	}
	// Only then are the names resolved, and the rules matched on the addresses.
	// A name the configuration exempts is never resolved.
	for _, ct := range checked {
		if ct.Kind != TargetDomain || ex.derived[db.TargetKey(ct.Host, ct.Port)] {
			continue
		}
		c.resolve(ct, c.fresh)
		if rule, hit := blockRule(rules, ct); hit {
			return c.block(TargetRuleBlocked, "rule_blocked", ct, fmt.Sprintf("%s is blocked by an asset rule. %s", ct.Target, rule.Reason()))
		}
	}

	i.mu.RLock()
	proxied := i.upstreamProxy
	i.mu.RUnlock()
	// Behind the upstream proxy the proxy chooses the address it connects to, so
	// every pin is name-only for this call, whatever the pin row says: the proxy
	// can be turned on after a pin was approved.
	nameOnly := proxied != nil && proxied()

	var unpinned []TargetRequest
	var uses []func()
	for _, ct := range checked {
		key := db.TargetKey(ct.Host, ct.Port)
		if ex.derived[key] {
			ct.cover = coverDerived
			uses = append(uses, func() { c.exemptUsed(ct, ex.digest) })
			continue
		}
		if ex.stored[key] {
			if exemptionHolds(ct) {
				ct.cover = coverStored
				uses = append(uses, func() { c.exemptUsed(ct, ex.digest) })
				continue
			}
			// A void exemption is not a block: the target goes on like any other.
			ct.exemptVoid = true
		}
		if ct.err != nil {
			return c.block(TargetResolveFailed, "resolve_failed", ct, c.resolveFailure(ct))
		}
		pins, err := i.targets.ActivePins(c.ref, ct.Host, ct.Port)
		if err != nil {
			return c.block(TargetGateUnavailable, "gate_unavailable", ct, "the pins could not be read: "+err.Error())
		}
		pin := coveringPin(pins, ct.ips, nameOnly)
		if pin == nil && ct.Kind == TargetDomain && !c.fresh {
			// A request is about to be raised: the addresses a human reads and
			// pins are resolved now, never taken from the cache. A fresh run
			// already has them.
			if c.resolve(ct, true); ct.err != nil {
				return c.block(TargetResolveFailed, "resolve_failed", ct, c.resolveFailure(ct))
			}
			if rule, hit := blockRule(rules, ct); hit {
				return c.block(TargetRuleBlocked, "rule_blocked", ct, fmt.Sprintf("%s is blocked by an asset rule. %s", ct.Target, rule.Reason()))
			}
			pin = coveringPin(pins, ct.ips, nameOnly)
		}
		if pin != nil {
			ct.cover = coverPin
			if nameOnly || pin.NameOnlyEffective {
				ct.cover = coverNameOnly
			}
			uses = append(uses, func() { c.pinUsed(ct, pin, nameOnly) })
			continue
		}
		req := TargetRequest{Host: ct.Host, Port: ct.Port, Kind: ct.Kind, ResolvedIPs: ct.ips,
			Resolver: ct.resolver, ResolvedAt: ct.resolvedAt, Reason: "no_pin", ExemptVoid: ct.exemptVoid}
		if len(pins) > 0 {
			// The request is raised on the key of the pin that exists (the one on
			// the exact port when both exist), so that an approval extends that pin.
			req.Port, req.Reason, req.Pin = pins[0].Port, "new_ip", pins[0]
		}
		if !hasRequest(unpinned, req) {
			unpinned = append(unpinned, req)
		}
	}
	if len(unpinned) > maxUnpinnedTargets {
		names := make([]string, len(unpinned))
		audit := make([]db.InterceptTarget, len(unpinned))
		for n, r := range unpinned {
			names[n] = targetName(r)
			audit[n] = db.InterceptTarget{Host: r.Host, Port: r.Port, Kind: r.Kind, ResolvedIPs: r.ResolvedIPs,
				Resolver: r.Resolver, ResolvedAt: r.ResolvedAt, Reason: r.Reason, Outcome: "too_many"}
		}
		reason := fmt.Sprintf("this call names %d targets that are not approved (%s); at most %d are requested per call",
			len(unpinned), strings.Join(names, ", "), maxUnpinnedTargets)
		c.log("denied", TargetTooMany+": "+reason, "", audit...)
		return nil, TargetResult{Code: TargetTooMany, Host: unpinned[0].Host, Port: unpinned[0].Port, Reason: reason}
	}
	if len(unpinned) == 0 {
		// The call passes: record what let it pass, once per process.
		for _, use := range uses {
			use()
		}
	}
	return unpinned, TargetResult{}
}

// resolve fills the addresses of a name. fresh skips the cache.
func (c *targetCheck) resolve(ct *checkedTarget, fresh bool) {
	ct.resolver = c.i.resolve.name()
	res, err := c.i.resolve.lookup(c.ctx, ct.Host, fresh)
	ct.ips, ct.resolvedAt, ct.err = res.ips, res.at, err
}

func (c *targetCheck) resolveFailure(ct *checkedTarget) string {
	reason := fmt.Sprintf("the platform could not resolve %s (%v)", ct.Host, ct.err)
	if pins, err := c.i.targets.ActivePins(c.ref, ct.Host, ct.Port); err == nil && len(pins) > 0 {
		reason += fmt.Sprintf(", so it cannot compare the address with the approved pin (v%d: %s)",
			pins[0].Version, strings.Join(pins[0].PinnedIPs, ", "))
	}
	return reason
}

// block logs a blocked call as a decided row and returns the block.
func (c *targetCheck) block(code, outcome string, ct *checkedTarget, reason string) ([]TargetRequest, TargetResult) {
	c.log("denied", code+": "+reason, "", ct.audit(outcome))
	return nil, TargetResult{Code: code, Host: ct.Host, Port: ct.Port, Reason: reason}
}

// log writes one decided row of the gate. Best effort: a failed write never
// changes the outcome of the call.
func (c *targetCheck) log(status, reason, configDigest string, targets ...db.InterceptTarget) {
	action := "deny"
	if status == "allowed" {
		action = "allow"
	}
	audit := auditFor(c.ctx, Decision{Action: action, Message: reason, ConfigDigest: configDigest}, c.input, status)
	if status == "allowed" {
		// The row records that a pin or an exemption was used, not this one call.
		audit.ExecutionStatus = "unknown"
	}
	for n := range targets {
		targets[n].RedirectFrom = c.redirectFrom
	}
	audit.Targets = targets
	_, agentName := taskInfoFromCtx(c.ctx)
	_ = c.i.targets.LogDecision(db.TargetDecision{Scope: c.ref, AgentName: agentName, ToolName: c.tool,
		ToolInput: c.input, Status: status, Reason: reason, Audit: audit})
}

// exemptUsed logs the first call of this process that passes through an
// exemption, per scope, host, port and list digest.
func (c *targetCheck) exemptUsed(ct *checkedTarget, digest string) {
	key := "exempt|" + c.scope.scopeName() + "|" + db.TargetKey(ct.Host, ct.Port) + "|" + digest
	if _, seen := c.i.firstUse.LoadOrStore(key, true); seen {
		return
	}
	c.log("allowed", fmt.Sprintf("Target %s is exempt from target approval for %s.", ct.Target, c.scope.scopeName()),
		digest, ct.audit("exempt"))
}

// pinUsed logs the first call of this process that a pin version covers.
// nameOnly is whether the upstream proxy made every pin name-only for the call:
// the row records the effective state, not only the pin's mark.
func (c *targetCheck) pinUsed(ct *checkedTarget, pin *db.TargetPin, nameOnly bool) {
	if _, seen := c.i.firstUse.LoadOrStore(fmt.Sprintf("pin|%d", pin.ID), true); seen {
		return
	}
	t := ct.audit("pin_match")
	t.PinID, t.PinVersion, t.PinnedIPs, t.NameOnlyEffective = pin.ID, pin.Version, pin.PinnedIPs, pin.NameOnlyEffective || nameOnly
	c.log("allowed", fmt.Sprintf("Target %s is covered by pin v%d of %s.", ct.Target, pin.Version, c.scope.scopeName()), "", t)
}

// blockRule matches the asset block rules against a target: its name, and its
// addresses. A range is matched as written and by its network address. URL
// rules are not matched here: run matches them once, on the declared URLs.
func blockRule(rules []db.AssetInterceptRule, ct *checkedTarget) (db.AssetInterceptRule, bool) {
	var domains []string
	ips := ct.ips
	switch ct.Kind {
	case TargetDomain:
		domains = []string{ct.Host}
	case TargetCIDR:
		if p, err := netip.ParsePrefix(ct.Host); err == nil {
			ips = []string{ct.Host, p.Addr().String()}
		}
	}
	rule, _, hit := db.MatchAssetInterceptRules(rules, domains, ips, nil)
	return rule, hit
}

// exemptionHolds reports whether the stored exemption on a target applies. On a
// name it is void when the name does not resolve or one of its addresses is
// private, loopback or otherwise local. An IP literal is not resolved; it holds
// unless it is an address that can never be exempt.
func exemptionHolds(ct *checkedTarget) bool {
	if ct.Kind == TargetIP {
		return ValidateExemptionHost(ct.Host) == nil
	}
	if ct.Kind != TargetDomain || ct.err != nil || len(ct.ips) == 0 {
		return false
	}
	for _, ip := range ct.ips {
		if voidsExemption(ip) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

// coveringPin returns the pin that covers the resolved addresses: the first
// candidate that is name-only, or that holds every address. The address sets
// of two pins are never merged.
func coveringPin(pins []*db.TargetPin, resolved []string, nameOnly bool) *db.TargetPin {
	for _, p := range pins {
		if nameOnly || p.NameOnlyEffective || subset(resolved, p.PinnedIPs) {
			return p
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func hasRequest(list []TargetRequest, r TargetRequest) bool {
	for _, x := range list {
		if x.Host == r.Host && x.Port == r.Port {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

package intercept

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// The tests below run the gate against PostgreSQL: the real store, the real
// request and decide path, and a fake resolver.

// pgGate returns an interceptor on d with a fake resolver.
func pgGate(t *testing.T, d *db.DB) (*Interceptor, *fakeResolver) {
	t.Helper()
	ic, res := New(d), newFakeResolver()
	ic.SetResolver(res)
	return ic, res
}

// storedExemptions sets the exemption list for one test and puts the previous
// one back afterwards. The list is global, so these tests do not run in parallel.
func storedExemptions(t *testing.T, d *db.DB, list ...db.TargetExemption) {
	t.Helper()
	previous, _, err := d.TargetExemptions()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := d.ReplaceTargetExemptions(list, "test", "test"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = d.ReplaceTargetExemptions(previous, "test", "test") })
}

// decidedRows returns the rows of the gate that no human decided, oldest first.
func decidedRows(t *testing.T, d *db.DB, scope TargetScope) []*db.InterceptDetail {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := d.Query(`SELECT id FROM intercept_pending
WHERE COALESCE(task_id,'')=$1 AND COALESCE(conversation_id,0)=$2 AND decision_source='target' AND decided_by='system' AND target_key IS NULL ORDER BY id`,
		scope.TaskID, scope.ConversationID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var ids []int64
	for rows.Next() {
		var id int64
		if err := rows.Scan(&id); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	rows.Close()
	out := make([]*db.InterceptDetail, len(ids))
	for n, id := range ids {
		if out[n], err = d.GetInterceptDetail(id); err != nil || out[n] == nil || out[n].Audit == nil || len(out[n].Audit.Targets) == 0 {
			t.Fatalf("row %d: detail=%+v err=%v", id, out[n], err)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func fetchInput(url string) []byte { return []byte(`{"url":"` + url + `"}`) }

// approveAll approves every open request of scope.
func approveAll(t *testing.T, d *db.DB, ic *Interceptor, scope TargetScope) {
	t.Helper()
	ids := openRows(t, d, scope)
	if len(ids) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("no open request to approve")
	}
	for _, id := range ids {
		if err := ic.Decide(id, true, "HIVE", "192.0.2.1"); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
}

// pin opens the request for an unpinned WebFetch target and approves it.
func pinURL(t *testing.T, d *db.DB, ic *Interceptor, scope TargetScope, url string) {
	t.Helper()
	reqs, res := ic.CheckTargets(context.Background(), scope, "WebFetch", fetchInput(url))
	if res.Code != "" || len(reqs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%s: requests=%+v result=%+v, want one request", url, reqs, res)
	}
	done := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, reqs...)
	eventually(t, "the request row", func() bool { return len(openRows(t, d, scope)) == 1 })
	approveAll(t, d, ic, scope)
	if out := result(t, done); out.Code != "" {
		t.Fatalf("%s: approved request ended with %+v", url, out)
	}
}

func mustPass(t *testing.T, what string, ic *Interceptor, scope TargetScope, url string) {
	t.Helper()
	if reqs, res := ic.CheckTargets(context.Background(), scope, "WebFetch", fetchInput(url)); res.Code != "" || len(reqs) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%s: requests=%+v result=%+v, want the call to pass", what, reqs, res)
	}
}

func TestExemptionChangeIsLogged(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	original, _, err := ic.Exemptions()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = d.ReplaceTargetExemptions(original, "test", "test") })
	logged := func() []db.TargetExemptionChange {
		t.Helper()
		changes, err := d.ListTargetExemptionLog(100)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return changes
	}
	before := logged()

	first := []db.TargetExemption{{Host: "PyPI.org.", Port: 443, Note: " index "}, {Host: "10.0.0.5", Port: 8080}, {Host: "pypi.org", Port: 443, Note: "duplicate"}}
	stored, digest, err := ic.SetExemptions(first, "alice")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := []db.TargetExemption{{Host: "pypi.org", Port: 443, Note: "index"}, {Host: "10.0.0.5", Port: 8080}}
	if !slices.Equal(stored, want) {
		t.Fatalf("stored = %+v, want %+v (normalised, without the duplicate)", stored, want)
	}
	if list, got, err := ic.Exemptions(); err != nil || !slices.Equal(list, want) || got != digest || digest == "" {
		t.Fatalf("read back: list=%+v digest=%q (want %q) err=%v", list, got, digest, err)
	}
	second, digest2, err := ic.SetExemptions(nil, "bob")
	if err != nil || len(second) != 0 || digest2 == digest {
		t.Fatalf("empty list: stored=%+v digest=%q err=%v", second, digest2, err)
	}

	// A refused list changes nothing and logs nothing.
	if _, _, err := ic.SetExemptions([]db.TargetExemption{{Host: "169.254.169.254", Port: 80}}, "mallory"); !errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidExemption) {
		t.Fatalf("metadata address: err=%v, want it refused", err)
	}
	if list, got, err := ic.Exemptions(); err != nil || len(list) != 0 || got != digest2 {
		t.Fatalf("after the refused change: list=%+v digest=%q err=%v", list, got, err)
	}

	changes := logged()
	if len(changes) != len(before)+2 {
		t.Fatalf("%d log rows added, want 2", len(changes)-len(before))
	}
	newest, older := changes[0], changes[1]
	var olderBefore, olderAfter, newestBefore, newestAfter []db.TargetExemption
	for raw, into := range map[*json.RawMessage]*[]db.TargetExemption{&older.Before: &olderBefore, &older.After: &olderAfter, &newest.Before: &newestBefore, &newest.After: &newestAfter} {
		if len(*raw) > 0 {
			if err := json.Unmarshal(*raw, into); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}
	}
	if older.ChangedBy != "alice" || older.Digest != digest || !slices.Equal(olderBefore, original) || !slices.Equal(olderAfter, want) || older.ChangedAt.IsZero() {
		t.Fatalf("first change = %+v", older)
	}
	if newest.ChangedBy != "bob" || newest.Digest != digest2 || !slices.Equal(newestBefore, want) || len(newestAfter) != 0 || string(newest.After) != "[]" {
		t.Fatalf("second change = %+v", newest)
	}
}

// The first call that passes through an exemption is logged once per scope,
// host, port and list digest, and per process.
func TestExemptionFirstUseLoggedOnce(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	storedExemptions(t, d, db.TargetExemption{Host: "pypi.org", Port: 443})
	ic, res := pgGate(t, d)
	ic.SetDerivedExemptions(func() []string { return []string{"https://llm.example.net/v1"} })
	res.set("pypi.org", "151.101.0.223")
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	_, digest, err := ic.Exemptions()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	for n := 0; n < 3; n++ {
		mustPass(t, "stored exemption", ic, scope, "https://pypi.org/simple/")
		mustPass(t, "derived exemption", ic, scope, "https://llm.example.net/v1/models")
	}
	rows := decidedRows(t, d, scope)
	if len(rows) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("%d first-use rows, want one per exemption", len(rows))
	}
	for n, host := range []string{"pypi.org", "llm.example.net"} {
		row := rows[n]
		target := row.Audit.Targets[0]
		if row.Status != "allowed" || row.DecidedBy != "system" || row.DecisionSource != "target" || row.ToolName != "WebFetch" ||
			target.Host != host || target.Port != 443 || target.Outcome != "exempt" || row.Audit.ConfigDigest != digest || row.DecidedAt == nil {
			t.Fatalf("first-use row %d = %+v audit=%+v", n, row.InterceptApprovalRow, row.Audit)
		}
	}
	if n := len(pins(t, d, scope)) + len(openRows(t, d, scope)); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("an exemption created %d pins or requests", n)
	}

	// Another scope logs its own first use.
	other := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	mustPass(t, "other task", ic, other, "https://pypi.org/simple/")
	if n := len(decidedRows(t, d, other)); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("other task: %d first-use rows, want 1", n)
	}
	// A changed list has another digest: the use is logged again.
	storedExemptions(t, d, db.TargetExemption{Host: "pypi.org", Port: 443}, db.TargetExemption{Host: "files.pythonhosted.org", Port: 443})
	mustPass(t, "changed list", ic, scope, "https://pypi.org/simple/")
	mustPass(t, "changed list, again", ic, scope, "https://pypi.org/simple/")
	if n := len(decidedRows(t, d, scope)); n != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("after the list change: %d rows, want 3", n)
	}
	// Another process (a second interceptor on the same database) logs again.
	second, res2 := pgGate(t, d)
	res2.set("pypi.org", "151.101.0.223")
	scope.Interceptor = second
	mustPass(t, "second process", second, scope, "https://pypi.org/simple/")
	if n := len(decidedRows(t, d, scope)); n != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("second process: %d rows, want 4", n)
	}
}

// The seeded package sources are stored entries like the ones an operator
// adds: the void rule applies to them.
func TestSeededExemptionIsVoidOnPrivateAddress(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	stored, _, err := d.TargetExemptions()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !slices.ContainsFunc(stored, func(e db.TargetExemption) bool { return e.Host == "pypi.org" && e.Port == 443 }) {
		t.Skipf("the stored list no longer holds the seeded pypi.org:443 entry: %+v", stored)
	}
	ic, res := pgGate(t, d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	res.set("pypi.org", "151.101.0.223")
	mustPass(t, "seeded entry, public address", ic, scope, "https://pypi.org/simple/")

	second, res2 := pgGate(t, d)
	res2.set("pypi.org", "151.101.0.223", "10.0.0.5")
	reqs, out := second.CheckTargets(context.Background(), scope, "WebFetch", fetchInput("https://pypi.org/simple/"))
	if out.Code != "" || len(reqs) != 1 || !reqs[0].ExemptVoid {
		t.Fatalf("seeded entry, one private address: requests=%+v result=%+v, want a request with a void exemption", reqs, out)
	}
	// The request row records that the exemption was void.
	done := request(context.Background(), second, scope, nil, reqs...)
	id := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
	detail, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(id)
	if err != nil || detail == nil || !detail.Audit.Targets[0].ExemptVoid {
		t.Fatalf("request row audit = %+v err=%v, want exempt_void", detail, err)
	}
	if err := second.Decide(id, false, "HIVE", "192.0.2.1"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if out := result(t, done); out.Code != TargetDenied {
		t.Fatalf("denied request ended with %+v", out)
	}
}

// Task allow rules play no role in the gate: they neither satisfy it nor
// restrict it. Block rules, global and of the task, always win.
func TestAllowRuleDoesNotSatisfyGate(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic, res := pgGate(t, d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	ref := scope.dbRef(t)
	res.set("app.example.com", "203.0.113.7")
	res.set("other.example.com", "203.0.113.9")
	rule := func(action, kind, pattern string) {
		t.Helper()
		if _, err := d.Assets().CreateTaskInterceptRule(ref.TaskID, action, kind, pattern, "target gate test", true); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}

	// An allow rule on the host does not replace the approval.
	rule("allow", "exact_domain", "app.example.com")
	reqs, out := ic.CheckTargets(context.Background(), scope, "WebFetch", fetchInput("https://app.example.com/"))
	if out.Code != "" || len(reqs) != 1 || reqs[0].Reason != "no_pin" {
		t.Fatalf("allow rule on the host: requests=%+v result=%+v, want a request", reqs, out)
	}
	// A pinned host outside the allow list still passes: the whitelist is not
	// applied at dispatch.
	pinURL(t, d, ic, scope, "https://other.example.com/")
	mustPass(t, "pinned host outside the allow list", ic, scope, "https://other.example.com/")

	// A block rule of the task beats the pin.
	rule("block", "exact_ip", "203.0.113.9")
	if reqs, out := ic.CheckTargets(context.Background(), scope, "WebFetch", fetchInput("https://other.example.com/")); out.Code != TargetRuleBlocked || len(reqs) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("task block rule: requests=%+v result=%+v", reqs, out)
	}
	// It is the task's rule: another task is not blocked by it.
	other := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	if reqs, out := ic.CheckTargets(context.Background(), other, "WebFetch", fetchInput("https://other.example.com/")); out.Code != "" || len(reqs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("other task: requests=%+v result=%+v, want a request", reqs, out)
	}
	// A global block rule applies to every scope.
	global, err := d.CreateAssetInterceptRule("exact_domain", "app.example.com", "target gate test", true)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = d.DeleteAssetInterceptRule(global.ID) })
	for name, s := range map[string]TargetScope{"task": scope, "other task": other} {
		if reqs, out := ic.CheckTargets(context.Background(), s, "WebFetch", fetchInput("https://app.example.com/")); out.Code != TargetRuleBlocked || len(reqs) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("global block rule, %s: requests=%+v result=%+v", name, reqs, out)
		}
	}
	// Each block is a decided row; none opened a request.
	rows := decidedRows(t, d, scope)
	blocks := 0
	for _, row := range rows {
		if row.Audit.Targets[0].Outcome == "rule_blocked" {
			blocks++
			if row.Status != "denied" || !strings.HasPrefix(row.Reason, TargetRuleBlocked+": ") || row.Audit.ExecutionStatus != "not_executed" {
				t.Fatalf("block row = %+v audit=%+v", row.InterceptApprovalRow, row.Audit)
			}
		}
	}
	if blocks != 2 || len(openRows(t, d, scope)) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%d block rows and %d open requests, want 2 and 0", blocks, len(openRows(t, d, scope)))
	}
}

// The proxy can be turned on between the approval and a later call. The pin
// row then still says name_only_effective = false, and the gate treats it as
// name-only at call time: a changed address neither blocks nor asks.
func TestProxyTurnedOnAfterApprovalMakesPinNameOnly(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic, res := pgGate(t, d)
	proxied := false
	ic.SetUpstreamProxyCheck(func() bool { return proxied })
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	res.set("app.example.com", "203.0.113.7")
	pinURL(t, d, ic, scope, "https://app.example.com/")
	approved := pins(t, d, scope)
	if len(approved) != 1 || approved[0].NameOnlyEffective || !slices.Equal(approved[0].PinnedIPs, []string{"203.0.113.7"}) {
		t.Fatalf("pins = %+v, want one pin that is not name-only", approved)
	}
	requestRows := allRows(t, d, scope)

	// global_proxy is set, and the name answers another address. A new
	// interceptor stands for a later call that has nothing cached.
	proxied = true
	res.set("app.example.com", "198.51.100.99")
	ic.SetResolver(res)
	mustPass(t, "changed address behind the proxy", ic, scope, "https://app.example.com/")

	if n := len(openRows(t, d, scope)); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%d open requests, want none", n)
	}
	if n := allRows(t, d, scope); n != requestRows {
		t.Fatalf("%d request rows, want %d: the call opened a request", n, requestRows)
	}
	after := pins(t, d, scope)
	if len(after) != 1 || after[0].ID != approved[0].ID || after[0].NameOnlyEffective || after[0].Status != db.TargetPinActive ||
		!slices.Equal(after[0].PinnedIPs, []string{"203.0.113.7"}) {
		t.Fatalf("pins after the call = %+v, want the same row, unchanged", after)
	}
	// The use of the pin is on record, with the address the platform saw.
	rows := decidedRows(t, d, scope)
	last := rows[len(rows)-1]
	if target := last.Audit.Targets[0]; last.Status != "allowed" || target.Outcome != "pin_match" || target.PinID != approved[0].ID ||
		!slices.Equal(target.ResolvedIPs, []string{"198.51.100.99"}) {
		t.Fatalf("last row = %+v audit=%+v", last.InterceptApprovalRow, last.Audit)
	}

	// Control: with the proxy off the same call asks.
	proxied = false
	if reqs, out := ic.CheckTargets(context.Background(), scope, "WebFetch", fetchInput("https://app.example.com/")); out.Code != "" || len(reqs) != 1 || reqs[0].Reason != "new_ip" {
		t.Fatalf("proxy off: requests=%+v result=%+v, want a new_ip request", reqs, out)
	}
}

// An approval never pins zero addresses: not on a first approval, and not when
// the key already has a pin with addresses.
func TestApprovalNeverPinsEmptyAddressList(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic, res := pgGate(t, d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	ref := scope.dbRef(t)

	// RequestTargets refuses to open such a request.
	for _, ips := range [][]string{nil, {}} {
		out := ic.RequestTargets(context.Background(), scope, "WebFetch", webFetchInput,
			[]TargetRequest{{Host: "app.example.com", Port: 443, Kind: TargetDomain, ResolvedIPs: ips, Reason: "no_pin"}}, nil)
		if out.Code != TargetResolveFailed || out.PendingID != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("request with %v: %+v, want %s", ips, out, TargetResolveFailed)
		}
	}
	// One empty target refuses the whole call, before any row is written.
	out := ic.RequestTargets(context.Background(), scope, "Bash", []byte(`{"command":"x"}`),
		[]TargetRequest{target("a.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7"), target("b.example.com", 443)}, nil)
	if out.Code != TargetResolveFailed || out.Host != "b.example.com" || allRows(t, d, scope) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("mixed call: %+v with %d rows, want %s and no row", out, allRows(t, d, scope), TargetResolveFailed)
	}

	// A row that reached the table without an address cannot be approved.
	open := func(host string, ips []string) int64 {
		t.Helper()
		id, created, err := d.FindOrCreateTargetRequest(db.TargetRequest{Scope: ref, Host: host, Port: 443, ToolName: "WebFetch", Reason: "test",
			Audit: &db.InterceptAudit{Targets: []db.InterceptTarget{{Host: host, Port: 443, ResolvedIPs: ips, Outcome: "requested"}}}})
		if err != nil || !created {
			t.Fatalf("open request: id=%d created=%v err=%v", id, created, err)
		}
		return id
	}
	for _, ips := range [][]string{nil, {}, {""}} {
		id := open("empty.example.com", ips)
		if err := ic.Decide(id, true, "HIVE", "192.0.2.1"); !errors.Is(err, db.ErrTargetPinEmpty) {
			t.Fatalf("approve %v: err=%v, want ErrTargetPinEmpty", ips, err)
		}
		if row, err := d.GetInterceptPending(id); err != nil || row == nil || row.Status != "pending" {
			t.Fatalf("refused approval: row=%+v err=%v, want it still pending", row, err)
		}
		if n := len(pins(t, d, scope)); n != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("%d pins after a refused approval, want none", n)
		}
		// The request can still be denied.
		if err := ic.Decide(id, false, "HIVE", "192.0.2.1"); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}

	// With a pin on the key: the approval is refused all the same, and the
	// pin is neither superseded nor re-issued with its old addresses.
	res.set("app.example.com", "203.0.113.7")
	pinURL(t, d, ic, scope, "https://app.example.com/")
	id := open("app.example.com", nil)
	if err := ic.Decide(id, true, "HIVE", "192.0.2.1"); !errors.Is(err, db.ErrTargetPinEmpty) {
		t.Fatalf("approve an empty new_ip request: err=%v, want ErrTargetPinEmpty", err)
	}
	if after := pins(t, d, scope); len(after) != 1 || after[0].Version != 1 || after[0].Status != db.TargetPinActive || !slices.Equal(after[0].PinnedIPs, []string{"203.0.113.7"}) {
		t.Fatalf("pins = %+v, want version 1 untouched", after)
	}

	// A name that stops resolving opens no request, so there is nothing to approve.
	res.errs["app.example.com"] = errors.New("no such host")
	ic.SetResolver(res)
	if reqs, out := ic.CheckTargets(context.Background(), scope, "WebFetch", fetchInput("https://app.example.com:8443/")); out.Code != TargetResolveFailed || len(reqs) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unresolvable name: requests=%+v result=%+v", reqs, out)
	}
}

// A block is logged for a conversation as it is for a task, on the
// conversation's own rows.
func TestTargetBlockIsLoggedForConversation(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic, res := pgGate(t, d)
	conv, err := d.CreateConversation("auto", "target gate block", nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = d.DeleteConversation(conv.ID)
		_, _ = d.Exec(`DELETE FROM target_pins WHERE conversation_id=$1`, conv.ID)
	})
	scope := TargetScope{ConversationID: conv.ID, Enabled: func() bool { return true }, WaitBound: time.Minute, Interceptor: ic}
	res.errs["app.example.com"] = errors.New("no such host")
	ctx := WithCall(WithConvID(context.Background(), conv.ID), "WebFetch", fetchInput("https://app.example.com/"))
	if reqs, out := ic.CheckTargets(ctx, scope, "WebFetch", fetchInput("https://app.example.com/")); out.Code != TargetResolveFailed || len(reqs) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("requests=%+v result=%+v", reqs, out)
	}
	rows := decidedRows(t, d, scope)
	if len(rows) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d rows, want 1", len(rows))
	}
	row := rows[0]
	if row.Status != "denied" || row.ConversationID == nil || *row.ConversationID != conv.ID || row.TaskID != nil ||
		row.Audit.Targets[0].Outcome != "resolve_failed" || row.Audit.InputDigest == "" {
		t.Fatalf("row = %+v audit=%+v", row.InterceptApprovalRow, row.Audit)
	}
}
