package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// The health columns must reflect the outcome of every connect attempt and
// transition cleanly down -> ok, so the UI badge and the mcp_status tool can
// show operators why a server's tools are missing (#38).
func TestMCPHealthStateTransitions(t *testing.T) {
	s, _, _ := trafficEvidenceServer(t)
	pg := s.m.pg

	row := &db.MCPServer{Name: "health-test", Transport: "http", URL: "http://127.0.0.1:1/mcp", Enabled: true}
	id, err := pg.SaveMCP(row)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = pg.DeleteMCP(id) })

	found := listMCPByName(t, pg, "health-test")
	if found.LastConnectAt != nil || found.LastConnectOK != nil || found.LastConnectErr != nil {
		t.Fatalf("fresh server should have no health state, got %+v", found)
	}

	if err := pg.UpdateMCPHealth(id, false, "connect: no route to host"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	found = listMCPByName(t, pg, "health-test")
	if found.LastConnectOK == nil || *found.LastConnectOK {
		t.Fatal("expected last_connect_ok = false after a failed connect")
	}
	if found.LastConnectErr == nil || !strings.Contains(*found.LastConnectErr, "no route") {
		t.Fatalf("expected the failure reason, got %+v", found.LastConnectErr)
	}

	if err := pg.UpdateMCPHealth(id, true, ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	found = listMCPByName(t, pg, "health-test")
	if found.LastConnectOK == nil || !*found.LastConnectOK {
		t.Fatal("expected last_connect_ok = true after a successful connect")
	}
	if found.LastConnectErr != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected the error cleared on success, got %q", *found.LastConnectErr)
	}
}

func listMCPByName(t *testing.T, pg *db.DB, name string) *db.MCPServer {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := pg.ListMCP()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, r := range rows {
		if r.Name == name {
			return r
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("server %s not found", name)
	return nil
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/mcphttp"
	"github.com/Autumn-27/norma/mcp"
	actool "github.com/Autumn-27/norma/tool"
)

// mcpClient is the shared surface of a connected MCP server (stdio, Streamable HTTP,
// or legacy SSE),
// so tools/list and cleanup are handled uniformly regardless of transport.
type mcpClient interface {
	Tools(context.Context) ([]actool.CoreTool, error)
	Close() error
}

// connectMCP dials one MCP server per its transport. Callers must Close the client.
func connectMCP(ctx context.Context, m *db.MCPServer) (mcpClient, error) {
	switch m.Transport {
	case "stdio":
		if m.Command == "" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("stdio transport is missing a command")
		}
		return mcp.NewStdioClient(ctx, m.Name, m.Command, jsonStrMap(m.Env), jsonStrSlice(m.Args)...)
	case "http":
		if m.URL == "" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("http transport is missing a URL")
		}
		// env map doubles as HTTP headers (e.g. Authorization).
		return mcphttp.New(ctx, m.Name, m.URL, jsonStrMap(m.Env), m.Insecure, m.TimeoutSeconds)
	case "sse":
		if m.URL == "" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("sse transport is missing a URL")
		}
		return mcphttp.NewSSE(ctx, m.Name, m.URL, jsonStrMap(m.Env), m.Insecure)
	default:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown transport %q", m.Transport)
	}
}

// discoverAndCacheMCP connects to one MCP, lists its tools, and persists the tool
// names to mcp_tools_cache so the UI shows them without a live connection.
func (s *Server) discoverAndCacheMCP(ctx context.Context, m *db.MCPServer) error {
	cl, err := connectMCP(ctx, m)
	if err != nil {
		_ = s.m.pg.UpdateMCPHealth(m.ID, false, err.Error())
		return err
	}
	defer cl.Close()
	ts, err := cl.Tools(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		_ = s.m.pg.UpdateMCPHealth(m.ID, false, err.Error())
		return err
	}
	_ = s.m.pg.UpdateMCPHealth(m.ID, true, "")
	tools := make([]db.MCPTool, 0, len(ts))
	for _, t := range ts {
		tools = append(tools, db.MCPTool{Name: t.Name(), Description: t.Description()})
	}
	if err := s.m.pg.SaveMCPTools(m.ID, tools); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	log.Printf("[mcp] %s discovered %d tools and cached them", m.Name, len(tools))
	return nil
}

// discoverEmptyMCPsOnStartup fills the tool cache for any enabled MCP that has none
// yet (notably the seeded browser MCP on first run). Runs sequentially in one
// goroutine so we never spawn many stdio servers (npx) at once, and never blocks
// startup. Best-effort: a failure leaves the cache empty to retry next start.
func (s *Server) discoverEmptyMCPsOnStartup() {
	servers, err := s.m.pg.ListMCP()
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("[mcp] startup auto-discovery: failed to read the list: %v", err)
		return
	}
	for _, m := range servers {
		if !m.Enabled || len(m.Tools) > 0 {
			continue
		}
		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(s.ctx, 90*time.Second)
		if err := s.discoverAndCacheMCP(ctx, m); err != nil {
			log.Printf("[mcp] startup auto-discovery of %s failed: %v", m.Name, err)
		}
		cancel()
	}
}

package server

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"
)

// TestMgmtAPI exercises the PostgreSQL-backed management API through the real mux.
func TestMgmtAPI(t *testing.T) {
	m, err := NewManager(t.TempDir(), "")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("database unavailable (%v) — skipping management API test", err)
	}
	if m.pg == nil {
		t.Skip("postgres unavailable — skipping management API test")
	}
	// New starts the notifier and task-archive workers on context.Background();
	// closing the pool stops them from claiming later tests' digest batches
	// and archive jobs.
	defer m.Close()
	td := t.TempDir()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	s := New(ctx, m, td, td, td)
	defer stopTestServer(t, s, cancel)
	h := s.Handler()
	tok, err := signJWT(s.jwtKey)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("sign jwt: %v", err)
	}

	do := func(method, path string, body any) (int, map[string]any) {
		var r *http.Request
		if body != nil {
			b, _ := json.Marshal(body)
			r = httptest.NewRequest(method, path, bytes.NewReader(b))
		} else {
			r = httptest.NewRequest(method, path, nil)
		}
		r.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+tok)
		rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
		h.ServeHTTP(rec, r)
		var out map[string]any
		json.Unmarshal(rec.Body.Bytes(), &out)
		return rec.Code, out
	}

	// agents list — must include at least the seeded builtins
	code, out := do("GET", "/api/agents", nil)
	if code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("GET agents: %d", code)
	}
	if ags, _ := out["agents"].([]any); len(ags) < 5 {
		t.Fatalf("want >=5 agents (seeded builtins), got %d", len(ags))
	}

	// invalid template var → 400 (catalog whitelist)
	code, out = do("PUT", "/api/agents/planner/prompt", map[string]string{"template": "hi {{.Nope}}"})
	if code != 400 {
		t.Fatalf("bad var should be 400, got %d (%v)", code, out)
	}

	// valid template using seeded catalog vars → 200
	code, _ = do("PUT", "/api/agents/planner/prompt", map[string]string{"template": "You are the planner. Goal: {{.Goal}}, summary {{.AssetSummary}}"})
	if code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("valid prompt save: %d", code)
	}

	// preview renders with catalog examples
	code, out = do("POST", "/api/agents/planner/prompt/preview", map[string]any{})
	if code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("preview: %d", code)
	}
	if rendered, _ := out["rendered"].(string); rendered == "" || rendered == "You are the planner. Goal: {{.Goal}}, summary {{.AssetSummary}}" {
		t.Fatalf("preview did not substitute: %q", out["rendered"])
	}

	// mcp create → visible to planner → resource-side sees planner → delete clears it
	// Remove any leftover from prior run to keep the test idempotent.
	m.pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM mcp_servers WHERE name = 't-itest'`)
	code, out = do("POST", "/api/mcp", map[string]any{"name": "t-itest", "transport": "stdio", "command": "x", "enabled": true})
	if code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("create mcp: %d", code)
	}
	mid := int64(out["id"].(float64))

	ag, _ := m.pg.GetAgentByKey("planner")
	code, _ = do("PUT", "/api/agents/planner/visibility", map[string]any{"mcp": []int64{mid}, "skill": []int64{}})
	if code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("set visibility: %d", code)
	}
	code, out = do("GET", "/api/visibility/mcp/"+itoaTest(mid), nil)
	if code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("resource visibility: %d", code)
	}
	if agents, _ := out["agents"].([]any); len(agents) != 1 || agents[0].(string) != itoaTest(ag.ID) {
		t.Fatalf("resource-side should list planner, got %v", out["agents"])
	}

	// cleanup
	do("DELETE", "/api/mcp/"+itoaTest(mid), nil)
	m.pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM agent_prompts WHERE agent_id=$1`, ag.ID)
	m.pg.Exec(`UPDATE agents SET current_prompt_id=NULL WHERE id=$1`, ag.ID)
}

func itoaTest(n int64) string {
	b := []byte{}
	if n == 0 {
		return "0"
	}
	for n > 0 {
		b = append([]byte{byte('0' + n%10)}, b...)
		n /= 10
	}
	return string(b)
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/notify"
)

// Global setting keys (stored in the settings key-value table, no dedicated table needed).
const (
	// settingNotifyEnabled is the master switch for delivery. Default on: it exists
	// as a one-shot kill switch during maintenance, not as the enable condition for
	// the feature — the real enable condition is "whether any channel is configured".
	settingNotifyEnabled = "notify_enabled"
	// settingNotifyPublicBaseURL is the externally reachable address used to build
	// detail back-links for vulnerabilities (e.g. https://hive.example.com). If left
	// empty, messages carry no back-link button. There is no reusable external-address
	// setting in the project, so a new one is added here.
	settingNotifyPublicBaseURL = "notify_public_base_url"
	// settingNotifyDigestMinutes is the digest-mode period (minutes).
	settingNotifyDigestMinutes = "notify_digest_interval_min"
	// settingNotifySummaryMaxRunes is how many characters the summary of a single
	// push is cut to, and settingNotifyAssetsMaxShown how many asset names a
	// message lists. 0 means no truncation; unset means the notify package
	// defaults (120 / 3).
	settingNotifySummaryMaxRunes = "notify_summary_max_runes"
	settingNotifyAssetsMaxShown  = "notify_assets_max_shown"
)

const (
	// notifyTick is the delivery engine's polling interval. 3 seconds is the upper
	// bound of this engine's realtimeness, and also the main source of latency
	// between "vulnerability persisted" and "message arrives at the IM".
	notifyTick = 3 * time.Second
	// notifyLease is the lease duration when claiming deliveries. It must be
	// significantly longer than the worst-case duration of a single delivery
	// (the notify package's HTTP client timeout is 15 seconds), otherwise the
	// same row could be delivered by two dispatchers at the same time.
	notifyLease = 3 * time.Minute
	// notifyFanOutPerTick limits the number of events fanned out per tick, so that
	// enabling a channel for the first time does not expand the entire historical
	// backlog into delivery tasks in one go.
	notifyFanOutPerTick = 200
	// notifyDefaultDigestMinutes is the default digest period.
	notifyDefaultDigestMinutes = 30
	// notifySummaryMaxRunesCap / notifyAssetsMaxShownCap are the upper bounds the
	// settings API accepts for the two render limits.
	notifySummaryMaxRunesCap = 4000
	notifyAssetsMaxShownCap  = 50
	// notifyUnlimitedBurstPerTick is the per-tick delivery cap when a channel has
	// no rate limit configured. It exists to prevent "one channel configured as
	// unlimited + a single scan finding thousands of vulnerabilities" from dragging
	// a single tick into a long blocking loop.
	notifyUnlimitedBurstPerTick = 50
	// notifyMaxSendsPerChannelPerTick is the maximum number of deliveries per tick
	// for a single channel.
	//
	// This cap is derived backwards from the **lease duration**: claiming marks rows
	// with a lease (notifyLease = 3 minutes); if one tick serially delivers so many
	// rows that the worst-case duration exceeds the lease, the lease on the later
	// rows expires before they are even sent. Within a single process this is
	// harmless (Run is a single serial goroutine, ticks never re-enter), but with
	// **two processes on the same database**, the peer will reclaim rows whose
	// leases expired and resend them, double-increment attempts, and mark them
	// failed while the original process is still delivering.
	//
	// Value: 3-minute lease / 30-second per-send timeout = 6, which **consumes the
	// lease exactly** with zero headroom, so it cannot be used; 5 leaves a 30-second
	// margin on a 150-second worst case. This relationship is pinned down by
	// TestNotifyTickBudgetFitsWithinLease — changing any of notifyLease,
	// notifySendTimeout, or this value will fail that assertion.
	notifyMaxSendsPerChannelPerTick = 5
	// notifySendTimeout is the timeout for a single delivery. It also determines
	// the value of the constant above; the two multiplied together must not exceed
	// notifyLease, see TestNotifyTickBudgetFitsWithinLease.
	notifySendTimeout = 30 * time.Second
)

// notifyBackoff is the backoff sequence for failed-delivery retries, indexed by
// the number of attempts already made. 3 chances (including the first attempt)
// correspond to db.MaxNotifyAttempts; the two must be changed together.
var notifyBackoff = []time.Duration{
	time.Second,
	5 * time.Second,
	30 * time.Second,
}

// Notifier is the delivery engine for vulnerability notifications.
//
// It runs as an independent goroutine alongside the Scheduler (see server.New).
// It deliberately does not reuse the Scheduler's tick: delivery's realtimeness
// requirement (3 seconds) differs from the trigger's business cadence, and their
// failures must not affect each other — a stuck delivery must not impact agent
// triggering.
type Notifier struct {
	s  *Server
	pg *db.DB

	// mu guards buckets. The number of channels is small and contention is low,
	// so a single mutex is enough; a finer-grained structure is not worth it.
	mu      sync.Mutex
	buckets map[int64]*notifyBucket
}

// notifyBucket is the token bucket for a single channel.
//
// A token bucket is used instead of a sliding window of "count then reset each
// minute", because the latter has terrible boundary effects: sending the full 20
// messages at the end of a window and another 20 right after means 40 messages in
// one second from the platform's perspective, which gets rate-limited; a token
// bucket refills at a constant rate and inherently avoids such bursts.
type notifyBucket struct {
	tokens   float64
	lastFill time.Time
}

func newNotifier(s *Server) *Notifier {
	return &Notifier{s: s, pg: s.m.pg, buckets: map[int64]*notifyBucket{}}
}

// Run loops until ctx ends. Started once by server.New.
func (n *Notifier) Run(ctx context.Context) {
	if n.pg == nil {
		return
	}
	t := time.NewTicker(notifyTick)
	defer t.Stop()
	for {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return
		case <-t.C:
			n.step(ctx)
		}
	}
}

// step runs one round: first fan out new events, then deliver due tasks.
//
// Failure of any step only logs and never interrupts the loop — a failure in the
// notification system must never escalate into a process-level problem. Every
// tick is independent, and the next round will naturally retry.
func (n *Notifier) step(ctx context.Context) {
	if !n.enabled() {
		return
	}
	if _, _, err := n.pg.FanOutPendingEvents(ctx, notifyFanOutPerTick); err != nil {
		log.Printf("[notify] failed to fan out events: %v", err)
		return
	}
	channels, err := n.pg.ListNotificationChannels(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("[notify] failed to read channels: %v", err)
		return
	}
	baseURL := n.publicBaseURL()
	for _, ch := range channels {
		if !ch.IsEnabled() {
			continue
		}
		// The token bucket is metered in **messages** (equivalent to HTTP requests),
		// not vulnerabilities. In realtime mode the two are the same (one message per
		// vulnerability); in digest mode a whole batch of vulnerabilities becomes one
		// message, so it consumes only one token.
		//
		// Both modes ask the token bucket first and then claim within that allowance —
		// the order must not be reversed, otherwise deliveries blocked by rate limiting
		// would already have consumed retry attempts.
		now := time.Now()
		if ch.Mode == db.NotifyModeDigest {
			tokens, claimLimit := digestTickPlan()
			if n.takeTokens(ch.ID, ch.RatePerMin, tokens, now) <= 0 {
				continue
			}
			n.stepDigest(ctx, ch, claimLimit, baseURL)
			continue
		}
		allow := n.takeTokens(ch.ID, ch.RatePerMin, notifyMaxSendsPerChannelPerTick, now)
		if allow <= 0 {
			continue
		}
		n.stepRealtime(ctx, ch, allow, baseURL)
	}
}

// digestTickPlan returns the token consumption and batch-size upper bound for a
// digest channel in this tick.
//
// The two return values are **two different dimensions**, which is exactly why
// this is a separate function:
//
//   - tokens is the number of messages. A batch of vulnerabilities becomes one
//     message and one HTTP request, so it is always 1. rate_per_min therefore
//     still applies to digests (at most this many digest messages per minute).
//   - claimLimit is how many vulnerabilities a batch may hold at most. It is
//     bounded only by memory and is unrelated to the request budget.
//
// A previous version, in order to make rate_per_min apply to digests, passed the
// per-tick request budget (notifyMaxSendsPerChannelPerTick, derived backwards
// from the lease) directly as the batch size. The consequence was that a channel
// with rate_per_min=20 only refilled 1 token in a 3-second tick, so every digest
// message carried just 1 vulnerability — the digest degenerated into "realtime
// delivery with digest wording", readers received a stream of "1 new vulnerability
// in the last 30 minutes", and db.MaxDigestBatchSize was never reachable.
//
// This symptom is hard to catch in end-to-end tests (existing cases all pass a
// large enough limit to stepDigest manually, bypassing the allowance calculation
// in step), so the decision is pinned down here directly by
// TestDigestTickPlanDecouplesBatchSizeFromSendBudget.
func digestTickPlan() (tokens, claimLimit int) {
	return 1, db.MaxDigestBatchSize
}

// stepRealtime claims and delivers a channel's realtime tasks, one message per
// vulnerability.
func (n *Notifier) stepRealtime(ctx context.Context, ch *db.NotificationChannel, allow int, baseURL string) {
	deliveries, err := n.pg.ClaimRealtimeDeliveries(ctx, ch.ID, allow, notifyLease)
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("[notify] failed to claim realtime deliveries channel=%d: %v", ch.ID, err)
		return
	}
	if len(deliveries) == 0 {
		return
	}
	channel, cfg, ok := n.adapt(ch)
	if !ok {
		_ = n.pg.FailDeliveries(ctx, deliveryIDs(deliveries), fmt.Sprintf("channel type %q is not registered", ch.Kind))
		return
	}
	limits := notifyLimits(n.pg)
	for _, dl := range deliveries {
		msg, err := n.renderSingle(ctx, dl, baseURL, limits)
		if err != nil {
			// A render failure is a local data problem; retrying will not help.
			_ = n.pg.FailDeliveries(ctx, []int64{dl.ID}, err.Error())
			continue
		}
		n.send(ctx, channel, cfg, msg, []*db.NotificationDelivery{dl})
	}
}

// stepDigest aggregates a channel's pending deliveries into one message and sends
// it when the batch is due.
func (n *Notifier) stepDigest(ctx context.Context, ch *db.NotificationChannel, allow int, baseURL string) {
	window := n.digestInterval()
	due, err := n.pg.DigestBatchDue(ctx, ch.ID, window)
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("[notify] failed to check digest batch channel=%d: %v", ch.ID, err)
		return
	}
	if !due {
		return
	}
	deliveries, err := n.pg.ClaimDigestBatch(ctx, ch.ID, allow, notifyLease)
	if err != nil {
		log.Printf("[notify] failed to claim digest batch channel=%d: %v", ch.ID, err)
		return
	}
	if len(deliveries) == 0 {
		return
	}
	channel, cfg, ok := n.adapt(ch)
	if !ok {
		_ = n.pg.FailDeliveries(ctx, deliveryIDs(deliveries), fmt.Sprintf("channel type %q is not registered", ch.Kind))
		return
	}
	msg, included, err := n.renderBatch(ctx, deliveries, baseURL, int(window.Minutes()), notifyLimits(n.pg))
	if err != nil {
		_ = n.pg.FailDeliveries(ctx, deliveryIDs(deliveries), err.Error())
		return
	}
	// Deliveries whose snapshots were broken and did not make it into the message
	// must be marked failed explicitly. Otherwise they stay outside `included`,
	// entering neither the message nor the failure list — when the send succeeds,
	// the later batch marking would miss them, and they would stay in `sending`
	// forever until their leases expire and they get reclaimed over and over.
	if skipped := excludeDeliveries(deliveries, included); len(skipped) > 0 {
		reason := "event snapshot could not be parsed; this vulnerability cannot be rendered into a message"
		if fErr := n.pg.FailDeliveries(ctx, deliveryIDs(skipped), reason); fErr != nil {
			log.Printf("[notify] failed to mark broken-snapshot deliveries failed channel=%s ids=%v: %v", ch.Kind, deliveryIDs(skipped), fErr)
		}
		log.Printf("[notify] skipped %d deliveries with unparseable snapshots channel=%d", len(skipped), ch.ID)
	}
	// Only pass those that made it into the message to send: included[i]
	// corresponds strictly to msg.Items[i], and send relies on this correspondence
	// to attribute "the channel reported fitting the first K entries" to the
	// correct delivery rows.
	n.send(ctx, channel, cfg, msg, included)
}

// send delivers and transitions state according to the result.
//
// A batch of deliveries (possibly dozens in digest mode) shares a single send
// result: either delivered, or retried as a whole batch. There is no per-item
// retry — a digest message is one message, and resending part of it would corrupt
// the batch semantics.
//
// The only exception is **segmentation caused by the channel's length limit**: if
// the channel reports that only the first K entries actually fit, then from entry
// K+1 onward must be left for the next batch instead of being marked succeeded
// along with the rest. Otherwise the truncated vulnerabilities would be neither
// in the message nor in the failure list — they would disappear entirely.
func (n *Notifier) send(ctx context.Context, channel notify.Channel, cfg map[string]any, msg notify.Message, deliveries []*db.NotificationDelivery) {
	// Cap the duration of a single delivery so one stuck channel cannot hold up
	// all remaining channels in this round.
	sendCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, notifySendTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	delivered, err := channel.Send(sendCtx, cfg, msg)
	if err == nil && delivered > 0 {
		if delivered > len(deliveries) {
			// The channel cannot possibly report more delivered entries than there
			// are deliveries; if it does, the render layer miscounted. Treat it as
			// fully delivered and record the problem — better than corrupting the
			// records.
			log.Printf("[notify] channel reported %d delivered entries, more than the %d deliveries channel=%s; treating as fully delivered",
				delivered, len(deliveries), channel.Kind())
			delivered = len(deliveries)
		}
		sent, rest := deliveries[:delivered], deliveries[delivered:]
		if err := n.pg.MarkDeliveriesSent(ctx, deliveryIDs(sent)); err != nil {
			log.Printf("[notify] failed to mark as sent channel=%s ids=%v: %v", channel.Kind(), deliveryIDs(sent), err)
		}
		if len(rest) > 0 {
			// This message has reached the channel's length limit: the remainder
			// re-queues immediately and the next tick continues sending. Use
			// DeferDeliveries rather than RescheduleDeliveries — this is not a
			// failure and must not consume the retry budget (claiming already
			// optimistically incremented attempts by +1, which this will undo).
			if err := n.pg.DeferDeliveries(ctx, deliveryIDs(rest),
				fmt.Sprintf("this message reached the channel length limit; only the first %d entries were delivered, the rest are left for the next batch", delivered)); err != nil {
				log.Printf("[notify] failed to queue segmented continuation channel=%s ids=%v: %v", channel.Kind(), deliveryIDs(rest), err)
			}
		}
		return
	}
	if err == nil {
		// The channel neither reported an error nor said how many entries were
		// delivered. Treat it as a failure (with backoff), so this delivery is not
		// repeatedly claimed yet never marked.
		err = fmt.Errorf("channel did not report a delivered count (delivered=%d)", delivered)
	}

	// Failure handling is decided **per delivery**, not by the maximum attempt
	// count of the whole batch.
	//
	// A previous version failed the entire batch with
	// `if maxAttempts(deliveries) >= MaxNotifyAttempts`, but the attempt counts of
	// items in a batch differ: an old delivery already retried twice (attempts=2)
	// would drag a brand-new delivery (attempts=1) in the same batch into failed —
	// a new vulnerability permanently lost without using a single retry, the exact
	// opposite of the intent of "don't let old rows sink new rows".
	permanent := notify.IsPermanent(err)
	var failIDs, exhaustedIDs []int64
	byDelay := map[time.Duration][]int64{}
	for _, dl := range deliveries {
		switch {
		case permanent:
			failIDs = append(failIDs, dl.ID)
		case dl.Attempts >= db.MaxNotifyAttempts:
			exhaustedIDs = append(exhaustedIDs, dl.ID)
		default:
			delay := notifyBackoff[min(dl.Attempts, len(notifyBackoff)-1)]
			byDelay[delay] = append(byDelay[delay], dl.ID)
		}
	}

	if len(failIDs) > 0 {
		if fErr := n.pg.FailDeliveries(ctx, failIDs, err.Error()); fErr != nil {
			log.Printf("[notify] error marking failed state channel=%s ids=%v: %v", channel.Kind(), failIDs, fErr)
		}
	}
	if len(exhaustedIDs) > 0 {
		reason := fmt.Sprintf("still failing after %d retries: %s", db.MaxNotifyAttempts, err)
		if fErr := n.pg.FailDeliveries(ctx, exhaustedIDs, reason); fErr != nil {
			log.Printf("[notify] error marking failed state channel=%s ids=%v: %v", channel.Kind(), exhaustedIDs, fErr)
		}
	}
	// Reschedule grouped by delay: with only 3 backoff tiers the number of groups
	// is inherently small, so there is no need to issue a separate UPDATE per row
	// (which would turn a 500-row batch into 500 round trips).
	for delay, group := range byDelay {
		if rErr := n.pg.RescheduleDeliveries(ctx, group, delay, err.Error()); rErr != nil {
			log.Printf("[notify] failed to reschedule deliveries channel=%s ids=%v: %v", channel.Kind(), group, rErr)
		}
	}
	if len(failIDs)+len(exhaustedIDs) > 0 {
		log.Printf("[notify] delivery failed channel=%d kind=%s permanent=%d retries-exhausted=%d pending-retry=%d: %s",
			deliveries[0].ChannelID, channel.Kind(), len(failIDs), len(exhaustedIDs), len(byDelay), err)
	}
}

// excludeDeliveries returns the items in all that are not in keep (compared by
// pointer identity). Used to find deliveries that "did not make it into the
// message" — they must be handled explicitly and must not be left in a gray zone.
func excludeDeliveries(all, keep []*db.NotificationDelivery) []*db.NotificationDelivery {
	inKeep := make(map[*db.NotificationDelivery]bool, len(keep))
	for _, dl := range keep {
		inKeep[dl] = true
	}
	var out []*db.NotificationDelivery
	for _, dl := range all {
		if !inKeep[dl] {
			out = append(out, dl)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// adapt resolves the channel implementation and parses its configuration.
// Returning ok=false means the type is not registered; deliveries should be
// marked failed directly instead of retried indefinitely.
func (n *Notifier) adapt(ch *db.NotificationChannel) (notify.Channel, map[string]any, bool) {
	channel, ok := notify.Get(ch.Kind)
	if !ok {
		return nil, nil, false
	}
	var cfg map[string]any
	if len(ch.Config) > 0 {
		// When config parsing fails, fall back to an empty map: the channel's own
		// Validate will report "which field is missing", an error far more
		// actionable for the user than a JSON parse error.
		_ = json.Unmarshal(ch.Config, &cfg)
	}
	if cfg == nil {
		cfg = map[string]any{}
	}
	return channel, cfg, true
}

// renderSingle renders a single-vulnerability message.
func (n *Notifier) renderSingle(ctx context.Context, dl *db.NotificationDelivery, baseURL string, limits notify.Limits) (notify.Message, error) {
	snap, err := parseSnapshot(dl)
	if err != nil {
		return notify.Message{}, err
	}
	item, err := n.itemFor(ctx, snap, baseURL)
	if err != nil {
		return notify.Message{}, err
	}
	return notify.Message{Items: []notify.Item{item}, HomeURL: baseURL, Limits: &limits}, nil
}

// renderBatch renders a digest message. Snapshots are parsed one by one — a
// single broken one only skips that entry and must not sink the whole digest.
//
// The return value included corresponds **strictly one-to-one** with msg.Items
// (the i-th delivery ↔ the i-th item). This correspondence is a hard requirement:
// the caller marks the first K deliveries as sent based on "the channel reported
// fitting the first K entries". If a broken snapshot were skipped here without
// removing the skipped delivery from included, the indices would shift — a broken
// entry that should have failed would be marked sent, and a good entry would be
// misjudged as undelivered. The broken ones are marked failed explicitly by the
// caller, see stepDigest.
func (n *Notifier) renderBatch(ctx context.Context, deliveries []*db.NotificationDelivery, baseURL string, windowMinutes int, limits notify.Limits) (notify.Message, []*db.NotificationDelivery, error) {
	items := make([]notify.Item, 0, len(deliveries))
	included := make([]*db.NotificationDelivery, 0, len(deliveries))
	for _, dl := range deliveries {
		snap, err := parseSnapshot(dl)
		if err != nil {
			// A broken snapshot goes neither into the message nor into included —
			// handling it is the caller's responsibility (explicitly marking it
			// failed, rather than sneaking it through among the "sent" ones).
			log.Printf("[notify] skipping unparseable snapshot in digest batch delivery=%d: %v", dl.ID, err)
			continue
		}
		item, err := n.itemFor(ctx, snap, baseURL)
		if err != nil {
			return notify.Message{}, nil, err
		}
		items = append(items, item)
		included = append(included, dl)
	}
	if len(items) == 0 {
		return notify.Message{}, nil, fmt.Errorf("all %d deliveries in the digest batch failed to parse", len(deliveries))
	}
	return notify.Message{
		Items:         items,
		Batch:         true,
		WindowMinutes: windowMinutes,
		HomeURL:       baseURL,
		Limits:        &limits,
	}, included, nil
}

// itemFor renders an event snapshot into a notification item, also resolving
// asset names and the detail back-link.
func (n *Notifier) itemFor(ctx context.Context, snap notify.Snapshot, baseURL string) (notify.Item, error) {
	assets, err := n.pg.NotificationAssetNames(ctx, snap.AssetIDs)
	if err != nil {
		// Failing to resolve asset names must not block delivery: missing names is
		// far less severe than missing the notification — the message just has one
		// fewer asset line.
		log.Printf("[notify] failed to resolve asset names finding=%d: %v", snap.FindingID, err)
	}
	item := notify.Item{
		FindingID:  snap.FindingID,
		Name:       snap.Name,
		VulnClass:  snap.VulnClass,
		Severity:   snap.Severity,
		Summary:    snap.Summary,
		Assets:     assets,
		FromStatus: snap.FromStatus,
		ToStatus:   snap.ToStatus,
	}
	if baseURL != "" {
		// The detail page route is in web/src/app/(main)/function/findings/detail/page.tsx;
		// it reads the finding id from the `id` query parameter.
		item.DetailURL = fmt.Sprintf("%s/function/findings/detail?id=%d", baseURL, snap.FindingID)
	}
	return item, nil
}

// takeTokens takes **at most want** tokens from the channel's token bucket and
// returns the number actually taken.
//
// One token = one message (one HTTP request). In realtime mode the caller passes
// as many as it needs; in digest mode a whole batch of vulnerabilities sends only
// one message, so pass 1.
//
// The bucket capacity is the channel's per-minute limit and refills at a constant
// rate. ratePerMin<=0 means no rate limit, in which case a finite but
// sufficiently large value is returned, to prevent a single tick from being
// dragged down by unlimited backlog.
//
// The `want` cap is necessary: without it the only option would be draining the
// whole bucket, while the caller has its own per-tick cap — the extra tokens are
// both unusable and gone before the next refill. Accumulated burst capacity would
// be forever unreachable, and even "no pending deliveries this round" would still
// be charged.
func (n *Notifier) takeTokens(channelID int64, ratePerMin, want int, now time.Time) int {
	if want <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	if ratePerMin <= 0 {
		return min(want, notifyUnlimitedBurstPerTick)
	}
	n.mu.Lock()
	defer n.mu.Unlock()
	b := n.buckets[channelID]
	if b == nil {
		b = &notifyBucket{tokens: float64(ratePerMin), lastFill: now}
		n.buckets[channelID] = b
	}
	// Refill by real elapsed time at a rate of ratePerMin/60 per second.
	if elapsed := now.Sub(b.lastFill).Seconds(); elapsed > 0 {
		b.tokens = minF(float64(ratePerMin), b.tokens+elapsed*float64(ratePerMin)/60)
		b.lastFill = now
	}
	// Add a tiny epsilon before truncating: the token count is accumulated in
	// floating point, and two half refills can yield 0.5 + 0.5 = 0.9999999999,
	// which a plain int() would truncate to 0 — a mathematically full bucket that
	// yields no token. 1e-9 is far smaller than one token and will not let a real
	// shortfall through.
	take := min(int(b.tokens+1e-9), want)
	if take <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	b.tokens -= float64(take)
	return take
}

// enabled reads the master switch.
func (n *Notifier) enabled() bool {
	return n.pg.GetBool(settingNotifyEnabled, true)
}

// publicBaseURL returns the external address for back-links, with trailing
// slashes removed.
func (n *Notifier) publicBaseURL() string {
	v, ok, err := n.pg.GetSetting(settingNotifyPublicBaseURL)
	if err != nil || !ok {
		return ""
	}
	return trimTrailingSlash(v)
}

// digestInterval returns the digest period, falling back to the default when the
// value is invalid or not configured.
func (n *Notifier) digestInterval() time.Duration {
	v, ok, err := n.pg.GetSetting(settingNotifyDigestMinutes)
	if err != nil || !ok {
		return time.Duration(notifyDefaultDigestMinutes) * time.Minute
	}
	m := 0
	if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(v, "%d", &m); err != nil || m <= 0 {
		return time.Duration(notifyDefaultDigestMinutes) * time.Minute
	}
	return time.Duration(m) * time.Minute
}

// notifyLimits reads the summary/asset render limits from the settings.
func notifyLimits(pg *db.DB) notify.Limits {
	summary, sOK, _ := pg.GetSetting(settingNotifySummaryMaxRunes)
	assets, aOK, _ := pg.GetSetting(settingNotifyAssetsMaxShown)
	return notify.Limits{
		SummaryRunes: notifyLimitValue(summary, sOK, notify.DefaultMaxSummaryRunes, notifySummaryMaxRunesCap),
		AssetsShown:  notifyLimitValue(assets, aOK, notify.DefaultMaxAssetsShown, notifyAssetsMaxShownCap),
	}
}

// notifyLimitValue resolves one stored render limit: def when the key is unset,
// unparseable, or outside [0, max]. 0 is a valid value (no truncation), which is
// why "unset" is carried by ok and not by the number.
func notifyLimitValue(v string, ok bool, def, max int) int {
	if !ok {
		return def
	}
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(v))
	if err != nil || n < 0 || n > max {
		return def
	}
	return n
}

// parseSnapshot parses the snapshot of the event a delivery corresponds to.
func parseSnapshot(dl *db.NotificationDelivery) (notify.Snapshot, error) {
	var snap notify.Snapshot
	if len(dl.Snapshot) == 0 {
		return snap, fmt.Errorf("event snapshot of delivery %d is empty", dl.ID)
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(dl.Snapshot, &snap); err != nil {
		return snap, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse event snapshot of delivery %d: %w", dl.ID, err)
	}
	if snap.Kind == "" {
		// The event kind is authoritative on the event row; the copy in the
		// snapshot may have been written by an older version.
		snap.Kind = dl.EventKind
	}
	return snap, nil
}

func deliveryIDs(deliveries []*db.NotificationDelivery) []int64 {
	out := make([]int64, 0, len(deliveries))
	for _, dl := range deliveries {
		out = append(out, dl.ID)
	}
	return out
}

func trimTrailingSlash(s string) string {
	for len(s) > 0 && s[len(s)-1] == '/' {
		s = s[:len(s)-1]
	}
	return s
}

func minF(a, b float64) float64 {
	if a < b {
		return a
	}
	return b
}

package server

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/notify"
)

// This file is the HTTP API for the notification delivery feature. All routes are
// mounted behind requireAuth (see Handler()), consistent with the other admin APIs.

// notifyChannelDTO is the external representation of a channel.
//
// Config is the **masked** configuration: credential fields are replaced with
// values prefixed by notify.MaskedPrefix. The frontend submitting a masked value
// back unchanged means "this field was not modified", and the server keeps the
// original value in the database accordingly (see notify.MergeConfig).
type notifyChannelDTO struct {
	ID         int64          `json:"id"`
	Name       string         `json:"name"`
	Kind       string         `json:"kind"`
	Enabled    bool           `json:"enabled"`
	Mode       string         `json:"mode"`
	Config     map[string]any `json:"config"`
	Filter     notify.Filter  `json:"filter"`
	RatePerMin int            `json:"rate_per_min"`
	CreatedAt  time.Time      `json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt  time.Time      `json:"updated_at"`
	// SecretKeys tells the frontend which fields are credentials, so it can render
	// password inputs and a "leave empty to keep unchanged" hint. Declared by the
	// channel itself (notify.Channel.SecretKeys); the frontend hardcodes no
	// channel-specific knowledge.
	SecretKeys []string `json:"secret_keys"`
}

// notifyDeliveryDTO is the external representation of a delivery history entry.
type notifyDeliveryDTO struct {
	ID          int64      `json:"id"`
	FindingID   int64      `json:"finding_id,string"`
	EventKind   string     `json:"event_kind"`
	ChannelID   int64      `json:"channel_id"`
	ChannelName string     `json:"channel_name"`
	ChannelKind string     `json:"channel_kind"`
	State       string     `json:"state"`
	Attempts    int        `json:"attempts"`
	LastError   string     `json:"last_error"`
	BatchID     *int64     `json:"batch_id,omitempty"`
	CreatedAt   time.Time  `json:"created_at"`
	SentAt      *time.Time `json:"sent_at,omitempty"`
	NextAttempt time.Time  `json:"next_attempt_at"`
	// Message title digest, so the history list can show what this delivery is
	// about without expanding it.
	Title    string `json:"title"`
	Severity string `json:"severity"`
}

func toNotifyChannelDTO(ch *db.NotificationChannel) notifyChannelDTO {
	var cfg map[string]any
	if len(ch.Config) > 0 {
		_ = json.Unmarshal(ch.Config, &cfg)
	}
	if cfg == nil {
		cfg = map[string]any{}
	}
	secrets := []string{}
	if c, ok := notify.Get(ch.Kind); ok {
		secrets = c.SecretKeys()
	}
	return notifyChannelDTO{
		ID:         ch.ID,
		Name:       ch.Name,
		Kind:       ch.Kind,
		Enabled:    ch.IsEnabled(),
		Mode:       ch.Mode,
		Config:     notify.MaskConfig(ch.Kind, cfg),
		Filter:     notify.ParseFilter(ch.Filter),
		RatePerMin: ch.RatePerMin,
		CreatedAt:  ch.CreatedAt,
		UpdatedAt:  ch.UpdatedAt,
		SecretKeys: secrets,
	}
}

func toNotifyDeliveryDTO(dl *db.NotificationDelivery) notifyDeliveryDTO {
	snap, _ := parseSnapshot(dl)
	dto := notifyDeliveryDTO{
		ID:          dl.ID,
		FindingID:   dl.FindingID,
		EventKind:   dl.EventKind,
		ChannelID:   dl.ChannelID,
		ChannelName: dl.ChannelName,
		ChannelKind: dl.ChannelKind,
		State:       dl.State,
		Attempts:    dl.Attempts,
		LastError:   dl.LastError,
		BatchID:     dl.BatchID,
		CreatedAt:   dl.CreatedAt,
		SentAt:      dl.SentAt,
		NextAttempt: dl.NextAttemptAt,
		Severity:    snap.Severity,
	}
	if snap.Name != "" {
		dto.Title = snap.Name
	} else {
		dto.Title = snap.VulnClass
	}
	return dto
}

// notifyMeta returns the static metadata and global settings the notification
// page needs, all in one request, so the frontend does not have to fire three
// requests just to render a dropdown.
func (s *Server) notifyMeta(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	kinds := make([]map[string]any, 0, len(notify.Kinds()))
	for _, k := range notify.Kinds() {
		ch, _ := notify.Get(k)
		kinds = append(kinds, map[string]any{
			"kind":                 k,
			"default_rate_per_min": ch.DefaultRatePerMin(),
			"secret_keys":          ch.SecretKeys(),
		})
	}
	baseURL, _, _ := pg.GetSetting(settingNotifyPublicBaseURL)
	digest, _, _ := pg.GetSetting(settingNotifyDigestMinutes)
	stats, err := pg.NotificationStatsSnapshot(r.Context())
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{
		"kinds":               kinds,
		"enabled":             pg.GetBool(settingNotifyEnabled, true),
		"public_base_url":     baseURL,
		"digest_interval_min": digest,
		"defaults": map[string]any{
			"digest_interval_min": notifyDefaultDigestMinutes,
		},
		"stats": stats,
	})
}

func (s *Server) notifyListChannels(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	channels, err := pg.ListNotificationChannels(r.Context())
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
		return
	}
	out := make([]notifyChannelDTO, 0, len(channels))
	for _, ch := range channels {
		out = append(out, toNotifyChannelDTO(ch))
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"channels": out})
}

// notifyChannelRequest is the request body for creating/updating a channel.
//
// All business fields are pointers, so that "not sent" can be told apart from
// "sent as zero value": under PATCH semantics, fields that were not sent must
// keep their original values in the database.
type notifyChannelRequest struct {
	Name       *string        `json:"name"`
	Kind       *string        `json:"kind"`
	Enabled    *bool          `json:"enabled"`
	Mode       *string        `json:"mode"`
	Config     map[string]any `json:"config"`
	Filter     *notify.Filter `json:"filter"`
	RatePerMin *int           `json:"rate_per_min"`
}

func (s *Server) notifyCreateChannel(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	var req notifyChannelRequest
	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, "request body is not valid JSON: "+err.Error())
		return
	}
	if req.Kind == nil || !notify.ValidKind(*req.Kind) {
		writeErr(w, 400, fmt.Sprintf("invalid channel type, available: %s", strings.Join(notify.Kinds(), " / ")))
		return
	}
	name := ""
	if req.Name != nil {
		name = strings.TrimSpace(*req.Name)
	}
	if name == "" {
		writeErr(w, 400, "channel name is required")
		return
	}
	channel, _ := notify.Get(*req.Kind)
	if err := channel.Validate(req.Config); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, err.Error())
		return
	}
	ch := &db.NotificationChannel{
		Name:       name,
		Kind:       *req.Kind,
		Enabled:    req.Enabled,
		Mode:       db.NotifyModeRealtime,
		RatePerMin: channel.DefaultRatePerMin(),
	}
	if req.Mode != nil {
		if !db.ValidNotifyMode(*req.Mode) {
			writeErr(w, 400, "invalid delivery mode, available: realtime / digest")
			return
		}
		ch.Mode = *req.Mode
	}
	if req.RatePerMin != nil {
		// Use the explicitly given value as-is — including 0, which means
		// "no rate limit" and is a valid configuration.
		if *req.RatePerMin < 0 {
			writeErr(w, 400, "rate limit must not be negative")
			return
		}
		ch.RatePerMin = *req.RatePerMin
	}
	// Only apply the channel default when the field is absent. The default must be
	// decided here rather than in the db layer: only the request body can
	// distinguish "this field was not sent" from "explicitly sent 0", and the two
	// mean entirely different things (former = use default, latter = no rate
	// limit). If the db layer also treated 0 as unspecified, the no-rate-limit
	// configuration would be unreachable.
	if req.RatePerMin == nil {
		ch.RatePerMin = channel.DefaultRatePerMin()
	}
	if req.Filter != nil {
		// Validate restricted-value filter fields (e.g. min_severity) on write. See
		// notify.Filter.Validate for details: a typo in the threshold would
		// silently disable the filter into delivering everything, so it must be
		// blocked at the entry point.
		if err := req.Filter.Validate(); err != nil {
			writeErr(w, 400, err.Error())
			return
		}
		raw, _ := json.Marshal(req.Filter)
		ch.Filter = raw
	}
	rawCfg, _ := json.Marshal(req.Config)
	ch.Config = rawCfg

	id, err := pg.SaveNotificationChannel(r.Context(), ch)
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"id": id})
}

func (s *Server) notifyUpdateChannel(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	id, ok := pathInt(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		writeErr(w, 400, "invalid channel id")
		return
	}
	current, err := pg.NotificationChannelByID(r.Context(), id)
	if err != nil {
		notifyChannelLookupErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	var req notifyChannelRequest
	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, "request body is not valid JSON: "+err.Error())
		return
	}

	// kind may be changed, but changing the type means the whole set of credential
	// fields is replaced and cannot be merged with the old config.
	kind := current.Kind
	if req.Kind != nil {
		if !notify.ValidKind(*req.Kind) {
			writeErr(w, 400, fmt.Sprintf("invalid channel type, available: %s", strings.Join(notify.Kinds(), " / ")))
			return
		}
		kind = *req.Kind
	}
	channel, _ := notify.Get(kind)

	var stored map[string]any
	if kind == current.Kind {
		if len(current.Config) > 0 {
			_ = json.Unmarshal(current.Config, &stored)
		}
	}
	if stored == nil {
		stored = map[string]any{}
	}
	// Use PrepareConfigUpdate rather than bare MergeConfig: when the target address
	// changes, the operator must re-affirm the credential fields, otherwise
	// "change the address only, keep the credentials" would send the real
	// credentials from the database to the new address.
	merged, err := notify.PrepareConfigUpdate(kind, stored, req.Config)
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, err.Error())
		return
	}
	if err := channel.Validate(merged); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, err.Error())
		return
	}
	rawCfg, _ := json.Marshal(merged)

	ch := &db.NotificationChannel{
		ID:         id,
		Name:       current.Name,
		Kind:       kind,
		Enabled:    current.Enabled,
		Mode:       current.Mode,
		Config:     rawCfg,
		Filter:     current.Filter,
		RatePerMin: current.RatePerMin,
	}
	if req.Name != nil {
		if ch.Name = strings.TrimSpace(*req.Name); ch.Name == "" {
			writeErr(w, 400, "channel name must not be empty")
			return
		}
	}
	if req.Enabled != nil {
		ch.Enabled = req.Enabled
	}
	if req.Mode != nil {
		if !db.ValidNotifyMode(*req.Mode) {
			writeErr(w, 400, "invalid delivery mode, available: realtime / digest")
			return
		}
		ch.Mode = *req.Mode
	}
	if req.RatePerMin != nil {
		if *req.RatePerMin < 0 {
			writeErr(w, 400, "rate limit must not be negative")
			return
		}
		ch.RatePerMin = *req.RatePerMin
	}
	if req.Filter != nil {
		if err := req.Filter.Validate(); err != nil {
			writeErr(w, 400, err.Error())
			return
		}
		raw, _ := json.Marshal(req.Filter)
		ch.Filter = raw
	}

	// Going through SetNotificationChannelEnabled instead of the plain
	// SaveNotificationChannel path ensures that "disabling" also marks pending
	// deliveries as skipped, so re-enabling does not deliver a batch of stale,
	// backlogged messages.
	enabledChanged := ch.Enabled != nil && current.Enabled != nil && *ch.Enabled != *current.Enabled
	if enabledChanged {
		// Persist the config update first (with enabled kept at the old value, so
		// the skip logic is not triggered prematurely), then flip the switch
		// separately. There is no concurrency window between the two steps: this
		// endpoint is the only entry point that modifies these two fields.
		prev := ch.Enabled
		ch.Enabled = current.Enabled
		if _, err := pg.SaveNotificationChannel(r.Context(), ch); err != nil {
			writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
			return
		}
		if err := pg.SetNotificationChannelEnabled(r.Context(), id, *prev); err != nil {
			writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
			return
		}
		writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"id": id})
		return
	}
	if _, err := pg.SaveNotificationChannel(r.Context(), ch); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"id": id})
}

func (s *Server) notifyDeleteChannel(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	id, ok := pathInt(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		writeErr(w, 400, "invalid channel id")
		return
	}
	if err := pg.DeleteNotificationChannel(r.Context(), id); err != nil {
		notifyChannelLookupErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"ok": true})
}

// notifyTestChannel sends one test message with the currently saved
// configuration.
//
// It calls the channel's Send directly, bypassing the delivery queue: the point
// of the test is to tell the user immediately "whether this configuration can
// deliver"; going through the queue would hide the result inside the delivery
// history, forcing the user to dig it up to know whether it worked. This
// endpoint is therefore **synchronous**, with the timeout bounded by the notify
// package's HTTP client (15 seconds).
func (s *Server) notifyTestChannel(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	id, ok := pathInt(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		writeErr(w, 400, "invalid channel id")
		return
	}
	ch, err := pg.NotificationChannelByID(r.Context(), id)
	if err != nil {
		notifyChannelLookupErr(w, err)
		return
	}
	channel, ok := notify.Get(ch.Kind)
	if !ok {
		writeErr(w, 400, fmt.Sprintf("channel type %q is not registered", ch.Kind))
		return
	}
	var cfg map[string]any
	if len(ch.Config) > 0 {
		_ = json.Unmarshal(ch.Config, &cfg)
	}
	if err := channel.Validate(cfg); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, err.Error())
		return
	}
	msg := notifyTestMessage(s.notifierBaseURL(pg))
	limits := notifyLimits(pg)
	msg.Limits = &limits
	start := time.Now()
	// The test message is a single entry, so the delivered count is not needed
	// here (for a single message the channel length limit falls back to
	// truncation; no segmentation is involved).
	if _, err := channel.Send(r.Context(), cfg, msg); err != nil {
		// Return the channel's raw error to the user as-is — it is their only clue
		// when debugging the configuration.
		writeErr(w, 502, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{
		"ok":         true,
		"latency_ms": time.Since(start).Milliseconds(),
	})
}

// notifyTestMessage builds the test message. Its content is deliberately
// recognizable as a test at a glance: recipients should not mistake it for a
// real vulnerability.
func notifyTestMessage(baseURL string) notify.Message {
	return notify.Message{
		Items: []notify.Item{{
			FindingID: 0,
			Name:      "Test message · channel configuration OK",
			VulnClass: "Connectivity test",
			Severity:  "low",
			Summary:   "This is a test message for an HIVE notification channel; receiving it means the channel is configured correctly.",
			Assets:    []string{"hive.example.com"},
			DetailURL: baseURL,
		}},
		HomeURL: baseURL,
	}
}

// notifierBaseURL reads the external address used for back-links.
func (s *Server) notifierBaseURL(pg *db.DB) string {
	v, _, _ := pg.GetSetting(settingNotifyPublicBaseURL)
	return trimTrailingSlash(v)
}

func (s *Server) notifyListDeliveries(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	f := db.NotificationDeliveryFilter{
		State:     r.URL.Query().Get("state"),
		EventKind: r.URL.Query().Get("event_kind"),
	}
	if v := r.URL.Query().Get("channel_id"); v != "" {
		f.ChannelID = int64(atoiDefault(v, 0))
	}
	page := queryInt(r, "page", 1)
	pageSize := queryInt(r, "page_size", 50)
	items, total, err := pg.ListNotificationDeliveries(r.Context(), f, page, pageSize)
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
		return
	}
	out := make([]notifyDeliveryDTO, 0, len(items))
	for _, dl := range items {
		out = append(out, toNotifyDeliveryDTO(dl))
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"deliveries": out, "total": total, "page": page, "page_size": pageSize})
}

func (s *Server) notifyRetryDelivery(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	id, ok := pathInt(r, "id")
	if !ok {
		writeErr(w, 400, "invalid delivery id")
		return
	}
	if err := pg.RetryNotificationDelivery(r.Context(), id); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, err.Error())
		return
	}
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"ok": true})
}

// notifyChannelLookupErr translates "channel does not exist" into 404, all other
// errors into 500.
func notifyChannelLookupErr(w http.ResponseWriter, err error) {
	if errors.Is(err, db.ErrNotificationChannelNotFound) {
		writeErr(w, 404, "notification channel does not exist")
		return
	}
	writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/notify"
)

// This file covers the end-to-end behavior of the notification delivery feature:
// vulnerability persisted → event → fan-out → real HTTP send.
//
// One safety note: these cases do **not** call the global Notifier.step(); they
// only call stepRealtime/stepDigest on channels they created themselves. The
// reason is that step() iterates over all enabled channels in the database — on
// a development database with real DingTalk/WeCom bots configured, a global step
// would push the vulnerabilities produced during the test into those groups for
// real. Per-channel calls strictly confine the blast radius to the fake receivers
// created by the tests.
//
// Cleanup: when a case finishes, the events it produced (with deliveries deleted
// by cascade) and its channels are removed, leaving no backlog for real channels.
//
// Assertion policy: stepRealtime/stepDigest return nothing and log internally, so
// what is asserted here is **observable external behavior** (what the fake
// receiver got, what state the delivery rows landed in), not function return
// values — this is closer to the real call path than stubbing return values.

// notifyFixture is the shared fixture for the cases in this file.
type notifyFixture struct {
	s       *Server
	pg      *db.DB
	request func(method, path, body string) *httptest.ResponseRecorder
	n       *Notifier
	// Self-created task/exploration: cases record vulnerabilities here, isolated
	// from other cases' data.
	taskID int64
	expID  int64
	// Events produced after cleanupMark are deleted during cleanup.
	cleanupMark int64
}

func newNotifyFixture(t *testing.T) *notifyFixture {
	t.Helper()
	// All fake receivers in this file run on 127.0.0.1, while delivery rejects
	// loopback addresses by default (SSRF protection for same-host services and
	// cloud metadata). The tests explicitly open this switch; the
	// "reject by default" guard behavior is covered by ssrf_test.go in the notify
	// package.
	t.Setenv(notify.AllowLocalTargetsEnv, "1")
	s, _, request := trafficEvidenceServer(t)
	pg := s.m.pg

	// Create our own task: the task made by the shared fixture
	// trafficEvidenceServer has no exploration id available, which recording a
	// vulnerability requires.
	task, err := s.m.CreateTask("notification delivery test", "delivery behavior verification", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	taskID, err := strconv.ParseInt(task.ID, 10, 64)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM tasks WHERE id=$1`, taskID) })

	var mark int64
	if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT COALESCE(max(id),0) FROM notification_events`).Scan(&mark); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Make the fixture self-contained: mark all events that existed before the
	// fixture was built as already fanned out in one go.
	//
	// Why this is necessary: FanOutPendingEvents is **global** and expands every
	// unfanned event in the database onto all matching channels. The shared
	// fixture trafficEvidenceServer itself records one vulnerability (exactly the
	// initial finding it returns), and other cases may have leftovers too. Without
	// isolation, these stray events would be fanned out onto this case's channels,
	// making assertions like "there should be N deliveries" intermittently wrong —
	// and the way they fail would depend on case execution order, which is harder
	// to debug than a straight failure.
	if _, err := pg.Exec(`UPDATE notification_events SET fanned_out = true WHERE id <= $1 AND NOT fanned_out`, mark); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	f := &notifyFixture{s: s, pg: pg, request: request, n: newNotifier(s), taskID: taskID, expID: task.ExpID, cleanupMark: mark}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		if _, err := pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM notification_events WHERE id > $1`, f.cleanupMark); err != nil {
			t.Logf("failed to clean up notification events: %v", err)
		}
	})
	// The master switch must be on (other cases may have turned it off).
	if err := pg.SetBool(settingNotifyEnabled, true); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return f
}

// record persists one vulnerability via the real evidence write path and returns
// the finding id. That path registers the notification event in the **same
// transaction** — which is exactly the hook point of this feature.
func (f *notifyFixture) record(t *testing.T, vulnclass, severity string) int64 {
	t.Helper()
	out, err := f.s.evidenceStore().Record(context.Background(), db.RecordFindingInput{
		TaskID:        f.taskID,
		ExplorationID: f.expID,
		Worker:        "test",
		VulnClass:     vulnclass,
		Name:          vulnclass,
		Severity:      severity,
		Summary:       vulnclass + " summary",
		Evidence:      "poc",
	}, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to record finding: %v", err)
	}
	return out.FindingID
}

// channel reads back the channel configuration (for per-channel stepX calls).
func (f *notifyFixture) channel(t *testing.T, id int64) *db.NotificationChannel {
	t.Helper()
	ch, err := f.pg.NotificationChannelByID(context.Background(), id)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to read channel: %v", err)
	}
	return ch
}

// deliver fans out events and runs one delivery round for the specified channel
// only.
func (f *notifyFixture) deliver(t *testing.T, chID int64, baseURL string) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, _, err := f.pg.FanOutPendingEvents(ctx, 500); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("fan-out failed: %v", err)
	}
	f.n.stepRealtime(ctx, f.channel(t, chID), 50, baseURL)
}

// createChannel creates a channel through the HTTP API, also covering the API's
// own validation paths along the way.
func (f *notifyFixture) createChannel(t *testing.T, payload map[string]any) int64 {
	t.Helper()
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(payload)
	r := f.request("POST", "/api/notify/channels", string(raw))
	if r.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("failed to create channel %d: %s", r.Code, r.Body)
	}
	var res struct {
		ID int64 `json:"id"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(r.Body.Bytes(), &res); err != nil || res.ID == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("create channel returned an abnormal response: %s (%v)", r.Body, err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { f.pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM notification_channels WHERE id=$1`, res.ID) })
	return res.ID
}

// fakeWebhook is a fake receiver that records the request bodies it gets.
type fakeWebhook struct {
	*httptest.Server
	mu     sync.Mutex
	bodies []map[string]any
}

func newFakeWebhook(t *testing.T) *fakeWebhook {
	t.Helper()
	f := &fakeWebhook{}
	f.Server = httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		raw, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
		var body map[string]any
		_ = json.Unmarshal(raw, &body)
		f.mu.Lock()
		f.bodies = append(f.bodies, body)
		f.mu.Unlock()
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"errcode":0,"errmsg":"ok"}`)
	}))
	t.Cleanup(f.Close)
	return f
}

func (f *fakeWebhook) count() int {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	return len(f.bodies)
}

func (f *fakeWebhook) body(t *testing.T, i int) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	if i >= len(f.bodies) {
		t.Fatalf("fake receiver only got %d requests, cannot get request %d", len(f.bodies), i)
	}
	return f.bodies[i]
}

func (f *fakeWebhook) last(t *testing.T) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	if f.count() == 0 {
		t.Fatal("fake receiver received no requests")
	}
	return f.body(t, f.count()-1)
}

// markdownText extracts the body text from the request body, tolerating the
// field-name differences between vendors: DingTalk markdown uses `text`,
// ActionCard uses `text`, WeCom markdown uses `content`.
func markdownText(t *testing.T, body map[string]any) string {
	t.Helper()
	for _, key := range []string{"markdown", "actionCard"} {
		section, ok := body[key].(map[string]any)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		for _, field := range []string{"text", "content"} {
			if s, ok := section[field].(string); ok && s != "" {
				return s
			}
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("no recognizable body text in request body: %v", body)
	return ""
}

// agePendingBatch ages the channel's pending deliveries, used to test digest
// batches becoming due.
func (f *notifyFixture) agePendingBatch(t *testing.T, chID int64) {
	t.Helper()
	if _, err := f.pg.Exec(`UPDATE notification_deliveries SET created_at = now() - interval '2 hours'
WHERE channel_id=$1 AND state=$2`, chID, db.NotifyStatePending); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func TestNotifyEndToEndRealtimeDelivery(t *testing.T) {
	f := newNotifyFixture(t)
	hook := newFakeWebhook(t)
	chID := f.createChannel(t, map[string]any{
		"name":   "realtime delivery",
		"kind":   notify.KindDingTalk,
		"config": map[string]any{"webhook": hook.URL},
	})
	f.record(t, "SQL injection", "high")
	f.deliver(t, chID, "")

	if hook.count() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 1 message sent, got %d", hook.count())
	}
	text := markdownText(t, hook.last(t))
	for _, want := range []string{"SQL injection", "High", "Summary"} {
		if !strings.Contains(text, want) {
			t.Fatalf("message body is missing %q:\n%s", want, text)
		}
	}
	// The delivery should transition to sent.
	var pending int
	if err := f.pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM notification_deliveries WHERE channel_id=$1 AND state <> $2`,
		chID, db.NotifyStateSent).Scan(&pending); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if pending != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%d deliveries still not marked sent after delivery", pending)
	}
}

func TestNotifyChannelAPIMasksSecretsAndPreservesOnUpdate(t *testing.T) {
	f := newNotifyFixture(t)
	chID := f.createChannel(t, map[string]any{
		"name":   "masking case",
		"kind":   notify.KindDingTalk,
		"config": map[string]any{"webhook": "https://oapi.dingtalk.com/robot/send?access_token=abc123456", "secret": "SECabcdef123456"},
	})

	r := f.request("GET", "/api/notify/channels", "")
	if r.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("failed to list channels %d: %s", r.Code, r.Body)
	}
	if strings.Contains(r.Body.String(), "abc123456") || strings.Contains(r.Body.String(), "SECabcdef123456") {
		t.Fatalf("API response leaked credentials: %s", r.Body)
	}
	var listed struct {
		Channels []struct {
			ID         int64          `json:"id"`
			Config     map[string]any `json:"config"`
			SecretKeys []string       `json:"secret_keys"`
		} `json:"channels"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(r.Body.Bytes(), &listed); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var mine *struct {
		ID         int64          `json:"id"`
		Config     map[string]any `json:"config"`
		SecretKeys []string       `json:"secret_keys"`
	}
	for i := range listed.Channels {
		if listed.Channels[i].ID == chID {
			mine = &listed.Channels[i]
		}
	}
	if mine == nil {
		t.Fatal("newly created channel did not appear in the list")
	}
	if !notify.IsMasked(fmt.Sprint(mine.Config["webhook"])) || !notify.IsMasked(fmt.Sprint(mine.Config["secret"])) {
		t.Fatalf("credential fields should be masked values: %v", mine.Config)
	}
	if len(mine.SecretKeys) == 0 {
		t.Fatal("the API should tell the frontend which fields are credentials")
	}

	// PATCH with only a rename + echoing back the masked credentials: the real
	// credentials must be preserved unchanged.
	body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
		"name":   "renamed",
		"config": map[string]any{"webhook": fmt.Sprint(mine.Config["webhook"]), "secret": fmt.Sprint(mine.Config["secret"])},
	})
	if r := f.request("PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/notify/channels/%d", chID), string(body)); r.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("update failed %d: %s", r.Code, r.Body)
	}
	cfg := f.channelConfig(t, chID)
	if cfg["webhook"] != "https://oapi.dingtalk.com/robot/send?access_token=abc123456" {
		t.Fatalf("masked echo overwrote the real credential: %v", cfg["webhook"])
	}
	if cfg["secret"] != "SECabcdef123456" {
		t.Fatalf("masked echo overwrote the secret: %v", cfg["secret"])
	}
	if f.channel(t, chID).Name != "renamed" {
		t.Fatal("name was not updated")
	}

	// Explicitly clearing the secret should take effect (as opposed to
	// "echoing back the mask = keep unchanged").
	body, _ = json.Marshal(map[string]any{"config": map[string]any{"secret": ""}})
	if r := f.request("PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/notify/channels/%d", chID), string(body)); r.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("clearing secret failed %d: %s", r.Code, r.Body)
	}
	if _, still := f.channelConfig(t, chID)["secret"]; still {
		t.Fatal("empty string should clear the secret")
	}
}

func (f *notifyFixture) channelConfig(t *testing.T, id int64) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	var cfg map[string]any
	if err := json.Unmarshal(f.channel(t, id).Config, &cfg); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return cfg
}

func TestNotifyChannelAPICreateValidation(t *testing.T) {
	f := newNotifyFixture(t)
	cases := []struct {
		name    string
		payload map[string]any
		wantSub string
	}{
		{"invalid kind", map[string]any{"name": "x", "kind": "nope", "config": map[string]any{}}, "invalid channel type"},
		{"missing name", map[string]any{"kind": notify.KindDingTalk, "config": map[string]any{"webhook": "https://e.com/h"}}, "channel name is required"},
		{"missing webhook", map[string]any{"name": "x", "kind": notify.KindDingTalk, "config": map[string]any{}}, "Webhook"},
		{"invalid webhook scheme", map[string]any{"name": "x", "kind": notify.KindDingTalk, "config": map[string]any{"webhook": "file:///etc/passwd"}}, "invalid Webhook address"},
		{"invalid mode", map[string]any{"name": "x", "kind": notify.KindDingTalk, "mode": "sometimes", "config": map[string]any{"webhook": "https://e.com/h"}}, "invalid delivery mode"},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			raw, _ := json.Marshal(tc.payload)
			r := f.request("POST", "/api/notify/channels", string(raw))
			if r.Code != 400 {
				t.Fatalf("expected 400, got %d: %s", r.Code, r.Body)
			}
			if !strings.Contains(r.Body.String(), tc.wantSub) {
				t.Fatalf("error message should mention %q, got %s", tc.wantSub, r.Body)
			}
		})
	}
	if r := f.request("DELETE", "/api/notify/channels/99999999", ""); r.Code != 404 {
		t.Fatalf("deleting a nonexistent channel should return 404, got %d", r.Code)
	}
}

func TestNotifyFilterBlocksBelowThreshold(t *testing.T) {
	f := newNotifyFixture(t)
	hook := newFakeWebhook(t)
	chID := f.createChannel(t, map[string]any{
		"name":   "critical only",
		"kind":   notify.KindDingTalk,
		"config": map[string]any{"webhook": hook.URL},
		"filter": map[string]any{"min_severity": "critical"},
	})
	f.record(t, "low-risk issue", "low")
	if _, _, err := f.pg.FanOutPendingEvents(context.Background(), 500); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var n int
	if err := f.pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM notification_deliveries WHERE channel_id=$1`, chID).Scan(&n); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("vulnerabilities below the threshold should not produce deliveries, got %d", n)
	}
	f.n.stepRealtime(context.Background(), f.channel(t, chID), 50, "")
	if hook.count() != 0 {
		t.Fatal("filtered vulnerabilities should not send messages")
	}
}

func TestNotifyDigestBatchesMultipleFindingsIntoOneMessage(t *testing.T) {
	f := newNotifyFixture(t)
	hook := newFakeWebhook(t)
	chID := f.createChannel(t, map[string]any{
		"name":   "digest delivery",
		"kind":   notify.KindDingTalk,
		"mode":   db.NotifyModeDigest,
		"config": map[string]any{"webhook": hook.URL},
	})
	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
		f.record(t, fmt.Sprintf("digest vuln %d", i+1), "high")
	}
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, _, err := f.pg.FanOutPendingEvents(ctx, 500); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ch := f.channel(t, chID)

	// Not due yet: do not send.
	f.n.stepDigest(ctx, ch, 50, "")
	if hook.count() != 0 {
		t.Fatal("digest batch sent before it was due")
	}

	// After aging the batch: three findings merge into one message.
	f.agePendingBatch(t, chID)
	f.n.stepDigest(ctx, ch, 50, "")
	if got := hook.count(); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("three findings should be digested into one message, actually sent %d", got)
	}
	text := markdownText(t, hook.last(t))
	if !strings.Contains(text, "in the last 30 minutes") || !strings.Contains(text, "3 new vulnerabilities") {
		t.Fatalf("digest message is missing the count/time-window wording:\n%s", text)
	}
	for i := 1; i <= 3; i++ {
		if !strings.Contains(text, fmt.Sprintf("digest vuln %d", i)) {
			t.Fatalf("digest message is missing entry %d:\n%s", i, text)
		}
	}
	// The same batch should share one batch_id.
	var distinct, total int
	if err := f.pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(DISTINCT batch_id), count(*) FROM notification_deliveries WHERE channel_id=$1`, chID).Scan(&distinct, &total); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if total != 3 || distinct != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("three deliveries should share one batch_id, got distinct=%d total=%d", distinct, total)
	}
}

func TestNotifyStatusChangeDelivery(t *testing.T) {
	f := newNotifyFixture(t)
	hook := newFakeWebhook(t)
	chID := f.createChannel(t, map[string]any{
		"name":   "status change subscription",
		"kind":   notify.KindDingTalk,
		"config": map[string]any{"webhook": hook.URL},
		"filter": map[string]any{"on_status_change": true},
	})
	finding := f.record(t, "status change case", "high")
	r := f.request("PATCH", fmt.Sprintf("/api/exploration/findings/%d", finding), `{"status":"fixed"}`)
	if r.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("failed to change status %d: %s", r.Code, r.Body)
	}
	f.deliver(t, chID, "")

	// There should be two messages: the "fixed" one is the status change; the
	// finding_created one may also go out in the same round. The status-change one
	// is actually created later, but do not rely on ordering — search them all.
	found := false
	for i := 0; i < hook.count(); i++ {
		text := markdownText(t, hook.body(t, i))
		if strings.Contains(text, "Status change") && strings.Contains(text, "Fixed") {
			found = true
		}
	}
	if !found {
		t.Fatalf("no message containing \"Status change → Fixed\" received (%d messages total)", hook.count())
	}
}

	}
}

func TestNotifyDeliveriesHistoryAndRetry(t *testing.T) {
	f := newNotifyFixture(t)
	// Point at an address that always fails, to produce failed deliveries.
	chID := f.createChannel(t, map[string]any{
		"name":   "failing retry",
		"kind":   notify.KindDingTalk,
		"config": map[string]any{"webhook": "http://127.0.0.1:1/hook"},
	})
	f.record(t, "delivery that fails", "high")
	ctx := context.Background()
	if _, _, err := f.pg.FanOutPendingEvents(ctx, 500); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ch := f.channel(t, chID)
	// Keep delivering until the retry budget is exhausted.
	for i := 0; i < db.MaxNotifyAttempts; i++ {
		f.n.stepRealtime(ctx, ch, 50, "")
		if _, err := f.pg.Exec(`UPDATE notification_deliveries SET next_attempt_at = now() - interval '1 minute' WHERE channel_id=$1`, chID); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	var state string
	if err := f.pg.QueryRow(`SELECT state FROM notification_deliveries WHERE channel_id=$1`, chID).Scan(&state); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if state != db.NotifyStateFailed {
		t.Fatalf("should be failed after retries are exhausted, got %s", state)
	}

	r := f.request("GET", fmt.Sprintf("/api/notify/deliveries?channel_id=%d&state=failed", chID), "")
	if r.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("failed to query history %d: %s", r.Code, r.Body)
	}
	var hist struct {
		Deliveries []struct {
			ID        int64  `json:"id"`
			State     string `json:"state"`
			LastError string `json:"last_error"`
			Attempts  int    `json:"attempts"`
			Title     string `json:"title"`
		} `json:"deliveries"`
		Total int `json:"total"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(r.Body.Bytes(), &hist); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if hist.Total != 1 || len(hist.Deliveries) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("should find 1 failed delivery, got total=%d len=%d", hist.Total, len(hist.Deliveries))
	}
	if hist.Deliveries[0].LastError == "" {
		t.Fatal("the history should carry the failure reason, otherwise users cannot troubleshoot")
	}
	if hist.Deliveries[0].Attempts < db.MaxNotifyAttempts {
		t.Fatalf("the attempt count should be recorded, got %d", hist.Deliveries[0].Attempts)
	}
	if hist.Deliveries[0].Title != "delivery that fails" {
		t.Fatalf("the history should include the vulnerability title, got %q", hist.Deliveries[0].Title)
	}

	// Manual resend: it should go back to pending with the counter reset.
	if r := f.request("POST", fmt.Sprintf("/api/notify/deliveries/%d/retry", hist.Deliveries[0].ID), ""); r.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("resend failed %d: %s", r.Code, r.Body)
	}
	var attempts int
	if err := f.pg.QueryRow(`SELECT state, attempts FROM notification_deliveries WHERE id=$1`, hist.Deliveries[0].ID).Scan(&state, &attempts); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if state != db.NotifyStatePending || attempts != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("after resend it should be pending with attempts=0, got %s/%d", state, attempts)
	}
}

func TestNotifyMetaAndSettingsRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	f := newNotifyFixture(t)
	r := f.request("GET", "/api/notify/meta", "")
	if r.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("meta failed: %s", r.Body)
	}
	var meta struct {
		Kinds []struct {
			Kind       string   `json:"kind"`
			SecretKeys []string `json:"secret_keys"`
		} `json:"kinds"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(r.Body.Bytes(), &meta); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(meta.Kinds) != len(notify.Kinds()) {
		t.Fatalf("meta should list all %d channels, got %d", len(notify.Kinds()), len(meta.Kinds))
	}
	for _, k := range meta.Kinds {
		if len(k.SecretKeys) == 0 {
			t.Errorf("channel %s did not report credential fields", k.Kind)
		}
	}

	// Round trip of the three global settings. The trailing slash should be
	// normalized away, otherwise back-links would be built as "//function/...".
	if r := f.request("PUT", "/api/settings", `{"notify_public_base_url":"https://hive.example.com/","notify_digest_interval_min":15,"notify_enabled":true}`); r.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("failed to write settings %d: %s", r.Code, r.Body)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		f.pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM settings WHERE key IN ($1,$2)`, settingNotifyPublicBaseURL, settingNotifyDigestMinutes)
	})
	payload := f.s.settingsPayload()
	if payload["notify_public_base_url"] != "https://hive.example.com" {
		t.Fatalf("back-link address was not normalized: %v", payload["notify_public_base_url"])
	}
	if payload["notify_digest_interval_min"] != 15 {
		t.Fatalf("digest interval did not take effect: %v", payload["notify_digest_interval_min"])
	}

	// Invalid values should be rejected.
	for _, body := range []string{
		`{"notify_public_base_url":"ftp://x"}`,
		`{"notify_digest_interval_min":0}`,
		`{"notify_digest_interval_min":99999}`,
	} {
		if r := f.request("PUT", "/api/settings", body); r.Code != 400 {
			t.Errorf("%s should return 400, got %d", body, r.Code)
		}
	}
}

// TestNotifyLimitSettingsRoundTrip covers the two render-limit keys through the
// settings API and the settings table: unset reads as the 120 / 3 defaults, a
// stored 0 reads back as 0 (no truncation) and not as the default, and
// out-of-range values are rejected without touching the stored value.
func TestNotifyLimitSettingsRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	f := newNotifyFixture(t)
	clear := func() {
		f.pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM settings WHERE key IN ($1,$2)`, settingNotifySummaryMaxRunes, settingNotifyAssetsMaxShown)
	}
	clear()
	t.Cleanup(clear)
	expect := func(step string, summary, assets int) {
		t.Helper()
		payload := f.s.settingsPayload()
		if payload["notify_summary_max_runes"] != summary || payload["notify_assets_max_shown"] != assets {
			t.Fatalf("%s: settings payload should report %d / %d, got %v / %v", step, summary, assets,
				payload["notify_summary_max_runes"], payload["notify_assets_max_shown"])
		}
		if got := notifyLimits(f.pg); got != (notify.Limits{SummaryRunes: summary, AssetsShown: assets}) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: the delivery engine should read %d / %d, got %+v", step, summary, assets, got)
		}
	}
	expect("unset", notify.DefaultMaxSummaryRunes, notify.DefaultMaxAssetsShown)

	for _, tc := range []struct{ summary, assets int }{{500, 10}, {0, 0}, {4000, 50}} {
		body := fmt.Sprintf(`{"notify_summary_max_runes":%d,"notify_assets_max_shown":%d}`, tc.summary, tc.assets)
		if r := f.request("PUT", "/api/settings", body); r.Code != 200 {
			t.Fatalf("%s failed %d: %s", body, r.Code, r.Body)
		}
		expect(body, tc.summary, tc.assets)
		for key, want := range map[string]int{settingNotifySummaryMaxRunes: tc.summary, settingNotifyAssetsMaxShown: tc.assets} {
			if v, ok, err := f.pg.GetSetting(key); err != nil || !ok || v != strconv.Itoa(want) {
				t.Fatalf("%s: settings row %s should hold %d, got %q (ok=%v err=%v)", body, key, want, v, ok, err)
			}
		}
	}

	for _, body := range []string{
		`{"notify_summary_max_runes":-1}`,
		`{"notify_summary_max_runes":4001}`,
		`{"notify_assets_max_shown":-1}`,
		`{"notify_assets_max_shown":51}`,
	} {
		if r := f.request("PUT", "/api/settings", body); r.Code != 400 {
			t.Errorf("%s should return 400, got %d", body, r.Code)
		}
	}
	expect("after rejected writes", 4000, 50)
}

// TestNotifySummaryLimitReachesDelivery is the end-to-end evidence that the
// stored limit reaches the message actually sent: with the key unset the summary
// is cut at 120 characters as before, and once it is set to 0 the same summary
// goes out whole.
func TestNotifySummaryLimitReachesDelivery(t *testing.T) {
	f := newNotifyFixture(t)
	clear := func() { f.pg.Exec(`DELETE FROM settings WHERE key=$1`, settingNotifySummaryMaxRunes) }
	clear()
	t.Cleanup(clear)
	hook := newFakeWebhook(t)
	chID := f.createChannel(t, map[string]any{
		"name":   "summary limit",
		"kind":   notify.KindDingTalk,
		"config": map[string]any{"webhook": hook.URL},
	})
	summary := strings.Repeat("Z", 300)
	record := func(name string) {
		t.Helper()
		if _, err := f.s.evidenceStore().Record(context.Background(), db.RecordFindingInput{
			TaskID:        f.taskID,
			ExplorationID: f.expID,
			Worker:        "test",
			VulnClass:     name,
			Name:          name,
			Severity:      "high",
			Summary:       summary,
			Evidence:      "poc",
		}, nil); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("failed to record finding: %v", err)
		}
	}

	record("summary limit unset")
	f.deliver(t, chID, "")
	text := markdownText(t, hook.last(t))
	if !strings.Contains(text, strings.Repeat("Z", 119)+"…") || strings.Contains(text, strings.Repeat("Z", 120)) {
		t.Fatalf("with the key unset the summary should be cut at 120 characters:\n%s", text)
	}

	if r := f.request("PUT", "/api/settings", `{"notify_summary_max_runes":0}`); r.Code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("failed to write settings %d: %s", r.Code, r.Body)
	}
	record("summary limit zero")
	f.deliver(t, chID, "")
	if hook.count() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 2 messages sent, got %d", hook.count())
	}
	if text := markdownText(t, hook.last(t)); !strings.Contains(text, summary) {
		t.Fatalf("with the limit at 0 the whole summary should be sent:\n%s", text)
	}
}
